Your server and your Flutter app are both written in Dart. So they can use the same code. This guide puts a @Dto class in a shared package. The server checks requests with it. The Flutter app checks the form with it, with the same rules and the same error messages, before it sends the request.

This works, and it was tested

The generated DTO code imports only dox_validation. It does not need dox_core. dox_validation is pure Dart: it imports only dart:async. No dart:io, no dart:mirrors. Tested on 2026-10-22 with Dart 3.13.6 and Dox 3.0.0-alpha.4. See What was tested.

docs.title: The layout
docs.text:
my_blog/
  packages/
    blog_shared/     # the DTOs. Pure Dart.
  server/            # the Dox app
  app/               # the Flutter app

flowchart LR
    S[packages/blog_shared<br>SaveBlog + SaveBlog.schema] --> A[app: Flutter<br>checks the form]
    S --> B[server: Dox<br>checks the request]
    A -- "POST /api/blogs (JSON)" --> B

docs.title: 1. The shared package
2. The Dox server
docs.text:
Add the shared package to the server:

server/pubspec.yaml
name: server
publish_to: none

environment:
  sdk: ^3.13.0

dependencies:
  dox_core: ^3.0.0-alpha.4
  blog_shared:
    path: ../packages/blog_shared

dev_dependencies:
  build_runner: ^2.17.1
  dox_builder: ^3.0.0-alpha.4

Dox finds a DTO in the dtos list of AppConfig. The server's own lib/dtos.g.dart lists only the DTOs in the server. So add the list of the shared package too:

server/lib/config/app.dart
import 'package:blog_shared/dtos.g.dart' as shared;
import 'package:dox_core/dox_core.dart';
import 'package:server/dtos.g.dart';

AppConfig appConfig = AppConfig(
  // ...
  dtos: <DtoSchema<Object>>[...dtos, ...shared.dtos],
);

When the server has no DTOs of its own, there is no server/lib/dtos.g.dart. Then use dtos: shared.dtos.

The controller asks for SaveBlog like any other DTO. Dox checks the body before the method runs. Bad input gets 422.

server/lib/app/http/controllers/blog.controller.dart
import 'package:blog_shared/blog_shared.dart' show SaveBlog;

class BlogController {
  Future<Map<String, dynamic>> store(SaveBlog body) async {
    // body.title is already trimmed and checked.
    return <String, dynamic>{'title': body.title, 'saved': true};
  }
}
server/lib/routes/api.dart
Route.post('/blogs', BlogController().store);

Why show SaveBlog

dox_core has its own ValidationException (it answers 422). blog_shared exports the one from dox_validation. show keeps only the DTO from blog_shared, so the two names do not clash in server code.

A bad request gets the errors as {"key": "message"}:

POST /api/blogs  {"title": "ab", "description": "short"}
422 {"title":"The title must be between 3 and 255 characters","description":"The description must be at least 10 characters"}

docs.title: 3. The Flutter app
What was tested
docs.text:
Three packages were made in a temp folder, with path dependencies to the Dox packages:

  1. blog_shared with the SaveBlog DTO above. dart run build_runner build wrote save_blog.g.dart and dtos.g.dart. Both import only package:dox_validation. dart analyze found no issues.

  2. A plain Dart console app that depends on blog_shared only. Its dependency tree has dox_validation and nothing else from Dox. dart run gave this output:

    bad input ok? false
errors: {title: The title must be between 3 and 255 characters, description: The description must be at least 10 characters}
good input ok? true
title after trim: "Hello Dox"
json to send: {title: Hello Dox, description: A post about sharing code with Flutter.}
parse threw: ValidationException

    The same app compiled with dart compile js and run in Node gave the same output. So the code also runs on the web. 3. A Dox server with dox_core and blog_shared, dtos: shared.dtos, and Route.post('/blogs', BlogController().store). A bad body got 422 with the errors shown above. A good body got 200 {"title":"Hello Dox","saved":true} (the title was trimmed).

Not tested here: the Flutter widget itself.

docs.title: Static files and SPA
docs.text: Serve a folder of files, or a single page app (React, Vue, Flutter web), from the Dox app, with the right cache headers.

docs.title: What you need
docs.text:
• A Dox app.
  • A public folder with the built front-end (index.html, assets/...).

docs.title: Serve a folder: one line
docs.text:
Route.files serves every file of a storage disk. Make a disk for the folder, and add the route.

lib/config/storage.dart
StorageConfig storage = StorageConfig(
  defaultDisk: 'local',
  disks: <String, Map<String, dynamic>>{
    'local': <String, dynamic>{'driver': 'local', 'root': 'storage'},

    /// the front-end files
    'public': <String, dynamic>{'driver': 'local', 'root': 'public'},
  },
);
lib/routes/web.dart
Route.files('static', disk: 'public', signed: false); // GET /static/{key*}

GET /static/app.js sends public/app.js, streamed, with the right Content-Type. A missing file answers 404. The disk rejects .. in the path, so a client can not read files outside public.

This is enough for a few files. It sends no Cache-Control header. For an SPA, go on.

docs.title: Serve an SPA
docs.text:
An SPA needs two things:

  • index.html for every URL the SPA router handles, with no cache.
  • The built assets with a long cache. Build tools put a hash in the file name (app.3f9c2b.js), so a new build has new names.

docs.title: 1. Write the controller
2. Add the routes
docs.text:
The catch-all route must come last. Put the API router before the web router in AppConfig.

lib/routes/web.dart
import 'package:dox_core/dox_core.dart';
import 'package:my_app/app/http/controllers/static.controller.dart';

class WebRouter extends Router {
  @override
  List<dynamic> get middleware => <dynamic>[];

  @override
  void register() {
    // the SPA: assets with a long cache, every other URL gets index.html
    Route.get('/assets/{path*}', staticController.asset);
    Route.get('/', staticController.index);
    Route.get('/{path*}', staticController.index);
  }
}
lib/config/app.dart
AppConfig appConfig = AppConfig(
  /// the SPA catch-all route is in WebRouter, so it comes last
  routers: <Router>[ApiRouter(), WebRouter()],
  // ...
);

Keep the route for / as well, so the start page is always served.

docs.title: 3. Put the build in public
docs.text:
# React (Vite)
npm run build && cp -r dist/. public/

# Flutter web
flutter build web && cp -r build/web/. public/

Vite puts the files in assets/. Flutter web puts them next to index.html. For Flutter, change the asset route to match, or serve everything with Route.files and give index.html the catch-all.

docs.title: Check it
docs.text:
curl -i http://localhost:3000/

HTTP/1.1 200 OK
cache-control: max-age=0
content-type: text/html

curl -i http://localhost:3000/settings/profile   # same answer: index.html
curl -i http://localhost:3000/assets/app.js

HTTP/1.1 200 OK
cache-control: max-age=31536000
content-type: text/javascript

GET /assets/nope.js answers 404. GET /assets/..%2Fpubspec.yaml answers 404 too. GET /api/nothing answers 404, not the page.

docs.title: In production
docs.text: Put the proxy in front of Dox, and let it do gzip. See Deployment. For a big site, serve public from the proxy or a CDN, and keep Dox for the API only.

docs.title: See also
docs.text:
• Routing: serve storage files
  • Response: files and big responses
  • File storage

docs.title: Testing with a database
docs.text: Run model tests against a real database: SQLite for fast local tests, or a test Postgres for the real thing. Migrations run once, and every test starts with an empty table.

docs.title: What you need
docs.text:
• A Dox app with Dart migrations in db/migration (see Migration).
  • test as a dev dependency: dart pub add dev:test.

docs.title: 1. Write the migration
docs.text:
If you do not have one yet:

dox make:migration create_users_table
db/migration/2026_10_22_000000_create_users_table.dart
import 'package:dox_migration/dox_migration.dart';

class CreateUsersTable extends Migration {
  @override
  Future<void> up(Schema schema) async {
    await schema.create('users', (Table table) {
      table.id();
      table.string('name');
      table.string('email').unique();
      table.string('password');
      table.timestamps();
      table.softDeletes();
    });
  }

  @override
  Future<void> down(Schema schema) async {
    await schema.dropIfExists('users');
  }
}

The command also writes db/migration/migrations.dart, the list of all migrations. The test imports that list. A Dart migration works on Postgres, MySQL and SQLite, so the same test runs on all of them.

docs.title: 2. Write the test (SQLite)
docs.text:
SQLite needs no server. The test makes its own config, so your .env does not matter.

test/user_test.dart
import 'dart:io';

import 'package:dox_core/dox_core.dart';
import 'package:dox_migration/dox_migration.dart';
import 'package:dox_orm/dox_orm.dart';
import 'package:my_app/app/models/user/user.model.dart';
import 'package:test/test.dart';

import '../db/migration/migrations.dart';

/// One SQLite file for this test file. No server, no Postgres.
const String dbFile = 'storage/test.sqlite';

DatabaseConfig testDatabase = DatabaseConfig(
  connection: 'sqlite',
  connections: <String, ConnectionConfig>{
    'sqlite': ConnectionConfig(
      driver: Driver.sqlite,
      database: dbFile,
      debug: false,
    ),
  },
);

Future<void> deleteDbFile() async {
  for (String suffix in <String>['', '-wal', '-shm']) {
    File file = File('$dbFile$suffix');
    if (await file.exists()) await file.delete();
  }
}

void main() {
  setUpAll(() async {
    await deleteDbFile();
    await Migrator(
      migrations: migrations,
      connection: await testDatabase
          .getConnectionConfig()
          .getDatabaseConnection(),
    ).migrate();
    SqlQueryBuilder.initializeWithDatabaseConfig(testDatabase);
  });

  // every test starts with an empty table
  setUp(() async {
    await User().truncate();
  });

  tearDownAll(() async {
    await deleteDbFile();
  });

  test('saves and finds a user', () async {
    User user = User()
      ..name = 'Ann'
      ..email = 'ann@example.com'
      ..password = Hash.make('secret123');
    await user.save();

    User? found = await User().where('email', 'ann@example.com').getFirst();
    expect(found?.id, user.id);
    expect(found?.name, 'Ann');
    expect(Hash.verify('secret123', found!.password!), isTrue);
  });

  test('the table is empty again', () async {
    expect(await User().count(), 0);
  });
}

What happens:

  1. setUpAll deletes an old database file, runs the migrations, and starts the ORM on the same file.
  2. setUp empties the table before each test. truncate() also resets the id counter.
  3. tearDownAll deletes the file.

A file, not :memory:

The migrator and the ORM each open their own connection. Two connections to :memory: are two different databases. A file is shared. Put storage/test.sqlite in .gitignore.

docs.title: 3. Run it
docs.text: dart test test/user_test.dart

docs.title: Check it
docs.text:
00:00 +0: (setUpAll)
Migrating: 2026_10_22_000000_create_users_table
Migrated: 2026_10_22_000000_create_users_table
00:00 +1: saves and finds a user
00:00 +2: the table is empty again
00:00 +2: All tests passed!

docs.title: The same test on Postgres
docs.text:
Use a separate database for tests. Never the one you develop on.

Start one with Docker:

docker run -d --name my_app_test -p 5433:5432 \
  -e POSTGRES_PASSWORD=postgres -e POSTGRES_DB=my_app_test postgres:18

Change the config at the top of the test:

DatabaseConfig testDatabase = DatabaseConfig(
  connection: 'postgres',
  connections: <String, ConnectionConfig>{
    'postgres': ConnectionConfig(
      driver: Driver.postgres,
      host: 'localhost',
      port: 5433,
      user: 'postgres',
      password: 'postgres',
      database: 'my_app_test',
      debug: false,
    ),
  },
);

Delete deleteDbFile() and its two calls. The rest is the same. Or read the values from the env, and run DB_PORT=5433 DB_NAME=my_app_test dart test.

docs.title: Many test files
docs.text:
Each test file runs in its own process. Two files that use the same table at the same time break each other. Either give each file its own SQLite file (storage/test_users.sqlite, storage/test_posts.sqlite), or run them one by one:

dart test --concurrency=1

docs.title: Test a route with the database
docs.text:
Start the server in setUpAll and send real requests. The server runs the services, so the ORM is set up by ORMService. Set the database with env variables, so lib/config/database.dart picks the test database:

DB_CONNECTION=sqlite DB_NAME=storage/test.sqlite APP_PORT=3999 dart test test/api_test.dart

See Testing: test HTTP routes for the server setup.

docs.title: See also
docs.text:
• Testing
  • Migration
  • Database: SQLite

docs.title: Contribute
docs.text:
This page shows how to work on Dox: set up the repo, run the tests, release packages and update the docs.

To send a change, fork the repo and open a pull request.

docs.title: 1. Clone the repo
docs.text: git clone git@github.com:dartondox/dox.git

docs.title: 2. Install melos
docs.text:
The repo is a Dart pub workspace. The melos config is in the root pubspec.yaml (under melos:). Use Dart 3.13 or newer.

dart pub global activate melos

docs.title: 3. Run melos bootstrap
docs.text:
It runs one dart pub get at the root. All local packages are linked. There is one pubspec.lock for the whole repo.

melos bs

docs.title: 4. Useful commands
docs.text:
# Run all tests (not dox_orm and not dox_mysql_native).
# Use `melos run test`. `melos test` is a built-in melos command.
melos run test

# Analyze and check format (same as CI)
melos run analyze
melos run format_check

# Run tests for dox_orm with postgres, mysql or sqlite
DB_PORT=5432 melos run test_pg
DB_USER=dox DB_PORT=3306 melos run test_mysql
melos run test_sqlite

# Build the dox cli executable (AOT).
# `dart compile exe` does not work: sqlite3 has a build hook. Use `dart build cli`.
cd packages/dox-cli
dart build cli --target bin/dox.dart --output build

# Run dox cli executable file
build/bundle/bin/dox --version

docs.title: If the project does not run
docs.text:
1. Remove pubspec.lock and .dart_tool at the root.
  2. Remove any old pubspec_overrides.yaml and pubspec.lock in packages/* (left from melos 3).
  3. Run melos bs again.

docs.title: Release (maintainers)
docs.text: The Release GitHub workflow (.github/workflows/publish.yaml) publishes all public packages to pub.dev. It runs when you push a tag like v3.0.0-alpha.4. It uses pub.dev automated publishing, so it needs no token or secret.

docs.title: Steps
docs.text:
1. Set the new version in the root pubspec.yaml, for example version: 3.0.0-alpha.4.
  2. Run the script. 
    bash bin/update_versions.sh
    It copies the version to every packages/*/pubspec.yaml. It sets every sibling dependency to ^3.0.0-alpha.4. It also writes the CLI version constant in packages/dox-cli/lib/src/version.dart.
  3. Add a ## 3.0.0-alpha.4 entry to the CHANGELOG.md of each package. pub.dev warns when it is missing.
  4. New package only: turn on pub.dev automated publishing for it. See One-time setup. If you skip this, the Release workflow fails on this package. A new package must first exist on pub.dev, so publish its first version by hand with dart pub publish.
  5. Commit and push. 
    git commit -am "release 3.0.0-alpha.4"
git push
  6. Wait until the Test workflow is green for this commit. The Release workflow does not run the tests.
  7. Tag and push the tag. This starts the publish. 
    git tag v3.0.0-alpha.4
git push origin v3.0.0-alpha.4

docs.title: What the workflow does
docs.text:
1. It checks that the tag (without v) is the root version, and that every package has this version. If not, it stops. Run bin/update_versions.sh and try again.
  2. It gets the publish order from bin/publish_order.py. The script reads every packages/*/pubspec.yaml. It puts each package after the sibling packages it depends on (dependencies and dev_dependencies). Packages with publish_to: none (like dox_app) are left out. A new package is picked up by itself.
  3. It publishes each package in this order. After each one, it waits until dart pub get can find the new version. Then the next package can depend on it.

To see the order on your machine:

python3 bin/publish_order.py

A package is skipped when its version is already on pub.dev. So if a run fails halfway, fix the problem and click "Re-run jobs". It continues where it stopped.

docs.title: Dry run
docs.text: Open Actions > Release > "Run workflow". It runs dart pub publish --dry-run for every package and publishes nothing. Warnings (for example a missing CHANGELOG entry) show as yellow warnings. They do not fail the run.

docs.title: One-time setup
docs.text:
Do this once for each published package, and for every new package before its first tag. The list of packages is the output of python3 bin/publish_order.py.

On pub.dev:

  1. Open https://pub.dev/packages/<name>/admin.
  2. Under "Automated publishing", click "Enable publishing from GitHub Actions".
  3. Repository: dartondox/dox.
  4. Tag pattern: v{{version}}.
  5. Tick "Require GitHub Actions environment" and set the environment to pub.dev.
  6. Save.

On GitHub, in dartondox/dox > Settings > Environments, there must be an environment named pub.dev. The publish job runs in it. Optional: add yourself as a required reviewer, and allow only tags v*. The old PUB_CREDENTIALS secret is not used any more.

docs.title: Docs
docs.text:
The docs site is https://dartondox.dev. It is built with MkDocs Material and mike. mike keeps one folder per version on the gh-pages branch.

URL What it is /3.x/... 3.x docs, built from develop /latest/... a copy of the newest version (now 3.x) /2.x/... the old 2.x docs, built from the v2.x branch / redirects to /latest/ old links like /the-basic/routing/ redirect to /latest/the-basic/routing/

docs.title: Write and preview
docs.text:
python3 -m venv .venv
.venv/bin/pip install mkdocs==1.6.1 mkdocs-material==9.7.7 mike==2.2.0
.venv/bin/mkdocs serve           # live preview of this branch
.venv/bin/mkdocs build --strict  # the same check as CI. Broken links fail.

docs.title: Deploy
docs.text:
• 3.x deploys by itself. The Docs workflow (.github/workflows/docs.yaml) runs on every push to develop that changes docs/, mkdocs.yml or the workflow. It runs mike deploy --update-aliases 3.x latest.
  • 2.x deploys by hand. Open Actions > Docs > "Run workflow", pick version 2.x. It builds from the v2.x branch (change it with the ref input).
  • After each deploy, the workflow writes small redirect pages for the old root links, the root index.html, a 404.html and the CNAME file. So dartondox.dev and old links keep working.
  • The workflow pushes with the built-in GITHUB_TOKEN. This works because gh-pages is not a protected branch.

docs.title: Why mike
docs.text:
• Old docs stay online at /2.x/, and readers switch with the version menu.
  • Each version is built once from its own branch. A new deploy does not touch the other versions.
  • Old links from before versioning are kept with redirect pages, so search results and blog posts still work.

docs.title: New major version
docs.text: When 4.x starts, deploy 4.x with mike deploy --update-aliases 4.x latest. Keep a v3.x branch, and add 3.x to the workflow input, so 3.x can still be fixed.

docs.title: Cache
docs.text:
This page shows the full API of dox_cache, the cache behind Cache() in Dox.

It works like Laravel Cache. It has remember, tags, atomic locks and four drivers.

Built into Dox

dox_core uses dox_cache for Cache(). In a Dox app, set the stores in config/cache.dart (the CacheConfig of this page), and use Cache(). Dox().cache is the CacheManager. Cache().repository is the CacheStore. This page is for the full API and for using dox_cache outside Dox.

docs.title: Install
docs.text:
dart pub add dox_cache

import 'package:dox_cache/dox_cache.dart';

Note

dox_core exports CacheConfig, CacheManager, CacheStore and CacheLock from this package. They are the same classes, so importing both packages is fine.

docs.title: Drivers
docs.text:
Driver What it is Shared between isolates memory a map in this isolate. Fast. Optional LRU size limit No file one JSON file per key in a folder Yes (same machine) redis Redis, with the ioredis package Yes null stores nothing. Use it to turn caching off -

Warning

Dox runs many isolates. Each isolate has its own memory cache. Use redis when isolates or servers must see the same data.

docs.title: Set up
docs.text:
CacheManager cache = CacheManager(CacheConfig(
  defaultStore: 'redis',
  stores: <String, Map<String, dynamic>>{
    'memory': <String, dynamic>{'driver': 'memory', 'max_size': 1000},
    'file': <String, dynamic>{'driver': 'file', 'path': 'storage/cache'},
    'redis': <String, dynamic>{'driver': 'redis', 'host': '127.0.0.1', 'prefix': 'app:'},
  },
));

CacheStore store = cache.store();     // the default store
await cache.store('file').get('a');   // a named store
Driver Options every driver driver, prefix (default dox_cache:) memory max_size: the most items. When full, the least recently used item is removed. No limit when not set file path (default storage/cache) redis host (default 127.0.0.1), port (default 6379), username, password, db, tls, pool_size

pool_size is the most Redis connections one store opens in one isolate. The default is 10. In practice a store uses one connection, because the cache sends no blocking commands. So you rarely need to change it. Each Dox isolate has its own connection.

docs.title: Basic use
docs.text:
await store.put('a', 1, Duration(minutes: 5));
await store.get('a');               // 1
await store.get('missing', 'none'); // 'none'
await store.has('a');               // true
await store.forget('a');

No ttl means forever

put without a ttl keeps the value forever. A zero or negative ttl removes the key. Cache() in dox_core takes the ttl as a named argument: Cache().put('a', 1, duration: Duration(minutes: 5)).

docs.title: Remember
docs.text:
Get the cached value, or run the function and cache the result.

List<dynamic> posts = await store.remember('posts', Duration(minutes: 10), () async {
  return await loadPostsAsJson();
});

docs.title: All methods
docs.text: Method What it does get(key, [default]) the value, or the default when missing or expired getRaw(key) the stored JSON text, with no decode. Null when missing put(key, value, [ttl]) store it add(key, value, [ttl]) store only when missing. Returns true when stored has(key) true when the value is not null forget(key) remove it. Returns true when it was there flush() remove all items of this store many(keys) / putMany(map, [ttl]) many keys at once increment(key, [by]) / decrement(key, [by]) change a number. A missing key starts at 0. The ttl stays forever(key, value) store without expiry remember(key, ttl, compute) see above rememberForever(key, compute) the same, without expiry pull(key, [default]) get it, then remove it tags([...]) a tagged view lock(name, [ttl, owner]) an atomic lock

docs.title: Values are JSON
docs.text:
Values must be JSON types: Map, List, String, num, bool, null. Other types throw.

  • A Map comes back as Map<String, dynamic>. A List comes back as List<dynamic>.
  • A stored null reads as a miss. has returns false for it.
  • For a model, store model.toJson(), not the model.

docs.title: Tags
docs.text:
await store.tags(<String>['users']).put('u1', 'Ann');
await store.tags(<String>['users']).flush(); // removes only the 'users' items

Tags work with every driver. Old items are not deleted right away. They are just not found any more, and they go away when their ttl ends.

docs.title: Locks
docs.text:
Only one worker runs the code at a time.

CacheLock lock = store.lock('report', Duration(seconds: 10));
if (await lock.get()) {
  try {
    // only one worker runs this
  } finally {
    await lock.release();
  }
}

bool got = await lock.block(Duration(seconds: 5)); // wait up to 5 seconds
  • get() takes the lock and returns true, or returns false when someone else has it.
  • block(timeout) tries again every 50 ms until it gets the lock or the time is over.
  • The ttl frees the lock by itself if the worker crashes. Without a ttl, the lock stays until release().
  • release() frees the lock only for the owner that took it.
  • memory and redis support locks. The memory lock works inside one isolate only. file and null throw UnsupportedError.

docs.title: Prefix
docs.text:
Every store has a prefix (default dox_cache:). It is added to every key. Use different prefixes when two apps share one Redis database.

Redis flush

flush deletes only the keys with the prefix. It never runs FLUSHDB. An empty prefix makes flush throw.

docs.title: Your own driver
docs.text:
class MyDriverFactory implements CacheDriverFactory {
  @override
  CacheDriver create(Map<String, dynamic> options) {
    return MyDriver(options);
  }
}

cache.extend('mine', MyDriverFactory()); // config: {'driver': 'mine'}
cache.addStore('ready', MemoryDriver()); // or add a ready driver

MyDriver extends CacheDriver. It must implement prefix, get, put, add, increment, forget and flush. Override lock to support locks.

docs.title: OpenAPI
docs.text:
This page shows how Dox makes OpenAPI 3.1 docs for your API, and how to change them. You write no docs code. You get a Scalar docs page at /docs, plus /openapi.json and /openapi.yaml.

The docs come from three places:

  • the routes: method, path, path params, middleware (login),
  • the request classes: a @Dto class,
  • the controllers: the /// comment, the arguments and the return type of each method.

docs.title: 1. Run the builder
docs.text:
dart run build_runner build      # or: dox build_runner:build

dox_builder reads your code and writes lib/openapi.g.dart. Run it again after you change routes, controllers, request classes or models. dox build_runner:watch does it for you while you work.

docs.title: 2. Pass the result to the config
3. Open /docs
docs.text:
Start the app and open http://localhost:3000/docs.

  • enabled is null by default. The docs are on only when APP_ENV is development or local. So production is off unless you set enabled: true.
  • When the docs are off, there is no extra work per request.
  • The document is built and encoded on the first /docs request, then kept. It is built again only when routes are added.

docs.title: The docs page
docs.text:
/docs uses Scalar by default. The page loads Scalar from the jsDelivr CDN, at a fixed version, and reads /openapi.json.

Change the look with scalar::

OpenApiConfig(
  registry: openApiRegistry,
  pageTitle: 'Blog API docs',          // default: info.title
  scalar: ScalarOptions(
    theme: ScalarTheme.purple,         // default: ScalarTheme.default_
    darkMode: true,                    // start in dark mode (default: false)
    showDownloadButton: false,         // hide "Download OpenAPI" (default: true)
    proxyUrl: 'https://proxy.scalar.com', // default: null, no proxy
  ),
);
Option Default What it does theme ScalarTheme.default_ Color theme. Same names as Scalar: moon, purple, deepSpace, saturn, kepler, mars and more. darkMode false Start in dark mode. The user can still switch. showDownloadButton true Show the button that downloads the document. proxyUrl null Send "Try it" requests through this proxy. Off by default, so requests go from the browser straight to your API.

pageTitle and all options are escaped, so a value can not break the page.

To use Swagger UI instead, set ui::

OpenApiConfig(registry: openApiRegistry, ui: DocsUi.swagger);

docs.title: What you write, what you get
docs.text:
A normal controller. There are no docs annotations here:

class BlogController {
  /// Get one blog
  ///
  /// Deleted blogs are not found.
  Future<Blog?> show(DoxRequest req, String id) async {
    return Blog().find(id);
  }

  /// Create a blog
  Future<Blog> store(CreateBlog body) async { ... }
}

// routes
Route.get('/blogs/{id}', [AuthMiddleware(), blogController.show]);

The generated docs for GET /blogs/{id}:

get:
  tags: [Blog]
  summary: Get one blog
  description: Deleted blogs are not found.
  operationId: BlogController.show
  parameters:
    - {name: id, in: path, required: true, schema: {type: string}}
  responses:
    "200":
      content:
        application/json:
          schema: {$ref: "#/components/schemas/Blog"}
    "401": {description: Not logged in}
    "404": {description: Not found}
    "500": {description: Server error}
  security:
    - bearerAuth: []

Blog is in components/schemas, made from the model:

Blog:
  type: object
  properties:
    id: {type: integer}
    title: {type: [string, "null"]}
    user: {anyOf: [{$ref: "#/components/schemas/User"}, {type: "null"}]}
    created_at: {type: [string, "null"], format: date-time}

docs.title: How each part is found
docs.text:
Part of the docs Where it comes from path, method the live route table path param types the controller arguments after the first one, in order. int id gives integer tags the controller class name without Controller (BlogController gives Blog) operationId Class.method, for example BlogController.show summary the first line of the /// comment description the rest of the /// comment request see Request below 200 answer the return type, see Response below 401 and bearerAuth a middleware whose class name ends with AuthMiddleware 404 the path has a {param} 422 the route has a request class. The body is {field: message} 500 every route

Routes that the builder does not know (for example inline closures) still get a basic entry.

docs.title: Request
docs.text:
The builder looks in this order. The first one wins.

  1. @Body(T), @Query(T) or @Request(T) on the method.
  2. An argument whose type is a @Dto class: store(CreateBlog body).
  3. A req.validate<T>() call in the method, where T is a @Dto class.

For POST, PUT and PATCH the request is the JSON body. For other methods each field is one query parameter. @Dto(source: Source.query) or Source.body chooses the place by hand. The route body: option still works, and it wins over all of these.

A @Dto class:

@Dto()
class CreateBlog {
  @Length(min: 3, max: 200)
  final String title;

  /// Text of the blog.
  final String? description;   // nullable: optional

  final int views;             // default: optional, `default: 0`

  final Status status;         // enum: only `draft` or `published`

  final List<Tag> tags;        // a list of another @Dto class

  const CreateBlog({required this.title, this.description, this.views = 0,
      required this.status, required this.tags});
}

The keys are the same as the keys the DTO reads: snake_case by default (postCode is post_code), or @Name('key'), or @Dto(keyCase: KeyCase.field). Each rule annotation adds its JSON Schema keys. See the rules reference.

docs.title: Response
docs.text:
The return type of the method gives the 200 answer. Future<T> counts as T.

Return type Schema a model (@DoxModel) $ref to the model. Keys in hidden are left out List<Model> an array of the model a @Dto class $ref to the class a Serializer<Model> the map that convert() returns, else the model Pagination total, per_page, last_page, current_page, data String, int, bool, Map, List the basic JSON type dynamic the types of the return values. A map literal gives its keys. Exceptions are left out DoxResponse, void no schema

A model schema has the primary key, the @Column fields, created_at, updated_at, the relations (only there when loaded) and the @Computed getters.

docs.title: Change the docs (optional)
docs.text:
Add these to a controller method when the automatic result is not what you want. They are all in dox_core.

@Summary('Log in')
@Description('Gives a bearer token for the Authorization header.')
@Tags(<String>['Auth'])
@Request(LoginUser)
@Response(200, LoginResult)
@Response(401, null, description: 'Wrong email or password')
Future<dynamic> login(DoxRequest req) async { ... }
Annotation What it does @Summary('text') short title. Default: the first line of the /// comment @Description('text') longer text. Default: the rest of the /// comment @Tags(['Users']) groups. On a method or on the class @Request(T) the request class. Body or query by the HTTP method @Body(T) the request class, always the body @Query(T) the request class, always the query @Response(status, Type, description: '') one answer. Add more than one for more codes. With a 2xx one, the return type is not used @ApiDeprecated() marks the route as deprecated. Dart @Deprecated works too @ApiIgnore() leaves the method (or the whole class) out of the docs @DoxController(tag: 'Users') for a class that the builder can not see in a Route.get(...) call

The Type of @Response can be a model, List<User>, a @Dto, a Serializer or a basic type like String.

Lower case names work too: @summary('Log in'), @description(...), @tags(...), @request(...), @body(...), @query(...), @apiDeprecated(), @apiIgnore(), @doxController(). The capital form is the normal Dart style. @Response has no lower case name, because response() is already the response helper of dox_core.

docs.title: Login schemes
docs.text:
A middleware whose class name ends with AuthMiddleware adds bearerAuth (a JWT bearer token) by itself. For other middleware, or another scheme, set it in the config:

OpenApiConfig(
  registry: openApiRegistry,
  securitySchemes: <String, SecurityScheme>{
    'apiKey': SecurityScheme.apiKey(name: 'X-API-Key'),
  },
  securityByMiddleware: <String, List<Map<String, List<String>>>>{
    'ApiKeyMiddleware': <Map<String, List<String>>>[
      <String, List<String>>{'apiKey': <String>[]},
    ],
  },
);

docs.title: How a route finds its docs
docs.text:
Routes are added when the app starts, so the builder can not see the final route table. It writes two lists into openapi.g.dart:

  • the docs of each controller method, by Class.method,
  • each Route.get(...) / Route.resource(...) call it found, with its path and Class.method.

At runtime, Dox reads the method name of each route handler. It picks the route call with the same HTTP method and the same end of path. If there is none, it picks the only method with that name and the same argument types. Group prefixes (like api/) do not matter.

Tip

If two controllers have a method with the same name, register the routes with Route.get('path', controller.method) so the builder can see them.

docs.title: Write the files: dox openapi:generate
docs.text:
dox openapi:generate              # storage/openapi/openapi.json and openapi.yaml
dox openapi:generate docs/api     # another folder

It runs bin/openapi.dart of your app:

bin/openapi.dart
import 'dart:io';

import 'package:dox_core/dox_core.dart';
import 'package:my_app/config/app.dart';

Future<void> main(List<String> args) async {
  Dox().initialize(appConfig);
  await Dox().writeOpenApi(args.isEmpty ? 'storage/openapi' : args.first);
  exit(0);
}

writeOpenApi runs your services and registers the routes. It does not start the server.

docs.title: Without Dox
docs.text:
dox_openapi also works on its own. Describe routes by hand with ApiDoc:

import 'package:dox_openapi/dox_openapi.dart';

ApiDoc docs = ApiDoc();
Map<String, dynamic> user = docs.schema('User', userSchema); // returns a $ref

docs.route('GET', '/users/{id}',
    summary: 'Get one user',
    tags: <String>['users'],
    params: <String, Object>{'id': <String, dynamic>{'type': 'integer'}},
    responses: <int, ResponseDoc>{
      200: ResponseDoc(schema: user, description: 'The user'),
      404: const ResponseDoc(description: 'Not found'),
    });

OpenApi api = OpenApi(info: const Info(title: 'My API', version: '1.0.0'), docs: docs);

api.toJson();                              // Map
api.toJsonString();                        // pretty JSON
api.toYaml();                              // YAML
await api.writeFiles('storage/openapi');   // openapi.json + openapi.yaml

// Serve the docs from your own server
OpenApiServer server = OpenApiServer(api); // Swagger UI: OpenApiServer(api, ui: DocsUi.swagger)
OpenApiResponse? page = server.handle('/docs'); // also '/openapi.json' and '/openapi.yaml'
if (page != null) {
  // send page.body with the header Content-Type: page.contentType
}

A schema can be a JSON Schema Map, a dox_validation schema, or any object with toJsonSchema(). Paths can use {id} or :id. Both become {id}. DoxRouteAdapter().addTo(docs, routes) adds a basic entry for each route you did not describe.

Tip

Do not serve /docs in production if your API is private.

docs.title: Socket.IO
docs.text:
This page shows how to run a Socket.IO server with dox_socketio, inside Dox or on its own.

dox_socketio is a Socket.IO v4 server for Dart. The official clients connect to it with no changes: socket.io-client (JavaScript v4) and the Dart socket_io_client package.

Socket.IO or WebSocket?

  • WebSocket (dox_websocket) runs inside the Dox HTTP server. It uses its own small JSON format.
  • Socket.IO (this page) works with the Socket.IO clients. It has acks, namespaces, binary data and long-polling.

docs.title: Install
docs.text: dart pub add dox_socketio

docs.title: Quick start
docs.text:
import 'package:dox_socketio/dox_socketio.dart';

Future<void> main() async {
  SocketIoServer io = SocketIoServer();
  io.on('connection', onConnection);
  await io.listen(3001);
}

void onConnection(Socket socket) {
  socket.emit('welcome', 'hello');
  socket.join('lobby');
  socket.on('chat', onChat);
}

void onChat(SocketEvent event) {
  event.socket.to('lobby').emit('chat', event.data); // everyone in lobby but me
  event.ack('ok'); // answer the client callback
}

Client (JavaScript):

import { io } from 'socket.io-client';

const socket = io('http://localhost:3001');
socket.emit('chat', 'hi', (answer) => console.log(answer)); // 'ok'

docs.title: In a Dox app: same port as HTTP
docs.text:
dox_core can serve Socket.IO at /socket.io/ on the app port. It is off by default.

dox_core does not export dox_socketio. Add it, and ioredis for the Redis adapter:

dart pub add dox_socketio ioredis
lib/config/socketio.dart
import 'package:dox_core/dox_core.dart';
import 'package:dox_socketio/dox_socketio.dart';
import 'package:ioredis/ioredis.dart';
import 'package:my_app/app/socket/chat.namespace.dart';
import 'package:my_app/config/env.dart';

Redis redis = Redis(RedisOptions(host: '127.0.0.1', port: 6379));

SocketIoConfig socketIo = SocketIoConfig(
  enabled: env.socketioEnabled,
  namespaces: <NamespaceHandler>[ChatNamespace(MessageService())],
  adapter: const RedisSocketAdapterFactory(), // shares broadcasts between isolates
);

/// makes the Redis adapter inside each isolate
class RedisSocketAdapterFactory extends SocketAdapterFactory {
  const RedisSocketAdapterFactory();

  @override
  Adapter create() {
    return RedisAdapter(subscriber: redis.duplicate(), publisher: redis);
  }
}

Add a getter for the SOCKETIO_ENABLED key to lib/config/env.dart, then run dart run build_runner build:

lib/config/env.dart
  /// serve Socket.IO on the app port
  bool get socketioEnabled => false;
lib/config/app.dart
AppConfig appConfig = AppConfig(
  socketIo: socketIo,
  // ...
);
SocketIoConfig option Default What it does enabled false serve Socket.IO at options.path options ServerOptions() see Options namespaces [] NamespaceHandler classes to register adapter null (in-memory) makes one adapter in each isolate
  • Requests to /socket.io/ go to Socket.IO before the router. Middleware and body reading are skipped.
  • When it is off, there is no extra work per request.
  • Dox().socketIo is the server of this isolate: Dox().socketIo?.to('room').emit('news', data).
  • dox_websocket (Route.websocket) still works next to it.

Many isolates

Dox runs one isolate per CPU core, and each isolate has its own Socket.IO server.

  • Clients should connect with websocket only. One websocket stays on one isolate. With the Redis adapter, a broadcast reaches clients on every isolate.
  • HTTP long-polling sends many requests, and they can reach different isolates. It only works with totalIsolate: 1, or with sticky sessions in front of many single-isolate servers.
const socket = io('http://localhost:3000/chat', { transports: ['websocket'] });

Dox logs this hint at startup when it runs many isolates and polling is allowed.

docs.title: Where to run it (outside Dox)
docs.text:
io.listen(port) opens its own port. Run it in its own small program, for example bin/socket.dart, next to the Dox HTTP server. Put both behind the same proxy.

  • io.attach(httpServer) uses a dart:io server you already have.
  • In your own dart:io server, call io.handle(request) when io.matches(request) is true.
  • The path is /socket.io/ by default.

docs.title: Namespaces in a class
docs.text:
A namespace can be a class. Its dependencies come in through the constructor.

class ChatNamespace extends NamespaceHandler {
  ChatNamespace(this.messages);

  final MessageService messages;

  @override
  String get path => '/chat';

  @override
  List<Middleware> get middleware => <Middleware>[checkToken];

  void checkToken(Socket socket) {
    if (socket.handshake.auth['token'] != 'secret') {
      throw SocketIoException('unauthorized', data: {'reason': 'bad token'});
    }
  }

  @override
  void onConnection(Socket socket) {
    socket.on('message', onMessage);
  }

  void onMessage(SocketEvent event) {
    event.ack(messages.save(event.data));
  }
}

io.register(ChatNamespace(MessageService()));

When a middleware throws, the client gets connect_error with the message and the data.

docs.title: Node.js to Dart
docs.text:
Node.js Dart socket.on('e', (a, cb) => ...) socket.on('e', (SocketEvent e) => ...), then e.data, e.args, e.ack(x) socket.emit('e', a, b) socket.emit('e', a) or socket.emitArgs('e', [a, b]) await socket.timeout(5000).emitWithAck('e', a) await socket.emitWithAck('e', a, timeout: Duration(seconds: 5)) socket.join(r) / socket.leave(r) the same socket.to(r).emit(...) the same socket.broadcast.emit(...) the same io.to(r).except(x).emit(...) the same io.of('/chat'), io.use(fn) the same socket.handshake .headers, .query, .auth, .address socket.data socket.data (a Map) io.in(r).fetchSockets() io.to(r).fetchSockets() (this server only)
  • disconnecting and disconnect give the reason in event.data, like transport close or ping timeout.
  • Binary data: send a Uint8List. It can be anywhere in lists and maps.

docs.title: Options
docs.text:
SocketIoServer(
  options: ServerOptions(
    path: '/socket.io/',
    pingInterval: Duration(seconds: 25),
    pingTimeout: Duration(seconds: 20),
    maxHttpBufferSize: 1000000,
    transports: ['polling', 'websocket'],
    cors: CorsOptions(origins: ['https://my.app'], credentials: true),
  ),
);
Option Default What it does path /socket.io/ the URL path pingInterval 25 s how often the server sends a ping pingTimeout 20 s how long to wait for the pong before the client is gone upgradeTimeout 10 s how long an upgrade from polling to websocket may take connectTimeout 45 s how long the client has to join a namespace maxHttpBufferSize 1,000,000 bytes the biggest message transports ['polling', 'websocket'] allowed transports allowUpgrades true let polling clients move to websocket cors null CORS headers for polling requests

docs.title: Many servers: Redis adapter
docs.text:
With more than one server process, use the Redis adapter. Then a broadcast on one server reaches the clients of all servers.

Redis redis = Redis(RedisOptions(host: '127.0.0.1', port: 6379));
SocketIoServer io = SocketIoServer(
  adapter: RedisAdapter(subscriber: redis.duplicate(), publisher: redis),
);

The subscriber needs its own connection. A Redis connection in subscribe mode can not run other commands.

  • It uses the message format of @socket.io/redis-adapter. A Node.js server can share broadcasts with it, when Node uses a JSON parser.
  • fetchSockets, socketsJoin and broadcast acks only work on the local server.
  • Long-polling needs sticky sessions when many servers share one port. If you can not have them, use transports: ['websocket'] on the client.

docs.title: Storage
docs.text:
This page shows how to save and read files with dox_storage.

dox_storage gives one API for files in many places: local disk, AWS S3 and S3-compatible services. The API follows FlyDrive and Laravel Filesystem.

Built into Dox

dox_core uses dox_storage for Storage(). In a Dox app, set the disks in config/storage.dart (a StorageConfig), and use Storage(). Storage().use('s3') gives the Disk of this page. Route.files('files') serves local signed URLs. This page is for the full Disk API and for using dox_storage outside Dox.

docs.title: Install
docs.text:
dart pub add dox_storage

import 'package:dox_storage/dox_storage.dart';

docs.title: Drivers
docs.text: Driver Use for Signed download URL Signed upload URL LocalDriver a folder on the server Yes (HMAC with your app key) No S3Driver AWS S3, Cloudflare R2, MinIO, DigitalOcean Spaces, GCS (HMAC keys) Yes (SigV4) Yes (SigV4) MemoryDriver tests fake URLs fake URLs

docs.title: Set up the disks
docs.text:
import 'dart:io';

import 'package:dox_storage/dox_storage.dart';

Map<String, String> env = Platform.environment;

DriveManager drive = DriveManager(
  defaultDisk: 'local',
  disks: <String, DriverContract>{
    'local': LocalDriver(LocalDriverConfig(
      root: 'storage',
      urlBase: 'https://app.test/uploads',
      appKey: env['APP_KEY'], // signs local URLs
    )),
    's3': S3Driver(S3DriverConfig(
      bucket: 'my-bucket',
      region: 'us-east-1',
      accessKeyId: env['AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID']!,
      secretAccessKey: env['AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY']!,
    )),
  },
);

Disk disk = drive.use('s3'); // or drive.use() for the default disk

use() throws UnsupportedOperationException when no disk has that name.

docs.title: Use a disk
docs.text:
await disk.put('avatars/1.png', bytes); // String, List<int> or Stream<List<int>>
await disk.put('a.json', '{}', options: WriteOptions(contentType: 'application/json', visibility: Visibility.public));
await disk.putStream('videos/big.mp4', File('big.mp4').openRead());

Uint8List data = await disk.get('avatars/1.png');
String text = await disk.getString('notes/a.txt');
Stream<List<int>> stream = await disk.getStream('videos/big.mp4');
ObjectMetaData meta = await disk.getMetaData('avatars/1.png'); // size, contentType, lastModified, etag
bool found = await disk.exists('avatars/1.png');

await disk.copy('a.png', 'b.png');
await disk.move('b.png', 'c.png');
await disk.delete('c.png');
await disk.deleteAll('avatars'); // every file under this prefix

ListResult page = await disk.listAll('avatars', ListOptions(recursive: true, limit: 100));
// next page: ListOptions(paginationToken: page.paginationToken)

await disk.setVisibility('avatars/1.png', Visibility.public);
Visibility v = await disk.getVisibility('avatars/1.png');

docs.title: Save an upload
docs.text:
Stream the upload to the disk. The file is not loaded into memory.

Route.post('/avatar', (DoxRequest req) async {
  RequestFile file = req.input('avatar');
  String key = 'avatars/${DateTime.now().microsecondsSinceEpoch}.${file.extension}';
  await disk.putStream(key, file.stream());
  return <String, String>{'url': await disk.getUrl(key)};
});

Warning

Do not use file.filename from the client as the key. A client can send any name. Make your own name, like above or with a uuid.

docs.title: URLs and signed URLs
docs.text:
String url = await disk.getUrl('avatars/1.png');

// a download link that works for 10 minutes
String signed = await disk.getSignedUrl('avatars/1.png',
    options: SignedUrlOptions(expiresIn: Duration(minutes: 10)));

// the browser can upload straight to S3 with this URL
String upload = await disk.getSignedUploadUrl('avatars/2.png',
    options: SignedUrlOptions(contentType: 'image/png'));
  • expiresIn is 30 minutes when you do not set it.
  • S3 signed URLs can live at most 7 days. This is an S3 rule.
  • contentDisposition asks the server to send this header on download, like attachment; filename="report.pdf".
  • Set urlBase to serve public files from a CDN.

docs.title: Check a local signed URL
docs.text:
In a Dox app, Route.files('files') does this for you.

LocalDriver.getSignedUrl returns <urlBase>/<key>?expires=...&signature=.... Check it in the route that serves the file:

LocalDriver local = LocalDriver(localConfig);
bool ok = local.verifySignedUrl(keyFromPath, req.uri.queryParameters);
if (!ok) {
  return response('Forbidden').statusCode(403);
}

docs.title: Cloudflare R2
docs.text:
Set supportsAcl: false. R2 does not take ACL headers.

S3DriverConfig(
  bucket: 'my-bucket',
  region: 'auto',
  endpoint: 'https://<account-id>.r2.cloudflarestorage.com',
  accessKeyId: '...',
  secretAccessKey: '...',
  supportsAcl: false,
);

docs.title: MinIO
docs.text:
MinIO needs path style URLs, so set forcePathStyle: true.

S3DriverConfig(
  bucket: 'my-bucket',
  region: 'us-east-1',
  endpoint: 'http://localhost:9000',
  forcePathStyle: true,
  accessKeyId: 'minioadmin',
  secretAccessKey: 'minioadmin',
);

docs.title: DigitalOcean Spaces
docs.text:
Spaces works like S3. Put the region of your space in region and in the endpoint.

S3DriverConfig(
  bucket: 'my-space',
  region: 'nyc3',
  endpoint: 'https://nyc3.digitaloceanspaces.com',
  accessKeyId: '...',
  secretAccessKey: '...',
);

docs.title: Google Cloud Storage
docs.text:
Set supportsAcl: false and supportsBatchDelete: false. GCS does not take ACL headers or the S3 batch delete call.

S3DriverConfig(
  bucket: 'my-bucket',
  region: 'auto',
  endpoint: 'https://storage.googleapis.com',
  accessKeyId: 'GOOG...',
  secretAccessKey: '...',
  supportsAcl: false,
  supportsBatchDelete: false,
);

Big files

  • put sends one request. S3 allows at most 5 GiB in one request.
  • putStream uses a multipart upload when the stream is bigger than multipartPartSize (8 MiB). Only one part is in memory at a time. The limit is about 78 GiB. Raise multipartPartSize for bigger files.
  • copy and move copy on the server. S3 allows at most 5 GiB here.

docs.title: Keys are checked
docs.text:
• a//b/./c.txt becomes a/b/c.txt. \ becomes /.
  • .., absolute paths (/etc/passwd) and null bytes throw InvalidKeyException.
  • LocalDriver also checks that the path stays inside its root folder.

docs.title: Errors
docs.text:
All errors extend StorageException and have the key.

Error When FileNotFoundException the file does not exist PermissionDeniedException file system permission error, or S3 403 InvalidKeyException unsafe key UnsupportedOperationException the driver can not do this DriverException anything else. The first error is in cause

docs.title: Tests
docs.text:
fake() swaps a disk for a memory disk.

Disk fake = drive.fake('s3'); // drive.use('s3') now writes to memory
await uploadAvatar();         // your code
expect(await fake.exists('avatars/1.png'), isTrue);
drive.restore('s3');

docs.title: Your own driver
docs.text:
Implement DriverContract and register it.

class DropboxDriver implements DriverContract { ... }

drive.register('dropbox', DropboxDriver(...));
await drive.use('dropbox').put('a.txt', 'hello');

docs.title: Validation
docs.text:
dox_validation checks input and gives you typed Dart objects. It has two parts:

  1. DTOs: a class with @Dto() and rule annotations. A generator writes the checks. Use this for almost everything.
  2. Fluent schemas: v.object(...), like Zod. Use it only when the shape is known at runtime.

Both give all errors at once, and a JSON Schema for OpenAPI.

Built into Dox

dox_core uses dox_validation and exports it. import 'package:dox_core/dox_core.dart' is all you need. The guide is at Validation. Every rule is in the rules reference. This page is about the package itself, and about using it outside Dox.

docs.title: Install (outside Dox)
docs.text:
dart pub add dox_validation
dart pub add dev:dox_builder dev:build_runner

import 'package:dox_validation/dox_validation.dart';

The DTO generator is in dox_builder. Run it with dart run build_runner build. @Unique and @Exists are in dox_orm, not here.

docs.title: DTOs
docs.text:
import 'package:dox_validation/dox_validation.dart';

part 'create_user.dto.g.dart';

@Dto()
class CreateUser {
  @Length(min: 3, max: 50)
  @Trim()
  final String name;

  @Email()
  final String email;

  const CreateUser({required this.name, required this.email});

  static const DtoSchema<CreateUser> schema = $CreateUserDto;
}

The generator makes, for each @Dto class:

Name What it is $CreateUserDto a const DtoSchema<CreateUser>: the checks, the converter and the JSON Schema lib/dtos.g.dart const List<DtoSchema<Object>> dtos: every DTO in lib/. Dox uses it to find DTOs by type.

The static const ... schema = $CreateUserDto; line is how you reach the schema: CreateUser.schema.

docs.title: DtoSchema<T>
docs.text:
DtoSchema<T> is also a Schema<T>. So it works everywhere a schema works: inside v.object(...), v.list(...), with OpenAPI, and as a StandardSchema.

Member Does Future<T> validateMap(Map<String, dynamic> input, {Source source = Source.body, Map<String, String> params = const {}, MessageResolver? messages, String? locale}) all checks, then the object. Throws ValidationException with the errors. Future<ParseResult<T>> safeValidateMap(input, {source, params, messages, locale}) the same, but never throws for bad input. result.success, result.value, result.errors. T fromMap(Map<String, dynamic> input) builds the object with no checks. Reads keys, converts JSON types, uses defaults. A wrong type throws a TypeError. Only for data you trust. Map<String, dynamic> toMap(T value) the object as a map with the input keys (snake_case). DateTime becomes an ISO 8601 string, an enum its name. Map<String, dynamic> toJsonSchema() JSON Schema (draft 2020-12). parse, safeParse, parseAsync, safeParseAsync the normal Schema methods, with Source.body. parse throws a StateError when the DTO has async rules. Type get type, String get name CreateUser and 'CreateUser'.

source: Source.query reads the map like a query string: text is converted to the field type. params are path params, used by @Unique(ignoreParam: ...). messages and locale change the error text for this call. See Messages.

ParseResult<CreateUser> result = await CreateUser.schema.safeValidateMap(input);
if (!result.success) {
  print(result.errors); // {'email': 'The email is not a valid email'}
}
ParseResult member What it is success true when there are no errors value the result. null when success is false errors the first message for each field, like {'user.email': '...'} fieldErrors all messages for each field issues the full list of ValidationIssue objects, with code and path

Note

dox_core has its own ValidationException (the HTTP 422 one), so it does not export the one from dox_validation. In a Dox app, both answer 422 when thrown in a controller. In tests, prefer safeValidateMap.

docs.title: JSON Schema of a DTO
docs.text:
For the CreateUser from the Validation guide (with age and role):

CreateUser.schema.toJsonSchema();

{
  "type": "object",
  "title": "CreateUser",
  "properties": {
    "name": { "type": "string", "minLength": 3, "maxLength": 50 },
    "email": { "type": "string", "format": "email" },
    "age": { "type": ["integer", "null"], "minimum": 18 },
    "role": { "type": "string", "enum": ["admin", "user"], "default": "user" }
  },
  "required": ["name", "email"]
}
  • required lists the required fields only.
  • A nullable field has "type": [..., "null"]. A default becomes default.
  • A nested DTO goes in $defs under its class name, with a $ref. OpenAPI moves it to components/schemas.
  • @Dto(strict: true) adds "additionalProperties": false.
  • A /// doc comment on a field becomes description.
  • Each rule adds its keys. See the rules reference.

docs.title: Fluent schemas (for dynamic input)
docs.text:
Use these when you only know the fields at runtime. The output is a Map, not a class.

final ObjectSchema createUser = v.object(<String, Schema<Object?>>{
  'name': v.string().trim().min(3).max(50),
  'email': v.string().email(),
  'age': v.coerce.int().min(18).optional(),
  'role': v.enumOf<String>(<String>['admin', 'user']).defaultTo('user'),
  'tags': v.list(v.string()).max(5),
  'address': Address.schema, // a DTO inside a fluent schema
});

// throws ValidationException when the input is not valid
Map<String, dynamic> data = createUser.parse(input);

// never throws for bad input
ParseResult<Map<String, dynamic>> result = createUser.safeParse(input);

In a controller: Map<String, dynamic> data = await req.validateSchema(createUser);

Different defaults

Fluent schemas do not follow the DTO rules. A key is required unless you add optional(). "" is a value, not "missing". Text is not converted, unless you use v.coerce.

docs.title: Schemas
docs.text:
Schema Checks v.string() min, max, length, nonEmpty, email, url, uuid, ip, datetime, regex, startsWith, endsWith, includes, alpha, alphaDash, alphaNumeric, trim, toLowerCase, toUpperCase v.int(), v.num() min, max, gt, lt, positive, nonNegative, multipleOf v.bool() v.date() DateTime only. min, max v.enumOf([...]), v.literal(x) v.list(item) min, max, nonEmpty v.object({...}) strict, passthrough, strip, pick, omit, extend, partial v.map(values, keys: ...) any keys v.union([...]) the first match wins v.any(), v.file() file() has image and extensions

On every schema:

  • optional(): the key may be missing. null is still an error.
  • nullable(): the value may be null. The key must be there.
  • nullish(): both.
  • defaultTo(x): the value when the key is missing. (default is a reserved word in Dart.)
  • transform(fn), refine(fn), refineAsync(fn), superRefine(fn), superRefineAsync(fn), use(rule).
  • describe(text), example(x): only used in the JSON Schema.

docs.title: Coercion
docs.text:
Query strings and form data are text. v.coerce turns text into the right type first.

v.coerce.int().parse('42');       // 42
v.coerce.num().parse('4.5');      // 4.5
v.coerce.bool().parse('on');      // true (true/1/yes/on, false/0/no/off)
v.coerce.date().parse('2024-01-31');
v.coerce.string().parse(5);       // '5'

docs.title: Checks across fields
docs.text:
final ObjectSchema signUp = v.object(<String, Schema<Object?>>{
  'password': v.string().min(8),
  'confirm': v.string(),
}).refine((Map<String, dynamic> data) {
  return data['password'] == data['confirm'];
}, message: 'Passwords do not match', path: <Object>['confirm']);

docs.title: Async checks
docs.text: refineAsync runs a check that needs the database. Then use parseAsync() or safeParseAsync(). parse() throws a StateError when a schema has async checks.

docs.title: Custom rules in a fluent schema
docs.text:
A Rule<T> class works in both worlds: as an annotation on a DTO, and with use() here.

v.string().min(3).use(const Slug());

See Custom rules for how to write one.

docs.title: Messages
docs.text:
Each error has a code, like required or min_length. Placeholders: {field}, {value}, and rule values like {min} and {max}.

// for the whole app (outside Dox; in Dox use AppConfig(validationMessages: ...))
MessageResolver.global = MessageResolver(messages: <String, String>{
  'required': 'Please fill in {field}',
});

// for one call
createUser.safeParse(input, messages: MessageResolver(messages: <String, String>{
  'email.required': 'We need your email',
}));

For other languages, extend MessageResolver and override resolve(). See Messages.

docs.title: Standard Schema
docs.text: Every schema, and every DtoSchema, implements the Standard Schema interface (StandardSchema). Code that only needs to validate can accept any StandardSchema, from Dox or from another library.

docs.title: Reference
docs.text:
Short lookup pages. Every value on these pages comes from the source code of version 3.0.0-alpha.4.

Page What is on it App config every field of AppConfig and the config classes it holds, with type, default and meaning CLI every dox command, its options and the files it writes Environment variables every env var the framework and its packages read HTTP exceptions the exception classes, their status codes and the body a client gets Request and response the members of DoxRequest, DoxResponse and response() Troubleshooting known problems, the exact error text, the cause and the fix Cheat sheet one page of the code you use every day, with links to the full pages Production checklist what to check before you deploy, and what Dox does not do for you Error index every message Dox prints or throws, when it happens and what to do

docs.title: App config
docs.text:
AppConfig is the one object you give to Dox().initialize(). It lives in lib/config/app.dart. This page lists every field, with its type, its default and what it does.

Source: packages/dox-core/lib/interfaces/app_config.dart.

docs.title: Server
docs.text: Field Type Default Meaning appKey String required Encrypts cookies (req.cookie(), DoxCookie) and signs local storage URLs. In production the app stops at start when it is empty. Make one with dox key:generate. serverPort int 3000 The port the HTTP server listens on. totalIsolate int? Platform.numberOfProcessors Isolates (threads) that serve HTTP, all on the same port. On Windows the native server runs on one isolate. server ServerBackend ServerBackend.native Which HTTP server runs: native (Rust, dox_http_native) or dartIo. The env var DOX_SERVER wins over this value. See Native server. compress bool false gzip responses in Dart (HttpServer.autoCompress). It costs CPU on every response. Let a proxy do it when you have one. maxBodySize int 10 * 1024 * 1024 (10 MB) Biggest JSON or urlencoded body in bytes. Bigger gets 413. maxMultipartSize int 100 * 1024 * 1024 (100 MB) Biggest multipart/form-data body (file uploads) in bytes. Bigger gets 413. trustedProxies List<String> [] IPs or CIDR ranges of reverse proxies. Only when the direct client is in this list does Dox read X-Forwarded-For for req.ip() and X-Forwarded-Proto for req.scheme(). ['*'] trusts any client.

docs.title: Routing and request handling
docs.text: Field Type Default Meaning routers List<Router> [] The router classes that register routes. globalMiddleware List<dynamic> [] Middleware that runs on every route. A function or an IDoxMiddleware. dtos List<DtoSchema<Object>> [] Every DTO of the app: dtos from lib/dtos.g.dart. Dox finds the DTO of a controller parameter and of req.validate<T>() with it. validationMessages MessageResolver? null (English messages) Messages for validation errors, for example in other languages. responseHandler ResponseHandlerInterface? null A class with DoxResponse handle(DoxResponse res). It sees every response before it is sent. errorHandler Function(Object?, StackTrace) defaultErrorHandler Called for every unhandled error. The default logs the error with Logger.warn and the stack with Logger.danger. services List<DoxService> [] Classes with a setup() method. Dox runs them in every isolate at start. The ORM, auth and WebSocket are set up here.

docs.title: Sub configs
docs.text: Field Type Default Meaning cors CORSConfig CORSConfig() CORS headers. See CORSConfig. logger LoggerConfig LoggerConfig() The Logger output. See LoggerConfig. cache CacheConfig file store in storage/cache, plus a memory store Cache stores for Cache(). See CacheConfig. storage StorageConfig local disk with root storage Storage disks for Storage(). See StorageConfig. openApi OpenApiConfig OpenApiConfig() /docs, /openapi.json and /openapi.yaml. See OpenApiConfig. socketIo SocketIoConfig SocketIoConfig() (off) Socket.IO on the HTTP port. See SocketIoConfig.

docs.title: CORSConfig
docs.text:
Source: packages/dox-core/lib/interfaces/app_config.dart. Headers are set in packages/dox-core/lib/http/http_cors_handler.dart.

A value can be a String ('*' or a comma list) or a List<String>. A null value sends no header.

Field Type Default Header enabled bool true Send CORS headers. A route can override it with its own cors setting. origin dynamic null Access-Control-Allow-Origin methods dynamic null Access-Control-Allow-Methods headers dynamic null Access-Control-Allow-Headers exposeHeaders dynamic null Access-Control-Expose-Headers credentials bool? null Access-Control-Allow-Credentials maxAge num? null Access-Control-Max-Age in seconds

Note

With the default CORSConfig() every value is null. So enabled: true alone sends no header. Set origin at least.

docs.title: LoggerConfig
docs.text: Field Type Default Meaning name String '' The name field in each JSON log line. enabled bool false Turn the Logger on. prettyPrint bool false true prints colored text. false prints one JSON object per line (for log services). level String 'info' Stored, but not read by the logger in this version.

docs.title: CacheConfig
docs.text:
Source: packages/dox-cache/lib/src/cache_config.dart. Option keys: packages/dox-cache/lib/src/constants/cache_constants.dart.

Field Type Default Meaning defaultStore String required The store Cache() uses when no store is named. stores Map<String, Map<String, dynamic>> required Store name to options. Each store needs a driver option.

Options of each driver:

Driver Option Type Default Meaning all driver String required file, memory, redis or null all prefix String dox_cache: Text in front of every key. file path String storage/cache Folder of the cache files. memory max_size int no limit Most items in the map. redis host String 127.0.0.1 Redis host. redis port int 6379 Redis port. redis username String none Redis user. redis password String none Redis password. redis db int 0 Redis database number. redis tls bool false Use TLS. redis pool_size int 10 Most connections per store.

docs.title: StorageConfig
docs.text:
Source: packages/dox-core/lib/storage/storage_config.dart.

Field Type Default Meaning defaultDisk String 'local' The disk Storage() uses when no disk is named. disks Map<String, Map<String, dynamic>> {'local': {'driver': 'local', 'root': 'storage'}} Disk name to options. Each disk needs a driver option.

Options of each driver:

Driver Option Type Default Meaning all driver String required local, s3 or memory local root String storage Folder of the files. local url String none Base of the public URLs, like http://localhost:3000/files. local app_key String AppConfig.appKey Key that signs the URLs. local visibility String public public or private. s3 bucket String required Bucket name. s3 region String us-east-1 Region. s3 key String required Access key id. s3 secret String required Secret access key. s3 token String none Session token. s3 endpoint String none Custom endpoint (R2, MinIO, Spaces). s3 path_style bool false Use path style URLs. s3 url String none Base of the public URLs. s3 visibility String private public or private. s3 acl bool true The service supports ACLs. s3 batch_delete bool true The service supports batch delete.

An unknown driver throws ArgumentError('Storage disk "<name>" has unknown driver "<type>"').

docs.title: OpenApiConfig
docs.text:
Source: packages/dox-core/lib/openapi/openapi_config.dart.

Field Type Default Meaning enabled bool? null Serve the docs routes. null means: on only when APP_ENV is development or local. info Info Info(title: 'Dox API', version: '1.0.0') Title and version of the API. servers List<Server> [] Base URLs of the API. securitySchemes Map<String, SecurityScheme> {} Ways to log in, like {'bearerAuth': SecurityScheme.bearer()}. securityByMiddleware Map<String, List<Map<String, List<String>>>> {} Security for routes that use a middleware class with this name. AuthMiddleware gets bearerAuth when it is not in the map. registry OpenApiRegistry OpenApiRegistry() (empty) What dox_builder found in the code. Pass openApiRegistry from lib/openapi.g.dart. ui DocsUi DocsUi.scalar scalar or swagger. scalar ScalarOptions ScalarOptions() Options of the Scalar page. See below. pageTitle String? null (uses info.title) Title of the /docs page.

ScalarOptions (packages/dox-openapi/lib/src/docs_ui.dart):

Field Type Default Meaning theme ScalarTheme ScalarTheme.default_ One of default_, alternate, moon, purple, solarized, bluePlanet, deepSpace, saturn, kepler, elysiajs, fastify, mars, laserwave, none. darkMode bool false Start in dark mode. showDownloadButton bool true Show the download button for the OpenAPI document. proxyUrl String? null Send "Try it" requests through this proxy.

docs.title: SocketIoConfig
docs.text:
Source: packages/dox-core/lib/socketio/socket_io_config.dart.

Field Type Default Meaning enabled bool false Mount Socket.IO on the HTTP port at /socket.io/. options ServerOptions ServerOptions() Engine options. See below. namespaces List<NamespaceHandler> [] Namespaces to register, like ChatNamespace(). adapter SocketAdapterFactory? null (in memory) Makes the adapter in each isolate. Use a Redis adapter with many isolates.

ServerOptions (packages/dox-socketio/lib/src/engine/server_options.dart). The defaults match the Node.js server.

Field Type Default Meaning path String /socket.io/ URL path. Must end with /. pingInterval Duration 25 s Time between two server pings. pingTimeout Duration 20 s Time to wait for a pong before the session is closed. upgradeTimeout Duration 10 s Time a websocket upgrade may take. connectTimeout Duration 45 s Time a client has to join a namespace after the handshake. maxHttpBufferSize int 1000000 Biggest message in bytes a client may send. transports List<String> ['polling', 'websocket'] Allowed transports. allowUpgrades bool true Allow upgrades from polling to websocket. cors CorsOptions? null (no CORS headers) CORS for the long-polling requests.

CorsOptions:

Field Type Default Meaning origins List<String> ['*'] Allowed origins. credentials bool false Send Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true. methods List<String> ['GET', 'POST'] Allowed methods for preflight. allowedHeaders List<String>? null (the requested headers) Allowed request headers. maxAge Duration? null How long a browser may cache the preflight answer.

docs.title: DatabaseConfig
docs.text:
The database is not a field of AppConfig. A service calls SqlQueryBuilder.initializeWithDatabaseConfig(databaseConfig) in its setup(). Source: packages/dox-orm/lib/src/types/database_config.dart and connection_config.dart.

Field Type Default Meaning connection String required Name of the connection to use. A missing name throws Exception('<name> not found'). connections Map<String, ConnectionConfig> required Connection name to config.

ConnectionConfig:

Field Type Default Meaning driver Driver required Driver.postgres, Driver.mysql (also MariaDB) or Driver.sqlite. host String 'localhost' Database host. Not used by sqlite. port int 0 Database port. Not used by sqlite. user String '' Database user. Not used by sqlite. password String '' Database password. Not used by sqlite. database String required Database name. For sqlite: the file path, or :memory:. useSSL bool false Use TLS. Postgres with TLS uses the Dart driver, not the native one. debug bool required Print every query with printer. printer QueryPrinter? null ConsoleQueryPrinter(), PrettyQueryPrinter(), FileQueryPrinter() or your own. extra Map<String, dynamic> {} Driver options. See below. driverFactory DBDriver Function(ConnectionConfig)? null Your own driver class. It wins over every other setting.

Keys of extra:

Driver Key Type Default Meaning postgres, mysql native bool true false uses the Dart driver instead of the native (Rust) one. postgres, mysql maxConnectionCount int 10 Most open connections. postgres, mysql preparedStatementCacheSize int 100 Prepared statements kept per connection. postgres sslMode postgres SslMode none Setting it uses the Dart driver. mysql collation String utf8mb4_general_ci Connection collation. mysql timeoutMs int 10000 Connect timeout. mysql allowPublicKeyRetrieval bool true Ask the server for its RSA key (needed for caching_sha2_password without TLS). mysql serverPublicKey String none The server RSA key, so it is not asked for. mysql timeZone String none Session time zone. mysql maxConnectionAge Duration 12 hours Close and reopen a connection after this time. sqlite busyTimeout int 5000 PRAGMA busy_timeout in milliseconds.

docs.title: AuthConfig
docs.text:
Auth is not a field of AppConfig. A service calls Auth.initialize(AuthConfig(...)) in its setup(). Source: packages/dox-auth/lib/src/interfaces.dart.

Class Field Type Default Meaning AuthConfig defaultGuard String required The guard Auth() uses when no guard is named. AuthConfig guards Map<String, AuthGuard> {} Guard name to guard. AuthGuard driver AuthDriver required How a token is made and checked, like JwtAuthDriver(secret: SecretKey(...)). AuthGuard provider AuthProvider required Where users come from. AuthProvider model dynamic Function() required Makes the user model, like () => User(). AuthProvider identifierFields List<String> ['email'] Columns attempt() matches the login with. AuthProvider passwordField String 'password' Column with the bcrypt hash.

docs.title: Full example
docs.text:
This is the lib/config/app.dart of a new project. The sub configs live in their own files in lib/config/.

lib/config/app.dart
import 'dart:io';

import 'package:dox_core/dox_core.dart';
import 'package:my_app/app/http/response_handler.dart';
import 'package:my_app/config/cache.dart';
import 'package:my_app/config/cors.dart';
import 'package:my_app/config/logger.dart';
import 'package:my_app/config/services.dart';
import 'package:my_app/config/storage.dart';
import 'package:my_app/routes/api.dart';
import 'package:my_app/routes/web.dart';
import 'package:my_app/config/env.dart';

AppConfig appConfig = AppConfig(
  /// Application secret key
  /// -------------------------------
  /// This key is use to encrypt/decrypt the data such as cache and cookies.
  /// Make sure to keep the `APP_KEY` as an environment variable and secure.
  ///
  /// Note: Changing the application key for an existing app will make all
  /// the cookies and cache invalid and also the existing encrypted data
  /// will not be decrypted.
  appKey: env.appKey,

  /// Server port
  /// -------------------------------
  /// App will be running on this port.
  serverPort: env.appPort,

  /// Total isolate (multi thread)
  /// -------------------------------
  /// Isolates that serve http requests, all on the same port.
  /// Default is one per CPU core, so the app uses all cores.
  /// Set `APP_TOTAL_ISOLATE` to change it.
  totalIsolate: env.appTotalIsolate ?? Platform.numberOfProcessors,

  /// Global middleware
  /// -------------------------------
  /// By registering global middleware here,
  /// middleware will be applied to all the routes.
  globalMiddleware: <dynamic>[LogMiddleware(enabled: true)],

  /// Routers
  /// -------------------------------
  /// Register routers to create route to dox framework.
  routers: <Router>[WebRouter(), ApiRouter()],

  /// Response handler
  responseHandler: ResponseHandler(),

  /// Cache stores (config/cache.dart)
  cache: cache,

  /// Storage disks (config/storage.dart)
  storage: storage,

  /// Cors configuration
  cors: cors,

  /// Service to run on multithread server
  services: services,

  /// logger configuration
  logger: logger,
);

The config files read their values from env, the typed env class in lib/config/env.dart. See Env reference.

The sub config files, with the values a new project ships:

lib/config/cache.dart
import 'package:dox_core/dox_core.dart';
import 'package:my_app/config/env.dart';

/// Cache stores
/// -------------------------------
/// `Cache()` uses the default store. `Cache().store('memory')` picks one.
/// Drivers: file, memory, redis, null. Values must be JSON types.
CacheConfig cache = CacheConfig(
  defaultStore: env.cacheStore,
  stores: <String, Map<String, dynamic>>{
    'file': <String, dynamic>{'driver': 'file', 'path': 'storage/cache'},

    /// one map per isolate, fast, not shared
    'memory': <String, dynamic>{'driver': 'memory', 'max_size': 10000},
  },
);
lib/config/storage.dart
import 'package:dox_core/dox_core.dart';
import 'package:my_app/config/env.dart';

/// Storage disks
/// -------------------------------
/// `Storage()` uses the default disk. `Storage().disk('local')` picks one.
/// Drivers: local, s3 (also R2, MinIO, Spaces), memory.
StorageConfig storage = StorageConfig(
  defaultDisk: env.storageDisk,
  disks: <String, Map<String, dynamic>>{
    /// files in the `storage` folder
    'local': <String, dynamic>{'driver': 'local', 'root': 'storage'},
  },
);
lib/config/logger.dart
import 'package:dox_core/dox_core.dart';
import 'package:my_app/config/env.dart';

LoggerConfig logger = LoggerConfig(
  /// Application name
  /// -------------------------------
  /// The name of the application you want to add to the log.
  name: env.appName,

  /// Toggle logger
  /// -------------------------------
  /// Enable or disable logger in application.
  enabled: true,

  /// Logging level
  /// -------------------------------
  /// The level from which you want the logger to flush logs.
  level: env.logLevel,

  /// Pretty print
  /// -------------------------------
  /// It is highly advised NOT to use `prettyPrint` in production, since it
  /// can have huge impact on performance.
  prettyPrint: env.isDevelopment,
);
lib/config/database.dart
import 'package:dox_orm/dox_orm.dart';
import 'package:my_app/config/env.dart';

/// Print every SQL query only in development.
/// Printing each query costs time, so it is off in production.
bool _debug = env.isDevelopment;

DatabaseConfig databaseConfig = DatabaseConfig(
  /// Connection
  /// -------------------------------
  /// The connection to use. It is one key of `connections` below.
  connection: env.dbConnection,

  connections: <String, ConnectionConfig>{
    /// Postgres
    'postgres': ConnectionConfig(
      driver: Driver.postgres,
      host: env.dbHost,
      port: env.dbPort ?? 5432,
      user: env.dbUsername,
      password: env.dbPassword,
      database: env.dbName,
      extra: <String, dynamic>{
        /// Each isolate has its own pool.
        'maxConnectionCount': 10,
        'maxConnectionAge': Duration(hours: 1),
      },
      debug: _debug,
      printer: PrettyQueryPrinter(),
    ),

    /// MySQL and MariaDB
    'mysql': ConnectionConfig(
      driver: Driver.mysql,
      host: env.dbHost,
      port: env.dbPort ?? 3306,
      user: env.dbUsername,
      password: env.dbPassword,
      database: env.dbName,
      extra: <String, dynamic>{'collation': 'utf8mb4_general_ci'},
      debug: _debug,
      printer: PrettyQueryPrinter(),
    ),

    /// SQLite. `DB_NAME` is a file path, or `:memory:`.
    'sqlite': ConnectionConfig(
      driver: Driver.sqlite,
      database: env.dbName,
      debug: _debug,
      printer: PrettyQueryPrinter(),
    ),
  },
);
lib/config/cors.dart
import 'package:dox_core/dox_core.dart';

CORSConfig cors = CORSConfig(
  /// Enabled
  /// -------------------------------
  /// A boolean to enable or disable CORS integration.
  /// Setting to true will enable the CORS for all HTTP request.
  enabled: false,

  /// Origin
  /// -------------------------------
  /// Set a list of origins to be allowed for `Access-Control-Allow-Origin`.
  /// The value can be one of the following:
  /// Array       : An array of allowed origins.
  /// String      : Comma separated list of allowed origins.
  /// String (*)  : A wildcard (*) to allow all request origins.
  origin: '*',

  /// Methods
  /// -------------------------------
  /// Set a list of origins to be allowed for `Access-Control-Request-Method`.
  /// The value can be one of the following:
  /// Array       : An array of request methods.
  /// String      : Comma separated list of request methods.
