  /// String (*)  : A wildcard (*) to allow all request methods.
  methods: '*',

  /// Headers
  /// -------------------------------
  /// Set a list of origins to be allowed for `Access-Control-Allow-Headers`.
  /// The value can be one of the following:
  /// Array       : An array of allowed headers.
  /// String      : Comma separated list of allowed headers.
  /// String (*)  : A wildcard (*) to allow all request headers.
  headers: '*',

  /// Expose Headers
  /// -------------------------------
  /// Set a list of origins to be allowed for `Access-Control-Expose-Headers`.
  /// The value can be one of the following:
  /// Array       : An array of expose headers.
  /// String      : Comma separated list of expose headers.
  exposeHeaders: <String>[
    'cache-control',
    'content-language',
    'content-type',
    'expires',
    'last-modified',
    'pragma',
  ],

  /// Credentials
  /// -------------------------------
  /// Toggle `Access-Control-Allow-Credentials` header.
  credentials: true,

  /// MaxAge
  /// -------------------------------
  /// Define `Access-Control-Max-Age` header in seconds.
  maxAge: 90,
);
lib/config/services.dart
import 'package:dox_core/dox_core.dart';
import 'package:my_app/services/orm_service.dart';

/// Services to register on dox
/// -------------------------------
/// Since dox run on multi thread isolate, we need to register
/// below extra services to dox so that dox can
/// register again on new isolate.
List<DoxService> services = <DoxService>[ORMService()];
lib/services/orm_service.dart
import 'package:dox_core/dox_core.dart';
import 'package:dox_orm/dox_orm.dart';
import 'package:my_app/config/database.dart';

/// Query builder service
/// --------------------------
/// Sets up the query builder, so this project can use the ORM.
/// If this project does not need a database, delete this file
/// and remove it from config/services.dart.
class ORMService implements DoxService {
  @override
  Future<void> setup() async {
    SqlQueryBuilder.initializeWithDatabaseConfig(databaseConfig);
  }
}

A new project has no openapi.dart, socketio.dart or auth service. You add them when you need them. See OpenAPI, Socket.IO and Authentication.

docs.title: Routes
docs.text:
class ApiRouter extends Router {
  @override
  String get prefix => 'api';

  @override
  List<dynamic> get middleware => <dynamic>[];

  @override
  void register() {
    Route.get('/ping', (DoxRequest req) => 'pong');
  }
}
Code Does Route.get('/blogs', c.index) also post, put, patch, delete, options Route.post('/blogs', c.store, body: schema) body: is for the docs only. It checks nothing. Route.get('/blogs/{id}', c.show) path param. show(int id) Route.get('/posts/{page?}', c.list) optional param. list(int? page) Route.get('/docs/{path*}', c.page) rest of the path, with / Route.get('/me', <dynamic>[AuthMiddleware(), c.me]) middleware first, controller last Route.group('/blogs', () { ... }) prefix. Start it with /. Route.middleware(<dynamic>[M()], () { ... }) middleware for a group Route.domain('api.app.com', () { ... }) match by Host Route.resource('blogs', BlogController()) index, create, store, show, edit, update, destroy Route.files('files') serve a storage disk, signed URLs only Route.enabledCors(() { ... }) / Route.disabledCors(...) CORS for some routes Route.websocket('ws', (WebsocketEvent e) { ... }) needs dox_websocket

Controller parameters, by type: DoxRequest, one @Dto class, String/int/double/num/bool for path params (by position). Only positional parameters.

Middleware order: globalMiddleware, router middleware, group, route.

See Routing, Controller, Middleware.

class ApiKeyMiddleware implements IDoxMiddleware {
  @override
  dynamic handle(IDoxRequest req) {
    if (req.header('X-Api-Key') != 'secret') {

    }
    return req; // go on

}

@Dto()
class CreateBlog {
  @Length(min: 3, max: 200)

docs.title: Model
docs.text:
@DoxModel(table: 'blogs', softDelete: true)
class Blog extends BlogGenerator {
  @Column()
  String? title;

  @Column(name: 'user_id')
  int? userId;

  @BelongsTo(User)
  User? user;

  @HasMany(Comment)
  List<Comment> comments = <Comment>[];

  @override
  List<String> get hidden => <String>['secret'];
}
Code Does await Blog().find(1) / find('slug', 'a') one row or null await Blog().all() every row (ignores where) await Blog().where('status', 'live').get() rows that match await Blog().where('id', '>', 5).getFirst() first match or null await Blog().count() int await Blog().paginate(currentPage: 1, perPage: 20) Pagination, getData<Blog>() await Blog().create(<String, dynamic>{'title': 'a'}) insert and return the model blog.title = 'b'; await blog.save() insert or update await blog.delete() soft delete when softDelete: true await blog.forceDelete() / await blog.restore() real delete / undo soft delete Blog().withTrash() include soft deleted rows Blog().preload('comments').get() load a relation, one query await blog.$getRelation('user') load a relation on one model blog.related<Comment>('comments')?.where(...).get() relation query blog.toJson() / blog.toMap() map, hidden left out of toJson() Blog().query() a new, empty query

Relations: @HasOne(T), @HasMany(T), @BelongsTo(T), @ManyToMany(T). Options: foreignKey, localKey, onQuery, eager.

Events: override onCreating(), onCreated(), onSaving(), onUpdated(), onDeleting(), ... or Model.observe<Blog>(BlogObserver()). throw CancelModelEvent('why') in a "before" event stops it. saveQuietly() skips events.

See Model, Events, HasMany.

class CreateBlogsTable extends Migration {
  @override
  Future<void> up(Schema schema) async {
    await schema.create('blogs', (Table table) {
      table.id();
      table.foreignId('user_id').constrained('users').cascadeOnDelete();
      table.string('title');
      table.text('body').nullable();
      table.enumeration('status', <String>['draft', 'live']).defaultTo('draft');
      table.timestamps();
      table.softDeletes();
    });

  @override
  Future<void> down(Schema schema) async {
    await schema.dropIfExists('blogs');
  }
}

@DoxEnv()
abstract class AppEnv {
  static AppEnv load([EnvReader? reader]) => _$AppEnv.load(reader);

docs.title: CLI
docs.text:
Every dox command, from the command registry in packages/dox-cli/lib/src/command_registry.dart. The file templates are Dart strings inside packages/dox-cli/lib/src/tools/. The path of each template is given below.

How to install the CLI is on the Dox CLI page.

Rules that apply to every command:

  • dox with no command prints Could not find a command. Rundox helpfor more information.
  • An unknown command prints Could not find a command named "<name>".
  • Too few or too many arguments prints Invalid number of arguments for command "<name>". with the expected count.
  • A name you pass is turned into snake_case for the file and PascalCase for the class. BlogPost and blog_post give the same result.
  • A create:* command does not overwrite. When the file exists it prints <name> already exists and stops.

docs.title: dox create
docs.text:
dox create <project_name> [--version <version>]

Makes a new project from the dox-sample repo.

Option Meaning --version <v> (or --v) The release tag to clone, like 3.0.0-alpha.4 or v3.0.0-alpha.4. Without it, the newest dox-sample release with the same major version as the CLI is used (pre-releases included).

What it does:

  1. Turns the name into snake_case. Stops with Folder name "<name>" already exist when the folder is there.
  2. Reads the release list of dartondox/dox-sample and takes the newest release with the same major version as the CLI.
  3. Runs git clone --depth 1 --branch v<version> https://github.com/dartondox/dox-sample.git <name>.
  4. Deletes the .git folder.
  5. Replaces dox_sample with your project name in every file, except files under bin/dox.

Needs curl and git on the PATH.

Known bug: dox create my_app without --version throws RangeError

The command reads args[1] before it checks how many arguments there are. With only the project name you get RangeError (index): Invalid value: Only valid value is 0: 1. Workaround: always pass the version, dox create my_app --version 3.0.0-alpha.4.

Source: packages/dox-cli/lib/src/tools/create_project.dart.

docs.title: dox serve
docs.text:
dox serve [--ignore-build-runner]
dox s
dox server

Starts the dev server.

Option Meaning --ignore-build-runner Do not start dart run build_runner watch.

What it does:

  1. Starts dart run build_runner watch (unless the option is set).
  2. Starts dart run bin/server.dart and prints its output.
  3. Watches the project folder. When a .dart file changes it prints [Dox] File changed: <file>, waits 500 ms, kills the server and starts it again.

Source: packages/dox-cli/lib/src/tools/server_serve.dart.

docs.title: dox build
docs.text:
dox build

AOT compiles the app for production into build/bundle. Use this in production, not dart run.

What it does:

  1. When pubspec.yaml contains build_runner: runs dart run build_runner build. Stops with exit code 1 when it fails.
  2. Runs dart build cli --target bin/server.dart --output build.
  3. Copies db/ to build/bundle/db (migrations are read at start).
  4. Copies .env.example to build/bundle/.env.example.
  5. Prints [Dox] Built build/bundle. Run it with: cd build/bundle && ./bin/server.

Output:

Path What build/bundle/bin/server the native binary, no Dart SDK needed build/bundle/lib/ native libraries from build hooks (SQLite, dox_http_native, ...) build/bundle/db/ your migrations build/bundle/.env.example copy it to .env or set real env vars

dart compile exe can not build packages with build hooks, so the CLI uses dart build cli.

Source: packages/dox-cli/lib/src/tools/server_serve.dart (buildServer).

docs.title: dox build_runner:build and dox build_runner:watch
docs.text:
dox build_runner:build
dox build_runner:watch

Run dart run build_runner build once, or dart run build_runner watch. No options. The CLI does not pass --delete-conflicting-outputs (build_runner removed that flag).

docs.title: dox key:generate
docs.text:
dox key:generate

Makes a 32 character key (A-Z, a-z, 0-9, from Random.secure()) and writes it to APP_KEY in .env. Prints <key> : Key have been updated successfully in .env!.

What it does with .env:

  • Reads .env in the current folder. The file must exist, else the command fails with a file error.
  • Keeps every KEY=value line. Replaces the value of APP_KEY.
  • Adds APP_KEY=<key> as the first line when there is no APP_KEY.

Warning

The rewrite only keeps lines with exactly one =. A line like DATABASE_URL=postgres://u:p@h/db?a=b has two = and is dropped from .env. Comment lines are dropped too. Back up .env first when it has such lines.

Source: packages/dox-cli/lib/src/tools/generate_key.dart.

docs.title: dox env:generate
docs.text:
dox env:generate

Writes lib/config/env.dart, the typed env class, from .env.example.

  • Stops with .env.example is missing. (exit code 1) when there is no example file.
  • Stops with lib/config/env.dart is already there. Delete it to make it again. (exit code 1) when the file exists.
  • Prints Rundart run build_runner buildto make env.g.dart. when done.

Rules for each key: digits give int get x => <value>;, true/false give bool, an empty value gives String? get x;, any other value gives String get x; (required, no default). # comment lines above a key become its doc comment. A key that does not map back from camelCase gets @EnvKey('KEY').

Source: packages/dox-cli/lib/src/tools/env_tools.dart (EnvScaffold).

docs.title: dox env:check
docs.text:
dox env:check

Loads AppEnv from lib/config/env.dart with the real environment and .env. Prints The env is valid. or an EnvException with every missing or bad key (exit code 1).

It writes a small script to .dart_tool/dox/env_check.dart and runs it with dart run. It needs lib/config/env.dart and a name: in pubspec.yaml.

Source: packages/dox-cli/lib/src/tools/env_tools.dart (envCheck).

docs.title: dox openapi:generate
docs.text:
dox openapi:generate [dir]

Runs dart run bin/openapi.dart [dir]. That file writes openapi.json and openapi.yaml into dir (default storage/openapi). Stops with bin/openapi.dart is missing. (exit code 1) when the file is not there. See OpenAPI.

Source: packages/dox-cli/lib/src/tools/openapi_generate.dart.

docs.title: dox update
docs.text:
dox update

Runs dart pub global activate dox. This installs the latest stable version of the CLI, not a preview. For a preview run dart pub global activate dox 3.0.0-alpha.4 yourself.

Source: packages/dox-cli/lib/src/tools/update_dox.dart.

docs.title: dox version
docs.text:
dox version
dox v
dox -v
dox --version

Prints Dox version: <version>. Aliases: --version, -version, v, -v, --v.

docs.title: dox help
docs.text:
dox help [command]

Without a command: lists every command by category. With a command: prints its usage, description, category, aliases and argument count.

docs.title: dox create:controller
docs.text:
dox create:controller <name> [-r] [-ws]
Option Meaning -r A resource controller with index, create, store, show, edit, update, destroy. -ws A WebSocket controller.

A trailing Controller in the name is removed: UserController and User give the same file.

Form Writes Template plain lib/app/http/controllers/<name>.controller.dart _getSample in packages/dox-cli/lib/src/tools/create_controller.dart -r lib/app/http/controllers/<name>.controller.dart _getResourceSample in the same file -ws lib/app/ws/controllers/<name>.controller.dart _getWsSample in the same file

The plain and resource templates also make an instance: <Name>Controller <name>Controller = <Name>Controller();.

docs.text:
dox create:middleware <name>

Writes lib/app/http/middleware/<name>.middleware.dart: a class <Name>Middleware extends IDoxMiddleware with a handle(IDoxRequest req) that returns req. A trailing Middleware in the name is removed.

Template: _getSample in packages/dox-cli/lib/src/tools/create_middleware.dart.

docs.title: dox create:dto
docs.text:
dox create:dto <name>

Writes lib/app/http/dtos/<name>.dto.dart: a @Dto() class with one name field and part '<name>.dto.g.dart';. A trailing Dto in the name is removed. Prints Rundox build_runner:buildto make <name>.dto.g.dart.

Template: _getSample in packages/dox-cli/lib/src/tools/create_dto.dart.

docs.title: dox create:serializer
docs.text:
dox create:serializer <name>

Writes lib/app/http/serializers/<name>.serializer.dart: a class <Name>Serializer extends Serializer<<Name>>. It imports the model from lib/app/models/<name>/<name>.model.dart. A trailing Serializer in the name is removed.

Template: _getSample in packages/dox-cli/lib/src/tools/create_serializer.dart.

docs.title: dox create:model
docs.text:
dox create:model <name> [-m|--migration]
dox make:model <name> [-m|--migration]

Writes lib/app/models/<name>/<name>.model.dart: a @DoxModel() class with part '<name>.model.g.dart';.

Option Meaning -m or --migration Also make a create_<table>_table migration. The table is the plural snake name: BlogPost gives blog_posts. The model then gets @DoxModel(table: 'blog_posts').

Any other second argument prints Invalid option <x>, use -m or --migration (exit code 1).

Template: _getSample in packages/dox-cli/lib/src/tools/create_model.dart.

docs.title: dox make:migration
docs.text:
dox make:migration <name> [--sql]
dox create:migration <name> [--sql]
Option Meaning --sql Make a .sql file with -- up and -- down sections instead of a Dart class.

Writes db/migration/<yyyy>_<mm>_<dd>_<hhmmss>_<name>.dart (or .sql). Characters that are not letters, digits or _ are removed from the name.

For a Dart migration it also:

  • writes db/migration/migrations.dart, the registry of every Dart migration in the folder, sorted by name;
  • writes bin/migrate.dart when it is missing, and prints bin/migrate.dart created.

The Dart template depends on the name:

Name up() down() create_<table>_table schema.create('<table>', ...) with id() and timestamps() schema.dropIfExists('<table>') <x>_to_<table>_table (also from, in, on) schema.table('<table>', ...) schema.table('<table>', ...) anything else a comment a comment

Templates: dartMigrationSource, migrateEntrySource and _sampleSql in packages/dox-cli/lib/src/tools/create_migration.dart.

docs.title: Migrations
docs.text:
All migration:* commands work the same way:

  1. When bin/migrate.dart exists: write the registry again, then run dart run bin/migrate.dart <command> [args]. Your app code runs, so Dart migrations work.
  2. When there is no bin/migrate.dart but db/migration has Dart files: print db/migration has Dart migrations, but bin/migrate.dart is missing. (exit code 1).
  3. Else: run the .sql migrations with Migrator() from dox_migration in the CLI process.

The database comes from DB_CONNECTION, DB_HOST, DB_PORT, DB_USERNAME, DB_PASSWORD and DB_DATABASE (or DB_NAME). See Environment variables. A failed run prints the error and sets exit code 1.

Command Aliases What it does dox migration:run dox migrate Run the migrations that did not run yet. dox migration:rollback [--step=<count>] dox migrate:rollback Undo the last batch, or the last <count> migrations. Any other option prints Invalid option <x>, use --step=<count> (exit code 1). dox migration:reset dox migrate:reset Undo every migration. dox migration:refresh dox migrate:refresh Undo every migration, then run them all again. dox migration:status dox migrate:status Print which migrations ran, and their batch.

docs.title: Environment variables
docs.text:
Every env var the framework and its packages read. How to read your own keys with the typed env class is on the Environment Variables page.

The code reads env vars in three ways:

  • Env.get() and EnvReader (dox_core): a real environment variable wins over the .env file.
  • Platform.environment straight: only the real environment, .env is not read.
  • dox_migration has its own loadEnv(): it reads .env when the file exists, else the real environment. See the note below.

docs.title: Read by the framework
docs.text:
Variable Who reads it Default Meaning Example APP_ENV dox_core (Dox().checkAppKey(), OpenApiConfig.isEnabled) empty production makes a missing APP_KEY a startup error. development or local turn the /docs routes on when openApi.enabled is null. Read with Env.get. APP_ENV=production DOX_SERVER dox_core (DoxServer.usesNative()) not set (uses AppConfig.server) dartio, dart_io or dart:io forces the dart:io server. native forces the native server, also for an app with WebSocket routes. Real environment only. DOX_SERVER=dartio DOX_HTTP_THREAD dox_http_native (Rust, shared_thread()) not set (one thread per isolate) shared puts the servers of all isolates on one network thread. Off by default: on 2 cores it cut req/s by a quarter. Real environment only. DOX_HTTP_THREAD=shared DOX_DB_DRIVER dox_orm (NativeDrivers.wanted()) not set (native driver) dart uses the Dart postgres / mysql_dart driver instead of the native (Rust) one. Same as extra: {'native': false}. Real environment only. DOX_DB_DRIVER=dart DB_CONNECTION dox_migration (DbConnection.open()) postgres postgres, mysql or sqlite. Any other value means postgres. DB_CONNECTION=sqlite DB_HOST dox_migration localhost Database host. DB_HOST=127.0.0.1 DB_PORT dox_migration 5432 (postgres), 3306 (mysql) Database port. DB_PORT=5432 DB_USERNAME dox_migration postgres (postgres), root (mysql) Database user. DB_USERNAME=app DB_PASSWORD dox_migration postgres (postgres), empty (mysql) Database password. DB_PASSWORD=secret DB_DATABASE dox_migration falls back to DB_NAME, then dox Database name. For sqlite: the file path. DB_DATABASE=dox DB_NAME dox_migration dox Same as DB_DATABASE. DB_DATABASE wins when both are set. DB_NAME=dox HOME / USERPROFILE build hooks of dox_http_native, dox_postgres_native, dox_mysql_native empty Used to find ~/.cargo/bin/cargo when the library must be built from source. set by the OS DART_VM_OPTIONS the Dart VM not set Flags for the VM. The AOT binary from dox build reads it. Dox never sets VM flags for you. See Performance. DART_VM_OPTIONS=--new_gen_semi_max_size=64

Migrations and .env

dox_migration reads .env when the file exists, and only then falls back to the real environment. So with a .env file in the folder, a real DB_HOST is ignored. See Troubleshooting.

DOX_SERVER, DOX_HTTP_THREAD and DOX_DB_DRIVER are read with Platform.environment or std::env::var. They do not work from .env.

docs.title: Read by a new project
docs.text:
A new project (dox create) reads these keys through its typed env class, lib/config/env.dart. The framework itself does not read them. In code, use the getter: env.appPort.

Variable Getter Type Default Used for APP_NAME appName String dox LoggerConfig.name. APP_ENV appEnv String development development, staging or production. env.isDevelopment is true for development. It turns on prettyPrint of the logger and the query log of the database. Also read by the framework (see above). APP_PORT appPort int 3000 AppConfig.serverPort. APP_KEY appKey String required AppConfig.appKey. The app stops at start when it is missing. APP_TOTAL_ISOLATE appTotalIsolate int? not set: one per CPU core AppConfig.totalIsolate. LOG_LEVEL logLevel String info LoggerConfig.level. CACHE_STORE cacheStore String file CacheConfig.defaultStore: memory, file or redis. STORAGE_DISK storageDisk String local StorageConfig.defaultDisk: local, s3 or memory. DB_CONNECTION dbConnection String sqlite DatabaseConfig.connection: sqlite, postgres or mysql. DB_NAME dbName String db/dox.sqlite The database name. For SQLite: the file path. DB_HOST dbHost String localhost Database host. DB_PORT dbPort int? not set: 5432 for Postgres, 3306 for MySQL Database port. DB_USERNAME dbUsername String postgres Database user. DB_PASSWORD dbPassword String empty Database password.

To add a key, add a getter to AppEnv and run dart run build_runner build. See Environments.

The .env.example of a new project:

.env.example
APP_NAME=dox
APP_ENV=development
APP_PORT=3000
APP_KEY=KKep5qC6uHlAgrwaQTQewgMRSIqQnoj0

CACHE_STORE=file
STORAGE_DISK=local

# SQLite needs no setup. The file is created at the first start.
DB_CONNECTION=sqlite
DB_NAME=db/dox.sqlite

# Postgres or MySQL: set DB_CONNECTION=postgres or mysql and fill these in.
DB_HOST=localhost
DB_PORT=5432
DB_USERNAME=postgres
DB_PASSWORD=postgres

docs.title: Only for work on Dox itself
docs.text: Variable Who reads it Meaning PG_URL Rust tests of dox_postgres_native A Postgres URL. The test is skipped when it is not set. DB_HOST, DB_PORT, THREADS packages/dox-postgres-native/tool/stress.dart The stress tool.

docs.title: How .env is parsed
docs.text:
Env._loadEnv() in packages/dox-core/lib/env/env.dart:

  • One KEY=value per line. The key is trimmed.
  • The value is everything after the first =. A second = is kept.
  • Every ", ' and ` character is removed from the value. Then it is trimmed.
  • # is not special. KEY=abc # note gives the value abc # note.
  • An empty value, or the text null, counts as missing.
  • The file is read once per isolate, from the current working directory.

docs.title: Error index
docs.text:
A lookup table of the messages Dox prints or throws. Search this page for the text you see.

  • <...> is a part that changes, like a name or a number.
  • Dart adds a prefix to some errors: Bad state: (StateError), Invalid argument(s): (ArgumentError), Unsupported operation: (UnsupportedError), Exception: (Exception).
  • For problems that need a longer story, see Troubleshooting.

docs.title: dox_core: start of the app
docs.text: Text When What to do APP_KEY is not set. Rundox key:generateand put the key in .env appKey is empty. A warning, or a StateError that stops the app when APP_ENV=production. Run dox key:generate, or set APP_KEY in the env. [dox] warning: dox_http_native did not load, using the dart:io server (<reason>) The native HTTP library is missing or from another version. See Troubleshooting. Or set DOX_SERVER=dartio. Server started at http://127.0.0.1:<port> with <n> isolate (<backend>) Normal start. <backend> is native or dart:io. Nothing. WebSocket or Socket.IO routes: using the dart:io server The app has WebSocket or Socket.IO. The native server can not upgrade yet. Nothing. This is info. Windows: the native server runs on one isolate Windows has no SO_REUSEPORT. Nothing, or DOX_SERVER=dartio to use every core. Socket.IO runs on <n> isolates: clients should use transports: ['websocket'] ... Socket.IO with more than one isolate and long-polling on. Use a Redis adapter, and transports: ['websocket'] in the client. [dox] isolate <n> error: <error> An error killed a worker isolate. The stack is on the next line. Fix the error. Dox restarts the isolate. [dox] isolate <n> exited, restarting A worker isolate died. A new one starts after 1 second. Look at the error line above it. SocketException: Failed to create server socket (OS Error: Address already in use, ...) The port is in use (dart:io server). See Troubleshooting. SocketException: dox_http_native: bind failed (<code>), port = <port> The port is in use (native server). Same as above.

docs.title: dox_core: routes and controllers
docs.text:
These stop the app at start, so a bad route never reaches a request.

Text When What to do Route <where>: the controller parameter type <T> is not known. Use DoxRequest, a @Dto class, or String, int, double, num, bool for path params. ... A controller parameter has another type, or the DTO is not in AppConfig.dtos. Change the type, or run dart run build_runner build and set dtos: dtos. Route <where>: the controller has more path params than the route has {...} params (<n>). The method asks for more path params than the path has. Add the {param} to the path, or remove the parameter. Route <where>: a controller can have one @Dto only. Two DTO parameters. Merge them into one DTO. Route <where>: only positional parameters are supported, not named or [optional] ones (<type>). Named or [optional] parameters. Use positional parameters. Use int? with {id?} for an optional param. Route <where>: a controller can not be generic. The handler has type parameters. Remove them. Route <where>: can not read the controller type <type>. Dox can not read the function type of the handler. Use a plain method or function. Exception: websocket is not registered Route.websocket() runs before a WebsocketServer(Dox()) exists. Add the WebSocket service to services. See WebSocket.

docs.title: dox_core: env
docs.text:
Text When What to do EnvException: the env is not valid then - <KEY> is missing AppEnv.load() found a required key with no value. Set the key, or give the getter a default. - <KEY> must be <type>, not "<value>" A value does not fit the getter type. Fix the value. Check for a # comment after it. Env key "<KEY>" is not set and has no default Env.get<int>(), <num>, <double> or <bool> with no value and no default. Set the key, or pass a default. Env key "<KEY>" is not a valid <type>: "<value>" Env.get<int>() (or another type) got text that is not that type. Fix the value.

See Environment variables.

docs.title: dox_core: requests (what the client gets)
docs.text: Status Body text When What to do 404 <METHOD> <path> not found No route matches. Check the method, the path and the router prefix. 404 Not Found A typed path param does not fit, like abc for int id. Send a valid value. 400 The body is not valid JSON A DTO reads a JSON body that does not parse. Send valid JSON. 400 The form body is not valid A urlencoded body that can not be decoded. Fix the client encoding. 415 Unsupported Media Type A DTO reads a body that is not JSON or form data. Send Content-Type: application/json or form data. 413 Payload Too Large The body is bigger than maxBodySize or maxMultipartSize. Send less, or raise the limit. 422 {"_root":"The input has too many items (max 1000) or levels (max 10)"} Form or query keys with more than 1000 list items or 10 levels. Send less nested data. 422 {"<field>":"<message>"} A DTO check failed. See Validation rules. 431 (no text) Native server: request line plus headers over 16 KB. Send smaller headers or cookies. 500 <error>.toString() Any error that is not an IHttpException. It also goes to errorHandler. Look at the server log.

docs.title: dox_core: DTOs, storage and config
docs.text: Text When What to do Bad state: <T> is not a known DTO. Add @Dto() to it, rundart run build_runner buildand setdtos: dtos(lib/dtos.g.dart) in AppConfig. req.validate<T>() can not find T. Do what the text says. Invalid argument(s): Storage disk "<name>" has unknown driver "<type>" A disk in StorageConfig has a driver other than local, s3 or memory. Fix the driver name. type 'Null' is not a subtype of type 'String' in type cast An s3 disk without bucket, key or secret, on its first use. Set AWS_BUCKET, AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID and AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY. Invalid argument(s): invalid file Storage().put() with no extension:, and Dox can not find the type from the bytes. Pass extension: 'pdf'. 403 invalid or expired signature A Route.files() URL without a valid signature, or after expires. Make a new link with Storage().signedUrl(). 404 file not found Storage().stream() or download() of a missing file. Check the path. Invalid argument (trustedProxies): not an ip or cidr: "<value>" A bad entry in AppConfig.trustedProxies. Use an IP, a CIDR like 10.0.0.0/8, or *. Invalid argument (type): must be asc or desc: "<value>" orderBy(column, type) with another direction. Use asc or desc. AESEncryption Error: <error> AESEncryptor.decode got bad text or a wrong key, for example an old cookie after a new APP_KEY. It returns ''. Nothing, or ask the user to log in again.

docs.title: dox_auth
docs.text:
Text When What to do 401 Authentication failed AuthMiddleware finds no token, a bad or expired token, or the user is deleted. Send Authorization: Bearer <token>. Log in again. Invalid argument(s) (salt): Invalid salt length ... Hash.verify() with a value that is not a bcrypt hash. See Troubleshooting. Invalid argument(s) (password): Password is too long ... bcrypt with a password over 72 bytes. Limit the length in the DTO.

Auth().attempt() returns null for a wrong password. It does not throw. See Authentication.

docs.title: dox_orm
docs.text: Text When What to do [dox] warning: dox_postgres_native did not load, using the Dart postgres driver (<reason>) The native Postgres library did not load. See Postgres native. Or set DOX_DB_DRIVER=dart. [dox] warning: dox_mysql_native did not load, using the Dart mysql driver (<reason>) The native MySQL library did not load. See MySQL native. Exception: <name> not found DatabaseConfig.connection (or withConnection()) names a connection that is not in connections. Fix DB_CONNECTION or the map. Exception: Invalid driver or not supported A ConnectionConfig.driver Dox can not open. Use Driver.postgres, Driver.mysql or Driver.sqlite. Invalid argument(s): dox_postgres_native: bad connection config The native driver can not read the connection values. Check host, port, user, database. Invalid argument(s): dox_mysql_native: bad connection config Same, for MySQL. Same. SqliteException with unable to open database file The SQLite folder does not exist. See Troubleshooting.

docs.title: dox_orm: schema builder
docs.text: Text When What to do Bad state: foreign key <name>: call on(table) table.foreign('x').references('id') with no .on('table'). Add .on('table'), or use foreignId('x').constrained(). Unsupported operation: postgres: change() of an auto increment column is not supported change() on an id() or increments() column. Write the ALTER by hand with schema.driver.execute(). Unsupported operation: sqlite: can not add a primary key to an existing table primary(...) in schema.table() on SQLite. Make the table again with the key in schema.create(). Unsupported operation: sqlite: can not rebuild <table>, it has CHECK constraints A SQLite rebuild (change(), foreign(), dropForeign()) on a table with other CHECKs. Make the new table by hand in the migration. Unsupported operation: sqlite: can not rebuild <table>, it has generated columns Same, on a table with generated columns. Same. Bad state: sqlite: table <table> not found A SQLite rebuild of a missing table. Check the table name. Bad state: sqlite: column <table>.<column> not found change() or renameColumn() of a missing column on SQLite. Check the column name. Bad state: sqlite: foreign key <names> not found dropForeign() of a key the table does not have. Check the key name or columns. Bad state: sqlite: rebuild of <table> breaks foreign keys After the rebuild, rows point to missing parent rows. Fix the data first. Unsupported operation: sqlite: change() rebuilds the table, it only runs on a database table.toSql(SqliteGrammar()) with change(). Run it on a database, not as text.

docs.title: dox_migration
docs.text:
Text When What to do Exception: Could not connect to database: <error> The migrator can not open the database. Check DB_* values. A .env file wins over the real env here. See Troubleshooting. Unknown migration command: <cmd> (use run, rollback, reset, refresh or status) dart run bin/migrate.dart <cmd> with another command. Use one of the five. Invalid argument(s): Invalid option <x>, use --step=<count> rollback with a bad option. Use --step=2. Bad state: Migration <name> is both a Dart and a .sql migration Two files with the same name in db/migration. Rename or delete one. Bad state: foreign key check failed: <table> points to a missing <parent> row SQLite: a migration left a broken foreign key. Fix the data in the migration. Migrating: <name> / Migrated: <name> Normal progress. Nothing. Migrations are already up to date! Nothing to run. Nothing. Nothing to rollback! No batch to undo. Nothing. No migrations found. status with no migrations. Check db/migration.

See Migration.

docs.title: dox_cache
docs.text:
Text When What to do Invalid argument(s): Cache store "<name>" is not configured Cache().store('<name>') or defaultStore names a missing store. Add the store to CacheConfig.stores, or fix CACHE_STORE. Invalid argument(s): Cache driver "<driver>" of store "<name>" is not supported A store has a driver other than file, memory, redis or null. Fix the driver name. Unsupported operation: <Driver> does not support locks lock() on the file or null store. Use the memory or redis store. Bad state: Cache value of "<key>" is not an integer increment() or decrement() on a value that is not an int. Store an int, or forget() the key. Invalid argument(s): Cache value of "<key>" is bigger than <limit> bytes A Redis value is too big. Store less, or use files or a database. Bad state: RedisDriver.flush needs a prefix. It will not delete the whole database. flush() on a Redis store with an empty prefix. Set a prefix.

See Cache.

docs.title: dox_storage
docs.text:
The text has the form <Exception>: <message> (key: "<key>").

Text When What to do FileNotFoundException: File not found The file is not on the disk. Check the path. Storage() paths start with /, Disk keys do not. PermissionDeniedException: Permission denied The OS (local) or S3 (403) refused it. Check file rights, or the S3 key and bucket policy. InvalidKeyException: Invalid key: path traversal is not allowed A key with ... Do not build keys from user input. InvalidKeyException: Invalid key: absolute paths are not allowed A Disk key that starts with / or a drive letter. Remove the first /. InvalidKeyException: Invalid key: key is empty An empty key. Pass a file name. UnsupportedOperationException: urlBase is not configured Storage().url() on a local disk with no url option. Set url on the disk. UnsupportedOperationException: urlBase and appKey are needed for signed URLs signedUrl() on a local disk with no url, or no APP_KEY. Set both. UnsupportedOperationException: S3 signed URLs must expire within 1 second and 7 days signedUrl() on S3 with a bad expiresIn. Use a time up to 7 days. UnsupportedOperationException: Disk "<name>" is not registered Storage().disk('<name>') with a missing disk. Add the disk to StorageConfig.disks. DriverException: <S3 error> Any other S3 error (network, 500, wrong bucket). Read the S3 code in the text.

See File storage.

docs.text:
These stop dart run build_runner build.

Text When What to do The @Dto class <Name> has problems: then a - ... list One or more lines below. Fix each line. - The field <Class.field> must be final. A DTO field is not final. Add final. - The field <Class.field> must be athis.parameter of the unnamed constructor. The field is not set by the constructor. Add this.<field> to the constructor. - A @Dto class needs an unnamed constructor. Only named constructors. Add const Name({...}). - A @Dto class can not extend another class (<Parent>). The DTO extends a class. Copy the fields in. - A @Dto class can not be generic. The DTO has type parameters. Remove them. - The type <T> of <where> is not supported. Use a basic type, an enum, DateTime, RequestFile, a @Dto class, or a List or Map of them. Field type not supported. Change the type. - @<Rule> does not fit the type <T> of <where>. A rule on the wrong type, like @Email() on an int. Move the rule, or change the type. - @Length on <where> needs min:, max: or both. @Length() with no limit. Add min: or max:. - The @Regex on <where> is not a valid regex: <reason> The pattern does not compile. Fix the pattern. - @MaxSize on <where> needs a size like '2MB' (units B, KB, MB, GB), not "<text>". Bad size text. Use '2MB'. - The Maybe field <where> needs the defaultconst Maybe.missing(). A Maybe<T> field without that default. Add it. - <where> can not have both @Lowercase and @Uppercase. Both on one field. Keep one. - The validate method of <Name> must take one DtoErrors:void validate(DtoErrors errors). Wrong validate signature. Use that signature. Two @Dto classes are named <Name>: in <a> and <b>. Dox finds DTOs by name, so rename one. Two DTOs with the same class name. Rename one. Env getter "<name>" has type <T>. Use String, int, double, num, bool, Uri, Duration, an enum or List<String>. A @DoxEnv getter with another type. Change the type. @DoxModel can only be used on a class. / @DoxEnv can only be used on a class. The annotation is on something else. Put it on a class. docs.title: HTTP exceptions
docs.text:
An exception that extends IHttpException turns into an HTTP error answer. You can throw it or return it from a middleware or a controller.

IHttpException is in packages/dox-annotation/lib/src/core_annotation.dart:

abstract class IHttpException {
  int code = 500;
  String errorCode = 'server_error';
  dynamic message = 'Server Error';

  dynamic toResponse() {
    if (message is Map) {
      return message;
    }
    return message.toString();
  }
}

docs.title: The classes
docs.text:
Every class takes the named parameters message, errorCode and code. The table shows the defaults.

Class Package Status code errorCode Default message Dox throws it when BadRequestException dox_core 400 bad_request Bad Request the body can not be read, like JSON that is not valid UnAuthorizedException dox_auth 401 unauthorized Authentication failed AuthMiddleware finds no valid token NotFoundHttpException dox_core 404 not_found Not Found a typed path param does not fit ({id} is not an int) PayloadTooLargeException dox_core 413 payload_too_large Payload Too Large the body is bigger than maxBodySize or maxMultipartSize UnsupportedMediaTypeException dox_core 415 unsupported_media_type Unsupported Media Type a DTO reads a body that is not JSON and not form data ValidationException dox_core 422 validation_failed {} (a Map) a DTO or req.validate() finds bad input InternalErrorException dox_core 500 server_error Server Error never by itself; for your own use QueryException dox_core 500 sql_query_error Error in sql query never by itself; for your own use

Source files: packages/dox-core/lib/exception/*.dart and packages/dox-auth/lib/src/auth_exception.dart.

docs.title: What the client gets
docs.text:
responseDataHandler in packages/dox-core/lib/http/http_response_handler.dart sends the answer:

  1. The status is set to code.
  2. The body is toResponse().
  3. A Map body is sent as JSON with Content-Type: application/json.
  4. Any other body is sent as text, with the default text/plain content type.

So the default exceptions answer with plain text:

HTTP/1.1 404 Not Found
content-type: text/plain; charset=utf-8

Not Found

throw NotFoundHttpException(message: 'Blog not found');

HTTP/1.1 404 Not Found
content-type: text/plain; charset=utf-8

Blog not found

A Map message gives JSON. ValidationException always has a map, one entry per field:

HTTP/1.1 422 Unprocessable Entity
content-type: application/json

{"email":"The email is not a valid email","name":"The name is required"}

A request for a path that has no route is not an exception. Dox answers 404 with the text <METHOD> <path> not found.

To get a JSON body from any exception, pass a map:

throw NotFoundHttpException(
  message: <String, dynamic>{'error': 'not_found', 'message': 'Blog not found'},
);

errorCode is not sent

errorCode is stored on the exception, but toResponse() does not use it. The client only gets the status and the message. Put the code in a map message, or in a responseHandler, when the client needs it.

Other errors: any Exception or Error that is not an IHttpException gets 500 with error.toString() as text body. It is also passed to errorHandler in AppConfig. An IHttpException is not passed to errorHandler.

A ValidationException from dox_validation (thrown by schema.parse() in a controller) is turned into the 422 ValidationException of dox_core with the same errors.

docs.title: Make your own
docs.text:
Extend IHttpException and set the three fields in the constructor:

import 'dart:io';

import 'package:dox_core/dox_core.dart';

class ForbiddenException extends IHttpException {
  ForbiddenException({
    dynamic message = 'Forbidden',
    String errorCode = 'forbidden',
    int code = HttpStatus.forbidden,
  }) {
    super.code = code;
    super.errorCode = errorCode;
    super.message = message;
  }
}

Use it:

Future<dynamic> destroy(DoxRequest req, int id) async {
  if (req.auth?.user<User>()?.id != id) {
    throw ForbiddenException();
  }
}

Override toResponse() when every error of your app should have the same JSON shape:

class ApiException extends IHttpException {
  ApiException(int code, String errorCode, String message) {
    super.code = code;
    super.errorCode = errorCode;
    super.message = message;
  }

  @override
  dynamic toResponse() {
    return <String, dynamic>{'code': errorCode, 'message': message};
  }
}

More examples are on the Response page.

docs.title: Production checklist
docs.text:
Check each item before you deploy. Each item says what to check, how to do it, and where to read more.

Items marked Dox limit are things Dox does not do for you. You must handle them outside Dox.

docs.title: Secrets and config
docs.text: Check How Read more APP_KEY is set, long and secret dox key:generate, or a 32 character random value in the real env. It signs JWT tokens and encrypts cookies. Never use the value from .env.example. Encryption APP_ENV=production With it, an empty APP_KEY stops the app at start (StateError). Without it, Dox only logs a warning and runs with an empty key. Env reference The env is complete Run dox env:check in CI or before the deploy. It exits with code 1 when a key is missing or bad. CLI No secrets in the image or in git .env in .dockerignore and .gitignore. Pass values as env vars (docker run -e, env_file:, systemd EnvironmentFile=). dox build copies .env.example only. Docker No comments after values in .env KEY=abc # note gives the value abc # note. Put comments on their own line. Troubleshooting

docs.title: Auth and passwords
docs.text: Check How Read more JWT tokens expire Dox limit. JwtAuthDriver.expiresIn is null by default, so tokens never expire. Set it: JwtAuthDriver(secret: SecretKey(env.appKey), expiresIn: Duration(days: 7)). Authentication You can not revoke one token Dox limit. There is no token list on the server. To log out everyone, change APP_KEY. Authentication Passwords are hashed user.password = Hash.make(input) (bcrypt). Never store or encrypt a plain password. Hashing The hash is never sent List<String> get hidden => <String>['password']; in the user model. The JWT payload is user.toJson(), and anyone can read it. Authentication Passwords have a max length bcrypt throws on input over 72 bytes. Add @MaxLength(72) to the password field of the DTO. It counts characters, so non-ASCII text can still pass 72 bytes. Troubleshooting No sensitive data in AESEncryptor It uses a fixed IV and no MAC. It is fine for cookies, not for tokens or personal data. Encryption

docs.title: HTTP and network
docs.text: Check How Read more HTTPS at the proxy Dox has no TLS server. Run Caddy or nginx in front. Keep the app port private. Deployment trustedProxies is set behind a proxy AppConfig(trustedProxies: <String>['127.0.0.1', '::1']), or the proxy network, like '172.16.0.0/12'. Without it, req.ip() is the proxy and req.scheme() is http. Do not use ['*'] when the app port is public. App config Body limits are on Keep maxBodySize (10 MB) and maxMultipartSize (100 MB), or lower them. Set the same limit in the proxy: client_max_body_size 100m; Request CORS has one real origin CORSConfig(origin: 'https://my.app'). Dox limit: a list is joined into one header (https://a.com,https://b.com), and browsers reject it. Dox does not compare the list with the request Origin. For many origins, set the header in the proxy. CORS No credentials: true with origin: '*' The new project's cors.dart has origin: '*' and credentials: true with enabled: false. When you turn CORS on, set a real origin first. CORS Rate limiting Dox limit. Dox has no rate limiter. Do it at the proxy. See below. Deployment gzip at the proxy Keep compress: false. Turn on gzip in Caddy (encode gzip) or nginx (gzip on;). Performance OpenAPI docs Off in production by default (on only for APP_ENV development or local). Do not set enabled: true for a private API. OpenAPI

docs.title: Build and run
docs.text: Check How Read more AOT binary, not dart run dox build, then run build/bundle/bin/server. Keep bin/ and lib/ together. Not dart compile exe. Deployment Native server is on The start line says (native). When it says (dart:io), look for the [dox] warning: dox_http_native did not load line. Native server Native database driver is on No [dox] warning: dox_postgres_native did not load (or mysql) line at start. Do not set DOX_DB_DRIVER=dart. Postgres with TLS uses the Dart driver. Postgres native Isolates = cores Keep the default totalIsolate (Platform.numberOfProcessors), or set APP_TOTAL_ISOLATE to the cores the container really gets. Use fewer when the database runs on the same machine. Isolate Shared state across isolates Cache: redis, not memory. WebSocket: WebsocketRedisAdapter. Socket.IO: a Redis adapter and transports: ['websocket']. Isolate A supervisor restarts the process Docker restart: unless-stopped, or systemd Restart=always. Dox restarts a dead worker isolate, but not the main isolate. Deployment Writable temp folder Uploads over 1 MB go to a temp file. A FROM scratch image needs /tmp with mode 1777. Docker Uploads live on a volume or S3 The local disk writes to storage/. Mount it as a volume, or use the s3 disk. File storage

docs.title: Database
docs.text: Check How Read more Postgres or MySQL for a busy app SQLite has one connection per isolate, and a query blocks the isolate. Use it for small apps only. With SQLite use an absolute file path, never :memory: with many isolates. Database Migrations run once per deploy The new project runs Migrator(migrations: migrations).migrate() in bin/server.dart before startServer(). Or run dart run bin/migrate.dart run (or dox migrate) in CI. Do one, not both at the same time on many machines. Migration Migrations use the right database dox_migration reads .env when the file exists, and ignores the real env then. Do not ship a .env next to the binary, or give Migrator(connection: ...) your own pool. Troubleshooting Small MySQL migrations MySQL saves CREATE, ALTER and DROP at once. A failed migration can leave half the changes. One table change per migration. Migration Pool size fits the database extra: {'maxConnectionCount': 10} is per isolate. Total = isolates x pool size. Keep it under the database max_connections. Database Query logging is off The new project's database.dart has debug: true on every connection, which prints every query. Set debug: false in production. Database Backups Dox limit. Dox has no backup tool. Use pg_dump, mysqldump, managed database snapshots, or a copy of the SQLite file (with the -wal file, or sqlite3 app.db ".backup x.db"). Test a restore.

docs.title: Logs and errors
docs.text: Check How Read more JSON logs LoggerConfig(enabled: true, prettyPrint: false). The new project sets prettyPrint only when APP_ENV=development. App config Log level Dox limit. LoggerConfig.level is stored but not read. Every level is printed. App config Access logs in one place LogMiddleware writes one line per request, every 20 ms. A hard kill can lose the last lines. Turn it off when the proxy already logs requests. Performance Errors go to your tracker Set AppConfig.errorHandler. Any non-HTTP error is passed to it. The client gets 500 with the error text, so do not put secrets in exception messages. HTTP exceptions

docs.title: Health and shutdown
docs.text: Check How Read more Health route Dox limit. Dox has no built-in health route. Add one that asks the database: Route.get('/health', healthController.check) with await QueryBuilder.query('select 1');. Docker Graceful shutdown Dox limit. Dox does not listen for SIGTERM. On stop, open requests are cut. Dox().server.close() closes the server of the main isolate only. Take the instance out of the proxy first, wait a few seconds, then stop it. Deployment Zero downtime deploys Run two processes (or machines) behind the proxy. Restart one at a time. Deployment

docs.title: Rate limit at the proxy
docs.text:
Dox has no rate limiter. Add one in the proxy.

nginx:

# in http { }
limit_req_zone $binary_remote_addr zone=api:10m rate=10r/s;

# in server { location / { } }
limit_req zone=api burst=20 nodelay;
limit_req_status 429;

Caddy needs the caddy-ratelimit plugin (build Caddy with xcaddy build --with github.com/mholt/caddy-ratelimit):

example.com {
  rate_limit {
    zone api {
      key    {remote_host}
      events 100
      window 1m
    }
  }
  reverse_proxy 127.0.0.1:3000
}

Note

The proxy must see the real client IP. When there is a load balancer in front of the proxy, set the real IP module of the proxy first.

docs.title: Request and response
docs.text: A compact list of the members. Examples and explanations are on the Request and Response pages.

docs.title: DoxRequest
docs.text: Source: packages/dox-core/lib/http/request/dox_request.dart. It implements IDoxRequest from dox_annotation. A middleware gets an IDoxRequest. A controller gets a DoxRequest. The members marked IDoxRequest are on both.

docs.title: Input
docs.text: Member Returns What it gives On IDoxRequest validate<T>({Source? source}) Future<T> The request checked with the DTO T. Throws the 422 ValidationException on bad input. Throws StateError when T is not in AppConfig.dtos. no validateSchema<O>(Schema<O> schema) Future<O> Query and body checked with a fluent dox_validation schema. no all() Map<String, dynamic> Query and body together. Body wins on the same key. yes only(List<String> keys) Map<String, dynamic> Only these keys from all(). A missing key gives null. yes input(String key) dynamic One value from all(). yes has(String key) bool true when the key is there and its text is not empty. yes add(String key, dynamic value) void Adds a value to all() and body. yes merge(Map<String, dynamic> values) void Adds many values to all() and body. yes body Map<String, dynamic> The parsed body (JSON or form fields). Files are RequestFile. no query Map<String, dynamic> The query string. no param Map<String, dynamic> The route params, like {'id': '5'}. no pathParams Map<String, String> The route params as text. null values are left out. no requestBody RequestBody The body as it was read, for DTOs. no isJson() bool The content type is JSON. yes isFormData() bool The content type is form data (multipart/form-data or urlencoded). yes toJson() Map<String, dynamic> all() with files replaced by their file name. Lets jsonEncode(req) work. yes

Many values of one name are joined. yes httpHeaders HttpHeaders The dart:io headers object. no contentType ContentType? The parsed Content-Type. yes cookie(String key, {bool decrypt = true}) String? One cookie. Decrypted with appKey unless decrypt: false. yes ip() String The client IP, or unknown. From X-Forwarded-For only behind a trusted proxy. yes scheme() String http or https. From X-Forwarded-Proto only behind a trusted proxy. no isSecure() bool scheme() is https. no clientIp String? The client IP, or null. no userAgent() String The User-Agent header, or unknown. yes host() String The Host header, or unknown. yes origin() String? The Origin header. yes referer() String? The Referer header. yes locale String? The first language of Accept-Language, like th. null when there is none or it is *. no auth IAuth? The auth object set by AuthMiddleware, or null. yes

docs.title: Route and raw request
docs.text: Member Returns What it gives On IDoxRequest method String The HTTP method in upper case. yes uri Uri The request URI. yes route RouteData The matched route. no getRouteData() RouteData Same as route. yes getRouteIdentifier() String base64 of <method>|<domain><path>. Useful as a cache or rate limit key. yes httpRequest HttpRequest The dart:io request. Use it for raw access. yes

docs.title: DoxResponse
docs.text:
Source: packages/dox-core/lib/http/response/dox_response.dart. Every setter returns the same DoxResponse, so calls chain.

Member Returns What it does DoxResponse(dynamic content) DoxResponse The constructor. content can be a String, number, Map, List, a JSON serializable object, a Stream<List<int>>, a File, a StreamFile or a DownloadableFile. response([dynamic content]) DoxResponse Top level helper. Same as DoxResponse(content). statusCode(int code) DoxResponse Sets the status. Default 200. content(dynamic content) DoxResponse Replaces the content. getContent() dynamic The content as it was given. stream(Stream<List<int>> stream) DoxResponse Sets a byte stream as content. contentType(ContentType type) DoxResponse Sets Content-Type. A File without it gets the type from its extension. header(String key, dynamic value) DoxResponse Adds one header. withHeaders(Map<String, dynamic> values) DoxResponse Replaces every header set so far with this map. cookie(DoxCookie cookie, {bool setExpire = false}) DoxResponse Adds a Set-Cookie header. setExpire: true sends the cookie as expired, which removes it. cache(Duration duration) DoxResponse Sets Cache-Control: max-age=<seconds>. process(HttpRequest request) dynamic Internal. Writes headers, status, cookies and the body.

How the content is sent (responseDataHandler in packages/dox-core/lib/http/http_response_handler.dart):

Content Sent as null an empty body String text, as it is Map, List, number, bool, object with toJson() JSON, Content-Type: application/json DateTime its ISO 8601 text File streamed, with Content-Length, Accept-Ranges and one Range supported StreamFile streamed with its content type DownloadableFile streamed with Content-Disposition: attachment Stream<List<int>> streamed chunk by chunk IHttpException its status and toResponse(), see HTTP exceptions other Exception or Error 500 with toString() as text

A plain value returned from a controller (not a DoxResponse) is sent the same way. It only goes through a DoxResponse when AppConfig.responseHandler is set, or when it is a File, StreamFile or DownloadableFile.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Real problems, with the text you see, the cause and the fix. The texts come from the source code.

docs.title: The native HTTP library did not load
docs.text:
Symptom. One line at start, on stderr:

[dox] warning: dox_http_native did not load, using the dart:io server (<reason>)

and the start line says (dart:io) instead of (native):

Server started at http://127.0.0.1:3000 with 8 isolate (dart:io)

At build time (dart pub get, dox serve or dox build) you may also see one of these:

dox_http_native: no native library for <os>-<arch>. Dox will use dart:io.
dox_http_native: download dox_http_native-<os>-<arch>.<ext>: 404
dox_http_native: download dox_http_native-<os>-<arch>.<ext> failed: <error>
dox_http_native: sha256 of dox_http_native-<os>-<arch>.<ext> does not match
dox_http_native: cargo build failed

Cause. The build hook of dox_http_native (packages/dox-http-native/hook/build.dart) tries, in this order: the lib_path user define, a local native/target/release build, the GitHub release download, and cargo build. None worked. Common reasons:

  • No internet during dart pub get, or the release has no build for your OS and CPU (there are builds for macOS arm64 and x64, Linux x64 and arm64, Windows x64).
  • Rust is not installed, so the fallback cargo build can not run.
  • You compiled with dart compile exe. It does not run build hooks, so no native library is in the binary.
  • The <reason> is native library ABI <x>, expected <y>: the library on disk is from another version of the package.

Fix. Pick one:

  1. Accept dart:io. The app works, only slower. To hide the warning set DOX_SERVER=dartio or server: ServerBackend.dartIo in AppConfig.
  2. Install Rust with rustup and run dart pub get again. The hook builds the library with cargo.

  3. Download the library from the GitHub release dox_http_native-v<version> yourself and point to it in the root pubspec.yaml:

    hooks:
  user_defines:
    dox_http_native:
      lib_path: /path/to/libdox_http_native.so

  4. Build with dox build (it runs dart build cli), not with dart compile exe.

The same applies to the native database drivers. The warning is then:

[dox] warning: dox_postgres_native did not load, using the Dart postgres driver (<reason>)
[dox] warning: dox_mysql_native did not load, using the Dart mysql driver (<reason>)

The Dart driver is used. To choose it on purpose set DOX_DB_DRIVER=dart or extra: {'native': false} on the connection.

See Native server, Postgres native and MySQL native.

docs.title: Port already in use
docs.text:
Symptom. With the dart:io server:

SocketException: Failed to create server socket (OS Error: Address already in use, errno = 48), address = ::, port = 3000

(errno = 48 on macOS, errno = 98 on Linux.) With the native server:

SocketException: dox_http_native: bind failed (<code>), port = 3000

Cause. Another process listens on the port. Often it is an old bin/server.dart that dox serve did not stop, or a second copy of the app.

Fix. Find and stop the process, or use another port.

lsof -i :3000          # macOS and Linux: who has the port
kill <pid>

Or set APP_PORT=3001 in .env (a new project reads it into serverPort).

docs.title: build_runner: conflicting outputs
docs.text:
Symptom. dox build_runner:build, dox serve or dox build stops with a build_runner message that starts with Conflicting outputs were detected, and names files like lib/dtos.g.dart or lib/app/models/user/user.model.g.dart.

Cause. The generated .g.dart files are on disk, but .dart_tool/build does not know them. This happens after a git clone with committed .g.dart files, after deleting .dart_tool, or after a Dart SDK update.

Fix. Delete the build cache and build again:

rm -rf .dart_tool/build
dart run build_runner build

If that is not enough, delete the named .g.dart files and build again. Older build_runner versions accept dart run build_runner build --delete-conflicting-outputs. Newer versions removed that flag, so the Dox CLI does not pass it.

docs.title: dox create throws RangeError
docs.text:
Symptom.

dox create my_app
RangeError (index): Invalid value: Only valid value is 0: 1

Cause. A bug in the dox CLI up to 3.0.0-alpha.4: the create command read the --version flag before it checked that one was given. The same versions also downloaded an old project template.

Fix. Update the CLI. The fix is in the version after 3.0.0-alpha.4:

dart pub global activate dox

Until then, pass the version by hand:

dox create my_app --version 3.0.0-alpha.4

docs.title: Migrations read .env instead of the real environment
docs.text:
Symptom. dox migration:run (or dart run bin/migrate.dart run) in Docker or CI fails with

Exception: Could not connect to database: <driver error>

and the host, user or database in the error are the ones from your .env, not the ones you set in the environment.

Cause. dox_migration has its own env loader (packages/dox-migration/lib/src/utils/env.dart). When a .env file exists in the current folder, it reads only that file. The real environment is used only when there is no .env. This is the opposite of Env.get() in dox_core, where the real environment wins.

Fix. Pick one:

  • Do not ship a .env to the server. dox build copies .env.example, not .env. Set real env vars and leave .env out.
  • Put the right values in the .env of the server.

  • Open the connection yourself and give it to the migrator in bin/migrate.dart:

    exitCode = await Migrator(
  migrations: migrations,
  connection: myPostgresPool,
).run(args);

The keys it reads are DB_CONNECTION, DB_HOST, DB_PORT, DB_USERNAME, DB_PASSWORD and DB_DATABASE (or DB_NAME). See Environment variables.

docs.title: A .env value with #
docs.text:
Symptom. The app stops at start with

EnvException: the env is not valid
  - APP_PORT must be an int, not "3000 # dev"

or, with Env.get:

Invalid argument(s): Env key "APP_PORT" is not a valid int: "3000 # dev"

Or a text value is longer than you expect, like a password with # prod at the end.

Cause. The .env parser (packages/dox-core/lib/env/env.dart) does not treat # as a comment. Everything after the first = is the value. Only ", ' and ` are removed.

Fix. Put comments on their own line:

# the dev port
APP_PORT=3000

A value that must contain # (a password, a URL fragment) works as it is. Do not quote it, the quotes are removed anyway.

docs.title: Hash.verify throws on a bad hash
docs.text:
Symptom.

Invalid argument(s) (salt): Invalid salt length (The length should be greater than or equal to 28): "..."

or

Invalid argument(s) (salt): Invalid salt version: "..."

or, when the password is long:

Invalid argument(s) (password): Password is too long (The length should be less than or equal to 72): "..."

Cause. Hash.verify(password, hash) calls BCrypt.checkpw from the bcrypt package. It throws an ArgumentError when hash is not a bcrypt hash (it must start with $2 and be at least 28 characters), for example when the column holds a plain password, an empty string or a hash from another algorithm. It also throws when the password is longer than 72 bytes.

Fix.

  • Make sure every stored password went through Hash.make(). A plain password in the column is a bug in the code that saved it.

  • Check the hash before you compare it, and treat a bad one as a failed login:

    bool ok = hash.startsWith(r'$2') && Hash.verify(password, hash);

  • Refuse passwords longer than 72 bytes in your DTO, for example @Length(max: 72).

For normal login use Auth().attempt() from dox_auth. See Hashing.

docs.title: MySQL 8 login fails
docs.text:
Symptom. The connection to MySQL 8 is refused at login, while the same user works from the mysql client. Often the user was made with the default caching_sha2_password plugin.

Cause. caching_sha2_password needs either TLS or the server RSA public key to send the password. A client that has neither can not log in.

Fix. Both Dox drivers handle this by default:

  • The native driver (dox_mysql_native) works with MySQL 8.4 caching_sha2_password and MariaDB 11.
  • The Dart driver asks the server for its RSA key (allowPublicKeyRetrieval is true by default), so it works without TLS. Migrations do the same.

So check these settings on the connection in lib/config/database.dart:

Setting What to do extra: {'allowPublicKeyRetrieval': false} Remove it, or give the key in extra: {'serverPublicKey': '...'}. useSSL: true The server must have TLS on. host, port, user, password A wrong value gives the same login error. DB_PORT is 3306 by default for MySQL.

As a last resort, change the user on the server:

ALTER USER 'app'@'%' IDENTIFIED WITH mysql_native_password BY 'secret';

docs.title: SQLite: the database file
docs.text:
Symptom. An SqliteException with unable to open database file, or an empty database after dox build.

Cause. database is a file path. A relative path is relative to the folder you start the app from. dox build tells you to run cd build/bundle && ./bin/server, so dox.sqlite is then build/bundle/dox.sqlite. SQLite makes a missing file, but not a missing folder.

Fix.

  • Use an absolute path, or make the folder first.
  • Set it with DB_NAME (a new project reads it): DB_NAME=/var/lib/my_app/dox.sqlite.
  • Migrations use DB_DATABASE or DB_NAME as the path too. Use the same value for both.

:memory: and isolates

:memory: opens a new empty database in each isolate. With totalIsolate above 1, every isolate sees different data. Use a file, or totalIsolate: 1.

Dox opens a file database with journal_mode = WAL, synchronous = NORMAL, foreign_keys = ON and busy_timeout = 5000 (change it with extra: {'busyTimeout': ...}).

docs.title: dox: command not found after dart pub global activate
docs.text:
Symptom.

zsh: command not found: dox

right after dart pub global activate dox 3.0.0-alpha.4.

Cause. dart pub global activate puts the dox script in $HOME/.pub-cache/bin. That folder is not in your PATH.

Fix. Add it to your shell profile and open a new terminal:

export PATH="$PATH":"$HOME/.pub-cache/bin"

On Windows the folder is %LOCALAPPDATA%\Pub\Cache\bin.

docs.title: Other startup errors
docs.text: Text Cause Fix APP_KEY is not set. Rundox key:generateand put the key in .env appKey is empty. A warning in development, a StateError that stops the app when APP_ENV=production. Run dox key:generate, or set APP_KEY in the environment. Env key "<KEY>" is not set and has no default Env.get<int>(), <num>, <double> or <bool> with no value and no default. Set the key, or pass a default. <T> is not a known DTO. Add @Dto() to it, rundart run build_runner buildand setdtos: dtos(lib/dtos.g.dart) in AppConfig. req.validate<T>() can not find the DTO. Do what the text says. Route <METHOD> <path>: the controller parameter type <T> is not known. ... A controller parameter is not DoxRequest, a DTO, or String, int, double, num, bool. Change the type, or add the DTO to AppConfig.dtos. Route <METHOD> <path>: a controller can have one @Dto only. Two DTO parameters on one controller. Merge them into one DTO. Route <METHOD> <path>: only positional parameters are supported, not named or [optional] ones The controller has named or [optional] parameters. Use positional parameters. db/migration has Dart migrations, but bin/migrate.dart is missing. dox migration:* found Dart migration files but no entry point. Run dox make:migration <name> once. It writes bin/migrate.dart. <name> not found (an Exception from DatabaseConfig) DatabaseConfig.connection names a key that is not in connections. Fix DB_CONNECTION or the map. Storage disk "<name>" has unknown driver "<type>" A disk in StorageConfig has a driver other than local, s3 or memory. Fix the driver name. Windows: the native server runs on one isolate Windows has no SO_REUSEPORT. Not an error. Use DOX_SERVER=dartio to use every core on Windows. WebSocket or Socket.IO routes: using the dart:io server The native server can not upgrade to WebSocket yet. Not an error. DOX_SERVER=native forces native, then WebSocket upgrades fail with 500.

docs.title: Authentication
docs.text:
This page shows how to log users in with dox_auth and protect routes with a JWT token.

dox_auth checks an email and a password against your user table. It gives back a JWT token. The client sends this token in the Authorization header. AuthMiddleware reads the token and loads the user from the database.

docs.title: Install
docs.text:
dart pub add dox_auth

A new app made with the dox CLI already has it.

docs.title: 1. Hide the password in the model
docs.text:
The token holds the user data as JSON, and anyone can read a JWT. So the password hash must never be in toJson(). Put it in hidden:

lib/app/models/user/user.model.dart
import 'package:dox_orm/dox_orm.dart';

part 'user.model.g.dart';

@DoxModel(table: 'users')
class User extends UserGenerator {
  @override
  List<String> get hidden => <String>['password'];

  @Column()
  String? name;

  @Column()
  String? email;

  @Column()
  String? password;
}

docs.title: 2. Set up the auth service
3. Add the routes
docs.text:
AuthMiddleware protects a route. When the token is missing or not valid, the request stops with 401 Authentication failed.

lib/routes/api.dart
AuthController authController = AuthController();

Route.post('/auth/register', authController.register);
Route.post('/auth/login', authController.login);
Route.get('/auth/user', <dynamic>[AuthMiddleware(), authController.user]);

docs.title: 4. Write the controller
5. Send the token from the client
docs.text:
GET /auth/user
Authorization: Bearer <token>

docs.title: Read the user
docs.text:
After AuthMiddleware, req.auth holds the login.

Code What it gives req.auth an IAuth?. null when the route has no AuthMiddleware req.auth?.isLoggedIn() true when a user is loaded req.auth?.user<User>() the user model req.auth?.toJson() the user as a map, without hidden fields

docs.title: The Auth class
docs.text:
Method What it does Auth.initialize(AuthConfig) sets the config. Call it once, in a service await Auth().attempt(credentials) finds the user and checks the password. Gives a token, or null Auth().login(user) gives a token for this user, with no password check user<T>() the user after attempt or login isLoggedIn() true when there is a user

attempt searches only by the fields in identifierFields. It returns null when the password is not a String, when no identifier is given, or when the password does not match.

docs.title: AuthProvider
docs.text: Option Default What it does model required a function that makes a new model, like () => User() identifierFields ['email'] the fields attempt searches by passwordField 'password' the column with the bcrypt hash

docs.title: JwtAuthDriver
docs.text: Option Default What it does secret required the key that signs tokens, like SecretKey(env.appKey) algorithm JWTAlgorithm.HS256 the signing algorithm expiresIn null how long a token is valid. null means it never expires issuer null the iss claim

docs.title: Things to know
docs.text:
Set expiresIn

Without expiresIn, a token never expires. A stolen token then works forever. Set a duration, for example Duration(days: 7).

  • The token is not secret. Its payload is user.toJson(). Anyone with the token can read it. Keep private columns in hidden.
  • You can not cancel one token. There is no token list on the server. A token works until it expires. If you change the secret (your APP_KEY), all tokens stop working.
  • Only the default guard is used. Auth() and AuthMiddleware always use defaultGuard. Other guards in guards are not read.
  • The user is loaded on each request. AuthMiddleware reads the user id from the token and runs find(id). A deleted user can not log in, even with a valid token.
  • Hash passwords with Hash.make() before you save them. See Hashing.

docs.title: CORS
docs.text:
This page shows how to let a web page on another domain call your API.

A browser blocks a request from https://my.app to https://api.my.app by default. The API must send CORS headers to allow it. Dox adds these headers from CORSConfig.

docs.title: Set up
docs.text:
The config is in lib/config/cors.dart. Pass it to AppConfig(cors: cors).

lib/config/cors.dart
import 'package:dox_core/dox_core.dart';

CORSConfig cors = CORSConfig(
  enabled: true,
  origin: 'https://my.app',
  methods: <String>['GET', 'POST', 'PUT', 'PATCH', 'DELETE'],
  headers: <String>['Content-Type', 'Authorization'],
  exposeHeaders: <String>['Content-Disposition'],
  credentials: true,
  maxAge: 600,
);
lib/config/app.dart
AppConfig appConfig = AppConfig(
  cors: cors,
  // ...
);

docs.title: Options
docs.text:
Each option sets one response header. An option that is null sends no header.

Option Header Value enabled - true adds the headers to every route. Default: true origin Access-Control-Allow-Origin one origin, or '*' for all methods Access-Control-Allow-Methods a List<String> or a text like 'GET,POST'. '*' allows all headers Access-Control-Allow-Headers a List<String> or a text. '*' allows all exposeHeaders Access-Control-Expose-Headers the response headers the page may read credentials Access-Control-Allow-Credentials true lets the browser send cookies maxAge Access-Control-Max-Age how many seconds the browser keeps the preflight answer

A list is joined with commas. The value is sent as it is. Dox does not compare it with the Origin of the request.

One origin only

Access-Control-Allow-Origin accepts one origin or *. If you set a list like ['https://a.com', 'https://b.com'], Dox sends https://a.com,https://b.com. Browsers reject this value. So set one origin, or '*'.

credentials with *

Browsers do not send cookies when origin is '*'. When you need cookies, set origin to your real front-end URL.

docs.title: Preflight requests
docs.text: Before some requests, the browser sends an OPTIONS request. You do not need an OPTIONS route for this. Dox answers it with 204 No Content and the CORS headers. It uses the CORS setting of the route that the browser asks about.

docs.title: Turn CORS on or off for some routes
docs.text:
enabled is the default for all routes. Change it for a group of routes:

lib/routes/api.dart
// CORS headers only on these routes (use with enabled: false)
Route.enabledCors(() {
  Route.get('/public/posts', postController.index);
});

// no CORS headers on these routes
Route.disabledCors(() {
  Route.post('/webhooks/stripe', webhookController.handle);
});

docs.title: Encryption
docs.text:
This page shows how to encrypt and decrypt text with AESEncryptor.

Dox uses AESEncryptor to encrypt cookies with your APP_KEY. You can also call it yourself.

docs.title: Encrypt and decrypt
docs.text:
AESEncryptor is not exported by package:dox_core/dox_core.dart. Import it from its own file.

import 'package:dox_core/utils/aes_encryptor.dart';

String secret = env.appKey; // 32 characters

String encoded = AESEncryptor.encode('Hello world', secret);
String decoded = AESEncryptor.decode(encoded, secret); // 'Hello world'
  • encode returns base64 text.
  • decode returns an empty string '' when the text or the key is wrong. It does not throw.
  • The secret must be 16, 24 or 32 bytes long (AES-128, AES-192 or AES-256). Another length makes encode throw.

Make a new 32-character APP_KEY with the CLI:

dox key:generate

docs.title: Cookies
docs.text:
DoxCookie encrypts its value with APP_KEY by default. req.cookie(key) decrypts it.

return response().cookie(DoxCookie('theme', 'dark'));  // encrypted
DoxCookie('theme', 'dark', encrypt: false);             // plain text

String? theme = req.cookie('theme');                    // decrypted
String? raw = req.cookie('theme', decrypt: false);      // as sent

If you change APP_KEY, old encrypted cookies read as ''.

docs.title: Limits
docs.text:
Do not use it for sensitive data

AESEncryptor uses AES in CTR mode with a fixed IV (all zeros). It has no message check (no MAC).

  • The same text with the same key always gives the same output. So a reader can see when two values are equal.
  • Someone can change the encrypted text, and decode does not notice.

This keeps old cookies working. But it is not safe for passwords, tokens or personal data. For those, use a library with an authenticated mode, like AES-GCM with a random nonce for each message.

To store passwords, do not encrypt them. Hash them. See Hashing.

docs.title: Hashing
docs.text:
This page shows how to hash passwords with Hash and check them later.

A hash is one-way. You can not turn it back into the password. To check a login, hash the new input and compare. Hash.verify does this for you. Hash uses bcrypt with a new random salt each time.

Hash is in package:dox_core/dox_core.dart.

docs.title: Hash a password
docs.text:
Hash the password before you save it.

user.password = Hash.make(body.password);
await user.save();

The result looks like $2a$10$.... It holds the salt, so you only store this one string. The same password gives a different hash each time.

docs.title: Check a password
docs.text:
bool ok = Hash.verify('secret', user.password!);

Hash.verify(password, hashedPassword) returns true when the password matches.

Warning

Hash.verify from dox_core throws when hashedPassword is not a valid bcrypt hash, for example an empty string. Check that the value is a real hash first, or catch the error.

docs.title: With login
docs.text: You do not need Hash.verify for normal login. Auth().attempt() from dox_auth finds the user and checks the password with bcrypt. See Authentication.

docs.title: Things to know
docs.text:
• Never store a plain password. Never encrypt a password. Hash it.
  • Never send the hash to the client. Put the column in the model hidden list.
  • bcrypt is slow on purpose. This makes guessing many passwords slow too. Do not hash in a loop on hot paths.

docs.title: Controller
docs.text: A controller holds the code that answers a route. It can be a class method, a static method or a plain function.

docs.title: Class based controller
docs.text:
Make one with the CLI:

dox create:controller Blog

It writes lib/app/http/controllers/blog.controller.dart.

lib/app/http/controllers/blog.controller.dart
import 'package:dox_core/dox_core.dart';

class BlogController {
  String index(DoxRequest req) {
    return 'all blogs';
  }
}
lib/routes/api.dart
BlogController blogController = BlogController();
Route.get('/blogs', blogController.index);

docs.title: Static method
docs.text:
class AppController {
  static String ping(DoxRequest req) {
    return 'pong';
  }
}

Route.get('/ping', AppController.ping);

docs.title: Function based controller
docs.text:
String listBlog(DoxRequest req) {
  return 'all blogs';
}

Route.get('/blogs', listBlog);

docs.title: Resource controller
docs.text:
A resource controller has the 7 methods that Route.resource uses.

Make one with the CLI:

dox create:controller Blog -r
lib/app/http/controllers/blog.controller.dart
import 'package:dox_core/dox_core.dart';

class BlogController {
  /// GET /resource
  Future<dynamic> index(DoxRequest req) async {}

  /// GET /resource/create
  Future<dynamic> create(DoxRequest req) async {}

  /// POST /resource
  Future<dynamic> store(DoxRequest req) async {}

  /// GET /resource/{id}
  Future<dynamic> show(DoxRequest req, int id) async {}

  /// GET /resource/{id}/edit
  Future<dynamic> edit(DoxRequest req, int id) async {}

  /// PUT|PATCH /resource/{id}
  Future<dynamic> update(DoxRequest req, int id) async {}

  /// DELETE /resource/{id}
  Future<dynamic> destroy(DoxRequest req, int id) async {}
}
lib/routes/api.dart
Route.resource('blogs', BlogController());

You can delete methods you do not need. Route.resource skips them. See Routing: resource routes.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text:
A controller asks for what it needs by type. Dox fills each parameter.
