Route.put('/teams/{teamId}/users/{id}', controller.update);

class UserController {
  Future<User> update(int teamId, int id, UpdateUser body) async { ... }
}
Parameter type Dox gives DoxRequest the request a @Dto class the checked body or query. See Validation. String, int, double, num, bool the path params, in the order of the route the same types with ? an optional path param ({id?}). null when it is not in the URL.

Rules:

  • The order of parameters is free. Path params are matched by position: the first path-param parameter gets the first {...} in the route.
  • DoxRequest is not needed. Add it only when you use it.
  • At most one @Dto parameter.
  • Only positional parameters. Named and [optional] parameters are not supported.
  • A catch-all {path*} param is a String.
  • The same rules work for static methods and plain functions.

Path param types. Dox converts the text from the URL:

  • int: "42" is 42. "abc" or "4.5" answers 404 Not Found.
  • double, num: "4.5" is 4.5.
  • bool: true or 1 is true. false or 0 is false.
  • Any other text answers 404 too.
  • Path params are checked first. When one is wrong, the DTO is not checked.

Checked at start. The server does not start when:

  • a parameter type is not in the list above, and not a @Dto (did you run dart run build_runner build?),
  • the method has more path-param parameters than the route has {...} params.

Why types, not names?

Dox reads the parameter types of your method once, when the routes are registered at start. It needs no dart:mirrors. So update(int teamId, int id) works by position, not by the names teamId and id.

docs.title: What to return
docs.text: Return a String, a Map, a model, a File and more. See Response.

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
This page shows how to install the Dox CLI, make a new project and start the server.

3.x is alpha

The latest version is 3.0.0-alpha.4. It needs Dart 3.13 or newer.

docs.title: Install the CLI
docs.text:
dart pub global activate dox 3.0.0-alpha.4

Check that it works:

dox version

dox: command not found

The shell can not find the CLI when the pub bin folder is not in your PATH. Add this line to ~/.bashrc or ~/.zshrc, then open a new terminal:

export PATH="$PATH":"$HOME/.pub-cache/bin"

docs.title: Create a new project
docs.text:
dox create new_blog

dox create downloads the newest 3.x release of dox-sample, the starter project. To get one exact version, add --version:

dox create new_blog --version 3.0.0-alpha.4

Then get the packages and make your .env file:

cd new_blog
dart pub get
cp .env.example .env

The starter project uses SQLite, so there is no database to install. The file db/dox.sqlite is created at the first start. To use Postgres or MySQL instead, change DB_CONNECTION and the DB_* values in .env. See Database.

Add Dox to an existing Dart project

Add the packages you need to pubspec.yaml. All Dox packages share one version, so use ^3.0.0-alpha.4 for each of them.

pubspec.yaml
dependencies:
  dox_core: ^3.0.0-alpha.4
  dox_orm: ^3.0.0-alpha.4
  dox_migration: ^3.0.0-alpha.4

dev_dependencies:
  dox_builder: ^3.0.0-alpha.4
  build_runner: ^2.17.1

docs.title: Start the server
docs.text:
dox s

dox s does two things:

  • It runs dart run build_runner watch, so generated files stay up to date.
  • It runs dart run bin/server.dart, and restarts it when a .dart file changes.

To skip the builder, use dox s --ignore-build-runner. To start the server without the CLI, run dart run bin/server.dart.

At the first start it also runs the migrations in db/migration. The server uses the port in APP_PORT in the .env file (3000 by default). Check it:

curl localhost:3000/ping

pong

docs.title: Start the server with Docker
docs.text:
docker-compose up -d --build

Production

Do not use dox s or dart run in production. Build a native binary with dox build. See Deployment.

docs.title: Run the code generator
docs.text:
Dox makes code for models and DTOs with build_runner. dox s already runs it. To run it alone:

dox build_runner:watch   # runs again on every file change
dox build_runner:build   # runs once

docs.title: Packages
docs.text:
All Dox packages use the same version.

Package What it does dox the CLI dox_core HTTP server, routing, requests, responses, validation dox_orm query builder and models dox_migration database migrations dox_auth JWT authentication dox_websocket WebSocket server dox_builder, dox_annotation code generation for models and DTOs dox_validation typed validation schemas dox_openapi OpenAPI docs dox_storage file storage: local, S3 dox_cache cache: memory, file, Redis dox_socketio Socket.IO server dox_http_native native HTTP server (Rust) dox_postgres_native, dox_mysql_native native database drivers for Postgres and MySQL/MariaDB

docs.title: Middleware
docs.text: Middleware is code that runs before the controller. Use it for checks like login, logging or rate limits.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
A middleware gets the request. It then does one of these:

  • Return the request. Dox goes on to the next middleware, then to the controller.
  • Return something else (a String, a Map, a response(...)). Dox sends it as the response. The controller does not run.
  • Throw an exception, like NotFoundHttpException(). Dox sends the error response. See Response: errors.

A middleware can be async. Dox waits for it.

docs.title: Class based middleware
docs.text:
Create one with the CLI. It writes lib/app/http/middleware/logger.middleware.dart.

dox create:middleware Logger
lib/app/http/middleware/logger.middleware.dart
import 'package:dox_core/dox_core.dart';

class LoggerMiddleware implements IDoxMiddleware { // (1)!
  @override
  dynamic handle(IDoxRequest req) { // (2)!
    print('${req.method} ${req.uri.path}');
    return req; // (3)!
  }
}
  1. IDoxMiddleware is the interface for a class middleware. Dox calls its handle method.
  2. handle gets the request. It can be async. Dox waits for it.
  3. Return the request to go on to the next middleware, then the controller. Return anything else, like response(...), and Dox sends that as the response.

Then put it on a route:

lib/routes/api.dart
Route.get('/ping', <dynamic>[LoggerMiddleware(), webController.pong]);

Note

handle takes an IDoxRequest, not a DoxRequest. This is the type that IDoxMiddleware asks for.

docs.title: Function based middleware
docs.text:
A function that takes a DoxRequest also works as middleware.

lib/app/http/middleware/api_key.middleware.dart
import 'package:dox_core/dox_core.dart';

dynamic apiKeyMiddleware(DoxRequest req) {
  if (req.header('X-Api-Key') != 'secret') {
    return response(<String, String>{'message': 'Unauthorized'}).statusCode(401);
  }
  return req;
}
lib/routes/api.dart
Route.get('/ping', <dynamic>[apiKeyMiddleware, webController.pong]);

docs.title: Many middleware on one route
docs.text:
Put them in the list before the controller. They run from left to right. You can mix class and function middleware.

Route.get('/ping', <dynamic>[
  LoggerMiddleware(),
  apiKeyMiddleware,
  webController.pong, // the controller is always last
]);

docs.title: Middleware for a group of routes
docs.text:
Route.middleware(<dynamic>[LoggerMiddleware()], () {
  Route.get('/me', controller.me);
  Route.post('/logout', controller.logout);
});

docs.title: Middleware for a router or for all routes
docs.text:
For one router, set its middleware list:

lib/routes/api.dart
class ApiRouter extends Router {
  @override
  String get prefix => 'api';

  @override
  List<dynamic> get middleware => <dynamic>[LoggerMiddleware()];

  @override
  void register() {
    // every route here runs LoggerMiddleware
  }
}

For all routes, set globalMiddleware in the app config:

lib/config/app.dart
AppConfig appConfig = AppConfig(
  globalMiddleware: <dynamic>[LogMiddleware(enabled: true)],
  // ...
);

The order is: global middleware, then router middleware, then group middleware, then route middleware.

flowchart LR
    Q["Request"] --> G["Global<br>globalMiddleware"]
    G --> R["Router<br>middleware getter"]
    R --> P["Group<br>Route.middleware"]
    P --> T["Route<br>list before the controller"]
    T --> C["Controller"]
    C --> S["Response"]
    G & R & P & T -.->|"returns a value or throws"| S

Built-in middleware

  • LogMiddleware from dox_core writes one JSON log line per request.
  • AuthMiddleware from dox_auth checks the JWT token. See Authentication.

docs.title: Request
docs.text: This page shows how to read input, files, headers and cookies from a request.

docs.title: Typed input (recommended)
docs.text:
Ask for a DTO in your controller. Dox reads the body (or the query for GET), checks it, and gives you a typed object.

Route.put('/users/{id}', controller.update);

class UserController {
  Future<User?> update( // (1)!
    int id, // (2)!
    UpdateUser input, // (3)!
  ) async {
    User? user = await User().find(id);
    user?.name = input.name;
    await user?.save();
    return user;
  }
}
  1. The return value is the response. Dox waits for a Future. A String is sent as text. A Map or a model is sent as JSON.
  2. A path param. It is {id} from the route. /users/abc answers 404, because abc is not an int.
  3. A DTO. Dox reads the body, checks it, and builds the object before this method runs.

Bad input gets 422 before your method runs. See Validation.

docs.title: Raw input
docs.text:
Add a DoxRequest parameter to read the raw values. These values are not checked.

class ApiController {
  String sayHello(DoxRequest req) {
    String? name = req.input('name');
    return 'Hello $name';
  }
}
Code Gives req.input('name') one value from the query string or the body. The body wins when both have the key. req.all() all values from the query string and the body, as a Map req.only(<String>['name', 'email']) only these keys req.has('name') true when the key is there and not empty req.body the body only (JSON, form data) req.query the query string only req.add('key', value), req.merge({...}) add values, for example in a middleware

docs.title: Route params
docs.text:
Ask for a path param as a typed parameter. int id gets 42 from /users/42.

Route.get('/hello/{name}', controller.sayHello);
Route.get('/users/{id}', controller.show);

class ApiController {
  String sayHello(String name) {
    return 'Hello $name';
  }

  Future<User?> show(int id) async {
    return User().find(id);
  }
}

The values are also in req.param, like req.param['id']. See Controller: parameters.

docs.title: Form data (File)
docs.text:
An uploaded file is a RequestFile. The request must be multipart/form-data. Put the file in a DTO, so Dox checks its type and size:

@Dto()
class UploadImage {
  @Image()
  @MaxSize('5MB')
  final RequestFile image;

  const UploadImage({required this.image});

  static const DtoSchema<UploadImage> schema = $UploadImageDto;
}

class ApiController {
  Future<Map<String, String>> uploadImage(UploadImage input) async {
    String uploadedPath = await input.image.store('images');
    return <String, String>{'filename': uploadedPath};
  }
}

Without a DTO, req.input('image') gives the RequestFile. It is not checked.

docs.title: RequestFile
docs.text:
RequestFile file = req.input('video');

file.filename;        // name from the client
file.filetype;        // content type, like video/mp4
file.extension;       // mp4
file.length;          // size in bytes
await file.size;      // size in KB
file.stream();        // read it in chunks
await file.store('videos');              // save to storage. returns the path
await file.moveTo('/data/videos/1.mp4'); // move it. returns the new File
await file.bytes;     // the whole file in memory. avoid for big files

Save the file before you return

A file up to 1 MB stays in memory. A bigger file is written to a temp file while it arrives. The temp file is deleted when the response is sent. So call store, moveTo or stream before your controller returns.

docs.title: Size limits
docs.text:
A body that is too big gets 413 Payload Too Large. Dox checks Content-Length first. It also counts the bytes while it reads the body.

lib/config/app.dart
AppConfig(
  maxBodySize: 10 * 1024 * 1024,        // JSON and urlencoded, default 10 MB
  maxMultipartSize: 100 * 1024 * 1024,  // form-data uploads, default 100 MB
);

Set the same limit in your proxy, like client_max_body_size in nginx.

docs.title: Headers
docs.text:
String? token = req.header('X-Token');
Map<String, dynamic> all = req.headers;

req.userAgent();  // User-Agent header
req.host();       // Host header
req.origin();     // Origin header, or null
req.referer();    // Referer header, or null
req.isJson();     // true for a JSON body
req.isFormData(); // true for multipart/form-data
req.locale;       // first language of Accept-Language, like 'th', or null

docs.title: Cookies
docs.text:
String? token = req.cookie('token');                 // decrypted value
String? raw = req.cookie('theme', decrypt: false);   // value as sent

See Response to set a cookie.

docs.title: Client IP and scheme
docs.text:
req.ip();       // client IP
req.scheme();   // http or https
req.isSecure(); // true for https

Behind a proxy, req.ip() shows the proxy, not the client. Set trustedProxies in AppConfig to fix it. See Deployment.

docs.title: Response
docs.text: This page shows what a controller can return, and how to set the status, headers and cookies.

docs.title: Return a value
docs.text:
Return the value from your controller. Dox turns it into the response.

You return The client gets a String the text a Map or a List JSON a model, a list of models, a serializer JSON (from toJson()) a DateTime the ISO 8601 text an IHttpException, like NotFoundHttpException() its status code and its message (text, or JSON for a Map) a File (from dart:io) the file, streamed a Stream<List<int>> the bytes, streamed StreamFile, DownloadableFile from Storage() the file, streamed response(...) full control: status, headers, cookies 
// text
String ping(DoxRequest req) {
  return 'pong';
}

// JSON
Map<String, String> hello(DoxRequest req) {
  return <String, String>{'message': 'hello world!'};
}

// a model
Future<Blog?> show(int id) async {
  return Blog().find(id);
}

// a list of models
Future<List<Blog>> index(DoxRequest req) async {
  return Blog().all();
}

// an error
Future<Blog> showOrFail(int id) async {
  Blog? blog = await Blog().find(id);
  if (blog == null) {
    throw NotFoundHttpException(); // 404 Not Found
  }
  return blog;
}

docs.title: Errors
docs.text:
Throw or return an exception to answer with an error.

Exception Status BadRequestException() 400 NotFoundHttpException() 404 PayloadTooLargeException() 413 UnsupportedMediaTypeException() 415 ValidationException() 422 InternalErrorException() 500

Each one takes message:, errorCode: and code::

throw NotFoundHttpException(message: 'Blog not found');

For another status, extend IHttpException:

import 'dart:io';

import 'package:dox_core/dox_core.dart';

class ForbiddenException extends IHttpException {
  ForbiddenException({String message = 'Forbidden'}) {
    super.code = HttpStatus.forbidden;
    super.errorCode = 'forbidden';
    super.message = message;
  }
}

Any other error gets 500. It is also passed to the errorHandler in AppConfig.

docs.title: Files and big responses
docs.text:
Return a File or a Stream<List<int>>. Dox sends it in chunks. It does not load it all into memory.

  • A File sets Content-Type (from the file name), Content-Length and Accept-Ranges.
  • It answers Range: bytes=... with 206 Partial Content. Video players can seek, and downloads can resume.
  • Storage().stream() and Storage().download() on the local disk also stream the file.
import 'dart:io';

// a file from disk
Route.get('/video', (DoxRequest req) => File('storage/video.mp4'));

// a download from Storage
Future<DownloadableFile> download(DoxRequest req) async {
  // sends Content-Disposition, so the browser saves the file
  return Storage().download('report.pdf');
}

// a stream from Storage
Future<StreamFile> show(DoxRequest req) async {
  return Storage().stream('photo.jpg');
}

See File Storage.

docs.title: The response() helper
docs.text:
Use response(content) when you need to set the status, headers or cookies. All methods return the response, so you can chain them.

import 'dart:io';

import 'package:dox_core/dox_core.dart';

DoxResponse store(DoxRequest req) {
  return response(<String, String>{'status': 'created'})
      .statusCode(201)
      .header('X-Request-Id', 'abc')
      .contentType(ContentType.json);
}
Method Does statusCode(201) sets the status code. Default 200. header('X-Key', 'value') adds one header withHeaders({...}) replaces all headers set before contentType(ContentType.html) sets Content-Type (ContentType is from dart:io) cache(Duration(minutes: 5)) sets Cache-Control: max-age=300 cookie(DoxCookie(...)) sets a cookie content(value) changes the body stream(byteStream) sends a Stream<List<int>> as the body

docs.title: Cookie
docs.text:
// set a cookie
DoxCookie cookie = DoxCookie('theme', 'dark');
return response('ok').cookie(cookie);

// set a cookie with options
DoxCookie token = DoxCookie(
  'token',
  'value',
  maxAge: Duration(days: 7), // sent as Max-Age in seconds. default 1 hour
  httpOnly: true,
  secure: true,
  path: '/',
);
return response('ok').cookie(token);

// delete a cookie
return response('ok').cookie(DoxCookie('token', ''), setExpire: true);

// read a cookie
String? value = req.cookie('token');

Encrypt and decrypt

By default, Dox encrypts the cookie value with APP_KEY, and decrypts it when you read it. To turn this off, use DoxCookie(key, value, encrypt: false) to set it, and req.cookie(key, decrypt: false) to read it.

docs.title: Change every response
docs.text:
To change every response in one place (for example, to add a header), set a responseHandler in AppConfig.

lib/app/http/handler.dart
import 'package:dox_core/dox_core.dart';

class ResponseHandler extends ResponseHandlerInterface {
  @override
  DoxResponse handle(DoxResponse res) {
    return res.header('X-Powered-By', 'Dox');
  }
}
lib/config/app.dart
AppConfig appConfig = AppConfig(
  responseHandler: ResponseHandler(),
  // ...
);

docs.title: Routing
docs.text:
A route connects a URL and an HTTP method to the code that answers it.

This is the path of one request through the router:

flowchart LR
    Q["Request<br>GET /blogs/42"] --> B["Router<br>method, host, path"]
    B -->|no match| N["404"]
    B -->|match| P["Params as text<br>req.param"]
    P --> M["Middleware"]
    M -->|returns a value| S["Response"]
    M -->|returns the request| T["Typed params, DTO<br>int id"]
    T --> C["Controller"]
    C --> S

docs.title: Where routes live
docs.text:
Routes are in the lib/routes folder. Each file has one Router class. The prefix of the router is added in front of all its routes.

lib/routes/api.dart
import 'package:dox_core/dox_core.dart';

class ApiRouter extends Router {
  @override
  String get prefix => 'api';

  @override
  List<dynamic> get middleware => <dynamic>[];

  @override
  void register() {
    Route.get('/ping', (DoxRequest req) => 'pong'); // GET /api/ping
  }
}

Add each router to routers in lib/config/app.dart:

lib/config/app.dart
AppConfig appConfig = AppConfig(
  routers: <Router>[WebRouter(), ApiRouter()],
  // ...
);

The leading / in a path is optional. 'ping' and '/ping' are the same route.

docs.title: Route methods
docs.text:
Route.get('/blogs', controller.index);
Route.post('/blogs', controller.store);
Route.put('/blogs/{id}', controller.update);
Route.patch('/blogs/{id}', controller.update);
Route.delete('/blogs/{id}', controller.destroy);

Info

There are also Route.options, Route.copy, Route.view, Route.link, Route.unlink, Route.purge, Route.lock, Route.unlock and Route.propfind.

docs.title: The handler
docs.text:
The second argument is the code that answers the request. It can be:

// a function
Route.get('/ping', (DoxRequest req) => 'pong');

// a controller method
WebController webController = WebController();
Route.get('/ping', webController.pong);

class WebController {
  String pong(DoxRequest req) {
    return 'pong';
  }
}

// a list: middleware first, the controller last
Route.get('/ping', <dynamic>[LoggerMiddleware(), webController.pong]);

In a list, the last item is the controller. The items before it are middleware.

See Controller for the parameters a handler can ask for.

docs.title: Route params
docs.text:
Put a param in {}. Ask for it as a typed parameter in the controller.

Route.get('/blogs/{id}', controller.show);

class BlogController {
  Future<Blog?> show(int id) async {
    return Blog().find(id);
  }
}

/blogs/abc answers 404, because abc is not an int. See Controller: parameters for all the rules.

docs.title: Optional param
docs.text:
{name?} can be missing. Use a nullable type.

Route.get('/posts/{page?}', (int? page) {
  return 'page ${page ?? 1}'; // GET /posts and GET /posts/2 both match
});

docs.title: Catch-all param
docs.text:
{name*} matches the rest of the path, with slashes.

Route.get('/docs/{page*}', (String page) {
  return page; // GET /docs/a/b/c gives 'a/b/c'
});

docs.title: Group routes
docs.text:
// by prefix
Route.group('/blogs', () { // (1)!
  Route.get('/', controller.index);     // GET /blogs
  Route.get('/{id}', controller.show); // (2)!
});

// by domain: these routes match only when the Host header is dartondox.com
Route.domain('dartondox.com', () { // (3)!
  Route.get('/ping', controller.ping);
});

// by middleware
Route.middleware(<dynamic>[AuthMiddleware()], () { // (4)!
  Route.get('/me', controller.me);
  Route.post('/logout', controller.logout);
});
  1. /blogs goes in front of every path in the callback. Start both parts with /. The text is joined as it is.
  2. Makes GET /blogs/{id}. {id} is a route param. The controller asks for it as int id.
  3. These routes match only when the Host header is dartondox.com. Other hosts get 404.
  4. AuthMiddleware runs before me and logout. It runs after the global and router middleware.

Start group paths with /

Route.group joins the text as it is. Route.group('blogs', ...) with Route.get('all', ...) makes blogsall. Write Route.group('/blogs', ...) and Route.get('/all', ...).

To turn CORS on or off for some routes, see CORS.

docs.title: Resource routes
docs.text:
One line makes the usual CRUD routes for a controller.

Route.resource('blogs', BlogController());
Method Path Controller method GET /blogs index GET /blogs/create create POST /blogs store GET /blogs/{id} show GET /blogs/{id}/edit edit PUT, PATCH /blogs/{id} update DELETE /blogs/{id} destroy

A method that the controller does not have is skipped. No route is made for it. See Resource controller to make one with the CLI.

docs.title: Serve storage files
docs.text:
Route.files(path) serves the files of a storage disk at GET <path>/{key*}. By default only signed URLs work. Other requests get 403. See File Storage.

Route.files('files');
Route.files('public', disk: 'local', signed: false);

docs.title: Request body for the docs
docs.text:
post, put and patch take a body: schema. It shows in the OpenAPI docs. It does not check the request. To check input, use a DTO.

Route.post('/posts', controller.store, body: v.object(<String, Schema<Object?>>{
  'title': v.string().min(3),
}));

docs.title: Validation rules
docs.text:
This page lists every annotation you can put on a @Dto field. See Validation for how DTOs work.

How to read the tables:

  • Code is the error code. Use it in @Dto(messages: ...) and in a MessageResolver.
  • Message is the default English text. {field} is the last key of the path.
  • Every annotation also takes message:. It wins over every other message.
  • All limits include the limit itself, unless the table says "exclusive".
  • On a List<T> field, a value rule checks each item. Only the list rules check the list itself.

docs.title: Type errors
docs.text:
These have no annotation. They come from the field type.

Code When Message required a required field is missing, null, or "" The {field} is required string not a string The {field} must be a string integer not a whole number The {field} must be an integer numeric not a number (double, num) The {field} must be a number boolean not a bool The {field} must be a boolean date not an ISO 8601 date The {field} must be a date in not a name of the enum The selected {field} is invalid. Valid options are {values} array not a list The {field} must be an array object not an object (nested DTO, Map) The {field} must be an object file not a file The {field} must be a file unrecognized_keys unknown key, with @Dto(strict: true) The {field} field is not allowed

docs.title: Text
docs.text:
For String fields (and List<String> items).

Annotation Code Message JSON Schema @Length(min: 3, max: 50) length_between The {field} must be between {min} and {max} characters minLength, maxLength @Length(min: 6, max: 6) length The {field} must be exactly {length} characters minLength, maxLength @MinLength(3) min_length The {field} must be at least {min} characters minLength @MaxLength(50) max_length The {field} may not be greater than {max} characters maxLength @Email() email The {field} is not a valid email format: email @Url() url The {field} must be a url format: uri @Uuid() uuid The {field} is invalid uuid format: uuid @Ip() ip The {field} must be an ip address anyOf ipv4 / ipv6 @Regex(r'[a-z]+') regex The {field} format is invalid pattern @In(['a', 'b']) in The selected {field} is invalid. Valid options are {values} enum @NotIn(['root']) not_in The {field} field cannot be {value} not: {enum} @StartsWith('dox') start_with The {field} must start with {prefix} pattern @EndsWith('.dev') end_with The {field} must end with {suffix} pattern @Alpha() alpha The {field} must be an alphabetic pattern @AlphaNumeric() alpha_numeric The {field} must be only alphabetic and number pattern @AlphaDash() alpha_dash The {field} must be only alphabetic and dash pattern

Details:

  • @Length has min: and max:. Both are optional, but you must give one. With only min: it acts like @MinLength, with only max: like @MaxLength.
  • Length counts characters (Unicode code points). é counts as 1.
  • @Url() needs http or https and a host.
  • @Uuid() takes any version. Upper or lower case.
  • @Regex(pattern, {message}) must match the whole value. You do not need ^ and $. The regex is checked when the generator runs. A bad regex stops the build.
  • @Alpha(), @AlphaNumeric() and @AlphaDash() use ASCII letters a-z, A-Z. @AlphaDash() also allows - and _.
  • @In and @NotIn compare exactly (case matters).

docs.title: Change text
docs.text:
These change the value before the rules run. They always run in this order, wherever you put them: @Trim, then @Lowercase or @Uppercase, then the "empty string is missing" check.

Annotation Does @Trim() removes spaces at the start and the end @Lowercase() makes the text lower case @Uppercase() makes the text upper case @AllowEmpty() keeps "" as a value. Without it, "" counts as missing.

They have no error and no JSON Schema output. @Lowercase() and @Uppercase() together stop the build.

docs.title: Numbers
docs.text:
For int, double and num fields (and list items).

Annotation Code Message JSON Schema @Min(18) min The {field} must be greater than or equal {min} minimum @Max(100) max The {field} must be less than or equal {max} maximum @Range(1, 10) between The {field} must be between {min} and {max} minimum, maximum @Positive() greater_than The {field} must be greater than 0 exclusiveMinimum: 0 @GreaterThan(0.5) greater_than The {field} must be greater than {min} (exclusive) exclusiveMinimum @LessThan(100) less_than The {field} must be less than {max} (exclusive) exclusiveMaximum @In([1, 2, 3]) in The selected {field} is invalid. Valid options are {values} enum @NotIn([0]) not_in The {field} field cannot be {value} not: {enum}

The values are num. @Min(1.5) on an int field stops the build.

docs.title: Lists
docs.text:
For List<T> fields. These check the list, not the items.

Annotation Code Message JSON Schema @MinItems(1) min_items The {field} must have at least {min} items minItems @MaxItems(5) max_items The {field} may not have more than {max} items maxItems @UniqueItems() unique_items The {field} must not have duplicate items uniqueItems: true

@UniqueItems() works for String, numbers, bool, enums and DateTime. On a list of DTOs it stops the build.

docs.title: Dates
docs.text:
For DateTime fields.

Annotation Code Message JSON Schema @After('2000-01-01') after The {field} must be a date after {date} format: date-time @Before('now') before The {field} must be a date before {date} format: date-time
  • The value is an ISO 8601 date, or 'now' (the time of the request).
  • Both are exclusive: @After('2000-01-01') does not accept 2000-01-01T00:00:00Z.
  • To compare two fields (end after start), use validate().

docs.title: Files
docs.text:
For RequestFile and List<RequestFile> fields.

Annotation Code Message JSON Schema @MaxSize('2MB') max_size The {field} may not be larger than {max} maxLength (bytes) @Mimes(['pdf', 'png']) mimes The {field} must be a file of type: {types} contentMediaType @Image() image The {field} must be an image contentMediaType: image/*
  • @MaxSize units: B, KB, MB, GB. 1KB = 1024 bytes. A bad size text stops the build.
  • @Mimes takes file extensions. Dox finds the real type from the first bytes of the file. For types without a byte signature (like txt or csv), it uses the file name extension.
  • @Image() is @Mimes(['jpg', 'jpeg', 'png', 'gif', 'webp', 'bmp']). No svg.
  • The JSON Schema of a file is {"type": "string", "format": "binary"}, plus the keys above.

docs.title: Database
docs.text:
From dox_orm. Async: they run after all other checks passed.

Annotation Code Message @Unique(table, {column, ignoreParam, ignoreColumn, connection}) unique The {field} has already been taken @Exists(table, {column, connection}) exists The selected {field} is invalid
  • @Unique column default: the input key. @Exists column default: id.
  • ignoreParam: 'id' skips the row where ignoreColumn (default id) equals the path param {id}.
  • They add nothing to the JSON Schema.

See Database rules.

docs.title: Keys and DTO options
docs.text:
Annotation Does @Name('emailAddress') the input key for this field. Default: the field name in snake_case. @Dto() marks the class. @Dto(source: Source.query) where to read: Source.auto (default), Source.query, Source.body. @Dto(keyCase: KeyCase.field) keys: KeyCase.snake (default) or KeyCase.field (the Dart name as is). @Dto(strict: true) unknown keys are errors. Default false: they are dropped. @Dto(messages: {...}) messages by code or key.code.

A /// doc comment on a field becomes its description in the JSON Schema.

docs.title: What the generator checks
docs.text:
The build stops with a clear error when:

  • a field is not final, or is not a parameter of the unnamed constructor,
  • a field type is not supported (see Types),
  • a rule does not fit the field type (like @Email() on an int),
  • a Maybe<T> field has no const Maybe.missing() default,
  • two @Dto classes in the app have the same name,
  • the class is generic, or extends another class (other than Object).

docs.title: Validation
docs.text:
This page shows how to check request input with typed DTO classes.

Write a class with @Dto(). Ask for it in your controller. Dox reads the request, checks it, and gives you a typed object. When the input is wrong, Dox answers 422 with the errors. Your controller does not run.

This is how a DTO goes from your code to a checked object:

flowchart LR
    D["@Dto class<br>CreateUser"] --> B["build_runner"]
    B --> G["Generated schema<br>$CreateUserDto"]
    G --> L["dtos list<br>AppConfig(dtos: dtos)"]
    Q["Request<br>body or query"] --> V["Check against the schema"]
    L --> V
    V -->|errors| E["422 with the errors"]
    V -->|ok| T["Typed object<br>CreateUser"]
    T --> C["Controller"]
lib/app/http/dtos/create_user.dto.dart
import 'package:dox_core/dox_core.dart';

part 'create_user.dto.g.dart'; // (1)!

enum Role { admin, user }

@Dto()
class CreateUser {
  @Length(min: 3, max: 50)
  @Trim() // (2)!
  final String name;

  @Email()
  final String email;

  @Min(18)
  final int? age; // (3)!

  final Role role; // (4)!

  @MaxItems(5) // (5)!
  final List<String> tags;

  const CreateUser({
    required this.name,
    required this.email,
    this.age,
    this.role = Role.user,
    this.tags = const <String>[],
  });

  static const DtoSchema<CreateUser> schema = $CreateUserDto; // (6)!
}
  1. build_runner writes this file. It holds the checks and the code that builds the object.
  2. Rules run from top to bottom. @Trim() cuts the spaces, then @Length checks the text. After @Trim(), an empty string counts as missing.
  3. A nullable field is optional. @Min(18) runs only when the client sends a value.
  4. An enum matches the name exactly, so only "admin" or "user". Role.user is used when the key is missing.
  5. @MaxItems(5) checks the list. A rule like @Email() on a list would check each item instead.
  6. $CreateUserDto is the generated schema. The generator also puts it in the list in lib/dtos.g.dart. Give that list to AppConfig(dtos: dtos), so Dox can find the DTO when a controller asks for it.
lib/app/http/controllers/user.controller.dart
class UserController {
  Future<User> store(CreateUser body) async {
    // body is already checked. body.age is an int?, body.role is a Role.
    User user = User()
      ..name = body.name
      ..email = body.email;
    await user.save();
    return user;
  }
}

Then run the generator:

dox build_runner:build   # or: dart run build_runner build

docs.title: Setup
docs.text:
You do this once per app.

  1. Put DTOs in lib/app/http/dtos/. Name the file <name>.dto.dart. dox create:dto CreateUser makes lib/app/http/dtos/create_user.dto.dart for you.
  2. Each DTO file has part '<name>.dto.g.dart'; and the schema line: static const DtoSchema<CreateUser> schema = $CreateUserDto;
  3. Run dart run build_runner build (or dox build_runner:watch). It writes a .dto.g.dart file next to each DTO and one list of all DTOs in lib/dtos.g.dart.
  4. Give that list to the app in lib/config/app.dart:
lib/config/app.dart
import 'package:my_app/dtos.g.dart';

AppConfig appConfig = AppConfig(
  dtos: dtos, // from lib/dtos.g.dart
  // ...
);

Why the list?

Dox does not use dart:mirrors. So it can not find a class by its name at runtime. Without the list, a controller that asks for a DTO stops the server at start, with a clear error. The generated list tells Dox which classes are DTOs. You never edit it by hand.

What the generator makes for each DTO (no reflection, works with dox build AOT):

  • the checks for every field,
  • the code that turns the input map into your class,
  • a JSON Schema, used by the OpenAPI docs.

docs.title: As a controller parameter
docs.text:
Add a parameter with the DTO type. Dox checks the request before your method runs.

Future<User> store(CreateUser body) async { ... }

// with path params and the request
Future<User> update(DoxRequest req, int id, UpdateUser body) async { ... }

See Controller: parameters for the full rules.

docs.title: Inside a method
docs.text:
req.validate<T>() does the same work. It returns the object or throws the 422 error.

Future<User> store(DoxRequest req) async {
  CreateUser data = await req.validate<CreateUser>();
  // ...
}

req.validate<T>() is always async. Always await it.

docs.title: Required and optional
docs.text:
The Dart type decides. You do not write required or nullable.

Field Missing key null Result final String name; (no default) error required error required required final int? age; null null optional final Role role; with this.role = Role.user the default error required optional, has a default final Maybe<String?> bio; with this.bio = const Maybe.missing() isPresent == false isPresent == true, value == null optional, knows "missing" from null

Rules:

  • Required = not nullable and no default in the constructor.
  • Optional = nullable (T?), or has a default.
  • A default is used only when the key is missing. A default value is not checked by the rules.
  • null is never allowed for a non-nullable field, even when it has a default.
  • An empty string counts as missing. After @Trim(), "" is treated like a missing key, in JSON, query and form data. So a required String rejects "" and " " (with @Trim()). A String? gets null. Add @AllowEmpty() to keep "" as a real value.
  • Rules on an optional field run only when it has a value.

docs.title: Missing or null? (for PATCH)
docs.text:
A T? field gives null for both a missing key and a null value. When you must know the difference, use Maybe<T>. Its default must be const Maybe.missing().

@Dto()
class UpdateUser {
  @Length(max: 500)
  final Maybe<String?> bio;

  const UpdateUser({this.bio = const Maybe.missing()});

  static const DtoSchema<UpdateUser> schema = $UpdateUserDto;
}

// in the controller
if (body.bio.isPresent) {
  user.bio = body.bio.value; // can be null: the client cleared it
}

Rules on a Maybe<T> field check value when it is present and not null.

docs.title: Types
docs.text:
Dart type JSON Query and form data (text) String a string as is int a whole number (18 or 18.0) "18" double any number (18 becomes 18.0) "4.5", "18" num any number "18", "4.5" bool true / false true, 1, yes, on / false, 0, no, off (any case) DateTime an ISO 8601 string the same an enum the name, like "admin" the same RequestFile not allowed a file part in multipart/form-data a @Dto class an object bracket keys, like address[city] List<T> an array repeated keys tags=a&tags=b, or tags[]=a&tags[]=b Map<String, T> an object with any keys bracket keys, like meta[color] Object?, dynamic, Map<String, dynamic> any JSON, not checked any text, not checked

JSON is strict. In a JSON body, "18" is not an int. You get the error integer. Query and form data are text, so Dox turns the text into the field type first. If it can not, you get the type error (like integer or boolean).

More details:

  • int never takes a fraction. "4.5" or 4.5 gives the error integer.
  • DateTime takes 2024-01-31 or 2024-01-31T10:00:00Z. A value without a time zone is read as UTC. The result is always UTC (isUtc == true). A number (timestamp) is not allowed.
  • An enum matches the name exactly. "Admin" does not match Role.admin.
  • In query and form data, one value for a List<T> field gives a list with one item.
  • In bracket keys, list indexes are sorted and packed: items[3] alone gives a list with one item. A list can have at most 1000 items, and keys can nest at most 10 levels. More gives 422.
  • The generator stops with an error for any other type.

docs.title: Where the data comes from
docs.text:
Request Dox reads GET, HEAD, DELETE the query string POST, PUT, PATCH the body

Dox reads one source. It never mixes the query and the body. So a query value can not overwrite a body value.

The body can be:

  • JSON: application/json (or any +json type). Strict types.
  • application/x-www-form-urlencoded: text, converted.
  • multipart/form-data: text, converted. Files go to RequestFile fields.

Other content types get 415 Unsupported Media Type. A body that is not valid JSON gets 400 Bad Request. A JSON body that is not an object (like [1, 2]) gets 422 with the key _root.

docs.title: Choose the source
docs.text:
Set it on the DTO, when this DTO is always read from one place:

@Dto(source: Source.query) // also for POST
class SearchUsers { ... }

Or set it for one call:

SearchUsers filter = await req.validate<SearchUsers>(source: Source.query);

Source.auto (the default) uses the table above. Source.query and Source.body force one source.

docs.title: Path params
docs.text:
Path params are not part of a DTO. Ask for them as typed controller parameters:

Route.put('/users/{id}', controller.update);

Future<User> update(int id, UpdateUser body) async { ... }

A path param that does not fit its type (like abc for int id) answers 404. See Controller: parameters.

docs.title: Keys: snake_case by default
docs.text:
The JSON key is the field name in snake_case, the same as the ORM. firstName reads first_name.

@Dto()
class SignUp {
  final String firstName; // key: first_name

  @Name('emailAddress')
  final String email; // key: emailAddress

  const SignUp({required this.firstName, required this.email});

  static const DtoSchema<SignUp> schema = $SignUpDto;
}

To use the field names as they are (camelCase), set it on the DTO:

@Dto(keyCase: KeyCase.field) // firstName reads firstName

Error keys always use the input key (first_name), not the Dart name.

docs.title: Unknown keys
docs.text:
Keys that the DTO does not have are dropped. You never see them.

With @Dto(strict: true), an unknown key is an error:

{ "is_admin": "The is_admin field is not allowed" }

docs.title: Rules
docs.text:
Put rules on a field as annotations. A field can have many. They run from top to bottom. The first rule that fails gives the error for that field.

@Trim()
@Lowercase()
@Email()
@MaxLength(255)
final String email;

Every rule is in the rules reference. The short list:

Kind Annotations Text @Length, @MinLength, @MaxLength, @Email, @Url, @Uuid, @Ip, @Regex, @In, @NotIn, @StartsWith, @EndsWith, @Alpha, @AlphaNumeric, @AlphaDash Change text @Trim, @Lowercase, @Uppercase, @AllowEmpty Numbers @Min, @Max, @Range, @Positive, @GreaterThan, @LessThan, @In, @NotIn Lists @MinItems, @MaxItems, @UniqueItems Dates @After, @Before Files @MaxSize, @Mimes, @Image Database @Unique, @Exists (from dox_orm) Keys @Name

Rules on a list check each item

@Email() on a List<String> checks every item. The error key is emails.2. Only @MinItems, @MaxItems and @UniqueItems check the list itself.

The generator stops with an error when a rule does not fit the type, like @Email() on an int.

Name clash

dox_core exports the rule names (Uuid, Name, Range, Image, ...). A file that also imports a package with the same name, like package:uuid, gets an "ambiguous import" error. Fix it with hide: import 'package:dox_core/dox_core.dart' hide Uuid;. dox_orm has a Schema class too: import 'package:dox_orm/dox_orm.dart' hide Schema;.

docs.title: Enums or @In
docs.text:
Use a Dart enum when you can. The allowed values are the enum names. Use @In([...]) for a plain String or int with a few allowed values:

final Role role;              // "admin" or "user"

@In(<String>['draft', 'published'])
final String status;

docs.title: Nested objects and lists
docs.text:
A field can be another @Dto class, or a list of them.

@Dto()
class Address {
  final String city;

  @Length(min: 5, max: 5)
  final String postCode;

  const Address({required this.city, required this.postCode});

  static const DtoSchema<Address> schema = $AddressDto;
}

@Dto()
class OrderItem {
  final String name;

  @Positive()
  final int quantity;

  const OrderItem({required this.name, required this.quantity});

  static const DtoSchema<OrderItem> schema = $OrderItemDto;
}

@Dto()
class CreateOrder {
  final Address address;

  @MinItems(1)
  final List<OrderItem> items;

  const CreateOrder({required this.address, required this.items});

  static const DtoSchema<CreateOrder> schema = $CreateOrderDto;
}

{
  "address": { "city": "Bangkok", "post_code": "10110" },
  "items": [
    { "name": "Shoes", "quantity": 2 },
    { "name": "Socks", "quantity": 0 }
  ]
}

Error: {"items.1.quantity": "The quantity must be greater than 0"}.

A nested DTO has its own options (keyCase, strict). A nullable nested field (Address?) is optional.

docs.title: Files
docs.text:
A RequestFile field reads a file from multipart/form-data.

@Dto()
class UploadAvatar {
  @Image()
  @MaxSize('2MB')
  final RequestFile avatar;

  @MaxItems(5)
  @Mimes(<String>['pdf', 'docx'])
  final List<RequestFile> documents; // documents[] or repeated documents

  const UploadAvatar({required this.avatar, this.documents = const <RequestFile>[]});

  static const DtoSchema<UploadAvatar> schema = $UploadAvatarDto;
}
  • Dox reads the first bytes of the file to find its real type. The file name and the client content type are not trusted.
  • @Image() allows jpg, jpeg, png, gif, webp and bmp. Not svg, because an SVG can hold scripts.
  • A text field sent where a file is expected gives the error file.
  • Save the file before you return. See Request: form data.

docs.title: Checks across fields: validate()
docs.text:
Add a method validate(DtoErrors errors) to the DTO. Dox calls it after every field rule passed. At that point, all fields have their typed values.

@Dto()
class SignUp {
  @MinLength(8)
  final String password;

  final String passwordConfirmation;

  final DateTime? startsAt;
  final DateTime? endsAt;

  const SignUp({
    required this.password,
    required this.passwordConfirmation,
    this.startsAt,
    this.endsAt,
  });

  void validate(DtoErrors errors) {
    if (password != passwordConfirmation) {
      errors.add('password_confirmation', 'The passwords do not match');
    }
    if (startsAt != null && endsAt != null && !endsAt!.isAfter(startsAt!)) {
      errors.add('ends_at', 'The end must be after the start');
    }
  }

  static const DtoSchema<SignUp> schema = $SignUpDto;
}

The exact API:

  • The method is named validate. It takes one DtoErrors and returns void or Future<void>.
  • errors.add(String key, String message) adds an error. key is the input key (snake_case), not the Dart name. The message is used as it is (no placeholders, no message resolver).
  • errors.has(String key) is true when that key already has an error.
  • Use the key _root for an error that is not about one field.
  • In a nested DTO, keys are relative. Dox adds the parent path: address.post_code.
  • Do not throw for bad input. Add an error.

docs.title: Database rules: @Unique and @Exists
docs.text:
These come from dox_orm. They read the database, so they run last.

import 'package:dox_orm/dox_orm.dart' hide Schema;

@Dto()
class CreateUser {
  @Email()
  @Unique('users', column: 'email')
  final String email;

  @Exists('teams') // column defaults to id
  final int teamId;

  @Exists('tags')
  final List<int> tagIds; // checks every item in one query

  const CreateUser({required this.email, required this.teamId, this.tagIds = const <int>[]});

  static const DtoSchema<CreateUser> schema = $CreateUserDto;
}
Annotation Passes when @Unique(table, {column}) no row has this value. column defaults to the input key. @Exists(table, {column}) a row has this value. column defaults to id.

For an update, skip the row you are updating. ignoreParam names a path param:

// PUT /users/{id}
@Unique('users', column: 'email', ignoreParam: 'id') // WHERE id != {id}
final String email;
  • ignoreColumn: sets the id column. Default id.
  • connection: uses another dox_orm connection. Default: the default connection.
  • Soft-deleted rows count too.
  • Upper or lower case: this depends on your database collation.
  • On a List<T> field, each item is checked. All items use one WHERE IN query.

docs.title: The order of checks
docs.text:
1. Read the input and convert types. Change text (@Trim, @Lowercase, @Uppercase). Missing required fields.
  2. The field rules, top to bottom.
  3. The validate() method (nested DTOs first, then the parent).
  4. Async rules (@Unique, @Exists, your AsyncRule), one at a time, in field order.

Each step runs only when the step before it had no errors. So the database is never asked about input that is already wrong.

  • Steps 1 and 2 run per DTO. A nested DTO checks its own types first, then its own rules. So one answer can have a type error in address and a rule error in items.1.
  • Inside one step, Dox collects the errors of all fields.
  • A default value is not checked by the field rules. (Async rules check the final value.)

docs.title: The error response
docs.text:
When a check fails, Dox answers 422 Unprocessable Entity with a flat JSON object. The key is the path to the value. The value is one message (the first error of that field).

{
  "email": "The email is not a valid email",
  "tags.0": "The tags may not be greater than 20 characters",
  "address.city": "The city is required",
  "items.1.quantity": "The quantity must be greater than 0"
}
  • Paths use dots. List items use the index: tags.0.
  • Paths use the input keys (post_code), after @Name and keyCase.
  • _root is for errors about the whole body.

docs.title: Messages
docs.text:
Every rule has a default English message. See the rules reference.

Placeholders: {field} is the last key of the path (for list items: the list key). {value} is the input value. Rules add their own, like {min} and {max}.

docs.title: On one rule
docs.text:
Every annotation takes message:.

@Email(message: 'Please check your email')
@Length(min: 3, message: 'At least {min} letters, please')

docs.title: On one DTO
docs.text:
@Dto(messages: ...) sets messages by code, or by key.code. Use it for messages that have no annotation, like required or a type error.

@Dto(messages: <String, String>{
  'email.required': 'We need your email',
  'required': 'Please fill in {field}',
  'integer': 'The {field} must be a number',
})

docs.title: For the whole app, and other languages
docs.text:
Dox finds a message in this order:

  1. message: on the annotation.
  2. @Dto(messages:): first key.code (like email.required), then code.
  3. The app message resolver.
  4. The default English text.

For other languages, extend MessageResolver and set it in the config. request.locale is the first language in the Accept-Language header, like th. It is null when there is none.

class AppMessages extends MessageResolver {
  static const Map<String, Map<String, String>> _texts = <String, Map<String, String>>{
    'th': <String, String>{'required': 'กรุณากรอก {field}'},
  };

  @override
  String resolve(MessageRequest request) {
    String? template = _texts[request.locale]?[request.code];
    if (template == null) {
      return super.resolve(request);
    }
    return format(template, request.params);
  }
}

AppConfig appConfig = AppConfig(
  validationMessages: AppMessages(),
  // ...
);

MessageRequest has code, path, params, fallback, customMessage and locale.

docs.title: Custom rules
docs.text:
A rule is a class that extends Rule<T>. It needs a const constructor, so you can use it as an annotation. T is the field type (or the item type, for a list).

class Slug extends Rule<String> {
  const Slug({super.message});

  @override
  String get name {
    return 'slug'; // the error code
  }

  @override
  String get defaultMessage {
    return 'The {field} must be a slug';
  }

  @override
  bool check(String value, RuleContext context) {
    return _pattern.hasMatch(value);
  }

  static final RegExp _pattern = RegExp(r'^[a-z0-9]+(-[a-z0-9]+)*$');
}

@Dto()
class CreatePost {
  @Slug()
  final String slug;

  const CreatePost({required this.slug});

  static const DtoSchema<CreatePost> schema = $CreatePostDto;
}
  • A rule with values: add final fields and override params. They become placeholders.
  • RuleContext gives path, field, root (the whole input) and lookup('other.key').
  • Override toJsonSchema() to add JSON Schema keys, like {'pattern': '^[a-z0-9-]+$'}.
  • A check that needs the database: extend AsyncRule<T> and implement Future<bool> checkAsync(T value, RuleContext context). It runs in step 4 of the order of checks.
class MinValue extends Rule<int> {
  const MinValue(this.min, {super.message});

  final int min;

  @override
  String get name {
    return 'min_value';
  }

  @override
  String get defaultMessage {
    return 'The {field} must be at least {min}';
  }

  @override
  Map<String, Object?> get params {
    return <String, Object?>{'min': min};
  }

  @override
  bool check(int value, RuleContext context) {
    return value >= min;
  }
}

docs.title: Dynamic input: fluent schemas
docs.text:
Some input has a shape you only know at runtime, like custom form fields from the database. For that, build a schema with v.object(...) and use req.validateSchema(). It returns a Map.

Map<String, Schema<Object?>> fields = <String, Schema<Object?>>{};
for (FormField f in form.fields) {
  fields[f.key] = f.required ? v.string().min(1) : v.string().optional();
}

Map<String, dynamic> data = await req.validateSchema(v.object(fields));

Use a DTO for everything else. See dox_validation.

docs.title: Testing
docs.text:
Make a DTO directly. It is a normal Dart class. This skips all checks.

CreateUser input = const CreateUser(name: 'Ann', email: 'ann@dox.dev');
await userService.create(input);

Check a map with the rules, like a request would:

CreateUser user = await CreateUser.schema.validateMap(<String, dynamic>{
  'name': 'Ann',
  'email': 'ann@dox.dev',
});
expect(user.role, Role.user);

Check the errors with safeValidateMap. It never throws.

ParseResult<CreateUser> result = await CreateUser.schema.safeValidateMap(<String, dynamic>{
  'name': 'A',
  'email': 'not-an-email',
});

expect(result.success, isFalse);
expect(result.errors, <String, String>{
  'name': 'The name must be between 3 and 50 characters',
  'email': 'The email is not a valid email',
});

Options of both methods:

  • source: Source.query reads the map like a query string (text is converted). Default: Source.body with JSON types.
  • params: {'id': '5'} gives path params, for @Unique(ignoreParam: 'id').

@Unique and @Exists need a database. Use a test database, or test those fields in an integration test.

docs.title: Not supported
docs.text:
• A DTO can not extend another class, and can not be generic. The generator stops with an error.
  • An enum value is always its Dart name. Custom wire values (like "ADMIN" for Role.admin) are not supported.

docs.title: Performance
docs.text:
• The generator writes plain Dart code for each DTO. No reflection, no rule strings to parse.
  • A check is a few if statements per field. Regexes are compiled once.
  • Dox finds the DTO for a route once, then keeps it.
  • It works with dox build (AOT).

docs.title: Build a blog API
docs.text:
This tutorial takes you from an empty folder to a small blog API that runs as one native binary. Every step has the full code and a curl command to check it.

The finished project is on GitHub: examples/blog-api. CI builds it and runs its tests on every push, so the code on these pages keeps working.

docs.title: What you will build
docs.text:
A JSON API for blog posts.

Method Path Who What it does GET /api/posts anyone list all posts GET /api/posts/{id} anyone one post, or 404 POST /api/posts logged in user make a post (201, or 422 on bad input) PUT /api/posts/{id} logged in user change a post POST /api/auth/register anyone make an account, get a token POST /api/auth/login anyone log in, get a token GET /api/auth/user logged in user the user of the token

You will use these parts of Dox:

  • a model and a Dart migration (dox_orm, dox_migration),
  • a controller and routes,
  • a @Dto class for checked input,
  • JWT login with dox_auth,
  • one HTTP test,
  • dox build for a native binary, and the Dockerfile.

docs.title: What you need
docs.text:
• Dart 3.13 or newer: dart --version.
  • curl, to call the API.
  • About 15 minutes.

You do not need Docker or a database server. The app uses SQLite, which is one file in your project.

docs.title: The steps
docs.text:
1. Create the project
  2. Model and migration
  3. Routes and controller
  4. Validation
  5. Login with dox_auth
  6. Test
  7. Build and deploy

docs.title: The finished project
docs.text:
Files that you make or change in this tutorial are marked with *.

blog/
├── bin/
│   ├── migrate.dart              runs the dox migration:* commands
│   └── server.dart               runs the migrations, starts the server
├── db/migration/
│   ├── ..._create_posts_table.dart   *
│   ├── ..._create_users_table.dart
│   └── migrations.dart           the list of migrations (Dox writes it)
├── lib/
│   ├── app/http/controllers/
│   │   ├── auth.controller.dart  *
│   │   └── post.controller.dart  *
│   ├── app/http/dtos/
│   │   ├── login_user.dto.dart   *
│   │   ├── register_user.dto.dart *
│   │   └── save_post.dto.dart    *
│   ├── app/models/
│   │   ├── post/post.model.dart  *
│   │   └── user/user.model.dart
│   ├── config/
│   │   ├── app.dart              * adds the DTO list
│   │   ├── database.dart
│   │   ├── env.dart              the .env keys, typed
│   │   └── services.dart         * adds AuthService
│   ├── routes/api.dart           *
│   ├── services/
│   │   ├── auth_service.dart     *
│   │   └── orm_service.dart
│   └── dtos.g.dart               * generated
├── test/http_test.dart           *
├── .env                          *
├── Dockerfile
└── pubspec.yaml                  * adds dox_auth

Start with step 1: create the project.

docs.title: Step 1: Create the project
docs.text: This step makes a new Dox project, points it at SQLite, starts the dev server and calls the first route.

docs.title: 1. Install the CLI and make the project
docs.text:
dart pub global activate dox 3.0.0-alpha.4
dox create blog
cd blog
dart pub get

dox create downloads the dox-sample template from GitHub and names the package blog. So every import in this tutorial starts with package:blog/.

Check the versions

Open pubspec.yaml. Every Dox package must be ^3.0.0-alpha.4. If the template has an older version, change it and run dart pub get again.

docs.title: 2. Use SQLite
docs.text:
Copy the example env file:

cp .env.example .env

The template already uses SQLite. These are the lines that matter:

.env
APP_PORT=3000
APP_KEY=KKep5qC6uHlAgrwaQTQewgMRSIqQnoj0

DB_CONNECTION=sqlite
DB_NAME=db/dox.sqlite

Dox makes the file db/dox.sqlite at the first start. The db folder is in the template. The DB_HOST, DB_PORT, DB_USERNAME and DB_PASSWORD lines are for Postgres and MySQL. SQLite does not read them.

The app reads these keys through lib/config/env.dart. It is a typed class, so env.appPort is an int and reads APP_PORT. A missing APP_KEY stops the app at start. See Environment variables.

The folder must exist

Dox makes the database file when it is missing, but not its folder. If you set DB_NAME=storage/blog.sqlite, run mkdir storage first.

docs.title: 3. Start the server
docs.text:
dox s

dox s runs the code generator (build_runner watch) and dart run bin/server.dart. It restarts the server when you save a .dart file. The first start takes a little longer. It prints Running build hooks... while it compiles the SQLite library.

The last line is:

Server started at http://127.0.0.1:3000 with 8 isolate (native)

The number of isolates is the number of CPU cores on your machine.

docs.title: Check it
docs.text:
In a second terminal:

curl -i http://localhost:3000/api/ping

HTTP/1.1 200 OK
content-type: text/plain; charset=utf-8
...

pong

The route is in lib/routes/api.dart. The ApiRouter has the prefix api, so /ping is served at /api/ping.

docs.text: Step 2: Model and migration

docs.title: Step 2: Model and migration
docs.text: This step makes the posts table with a Dart migration and a Post model for it.

docs.title: 1. Make the model and the migration
docs.text:
dox create:model Post -m

This makes two files and updates one:

File What it is lib/app/models/post/post.model.dart the model (new) db/migration/<date>_create_posts_table.dart the migration (new) db/migration/migrations.dart the list of all Dart migrations. Dox writes it. Do not edit it.

The template already has bin/migrate.dart. The dox migration:* commands run it.

The numbers in the migration file name are the date and time when you ran the command.

docs.title: 2. Add the columns to the migration
docs.text:
Open the new file in db/migration. Add title and body:

db/migration/2026_10_22_205345_create_posts_table.dart
// ignore_for_file: file_names
import 'package:dox_migration/dox_migration.dart';

class CreatePostsTable extends Migration {
  @override
  Future<void> up(Schema schema) async {
    await schema.create('posts', (Table table) {
      table.id();
      table.string('title');
      table.text('body');
      table.timestamps();
    });
  }

  @override
  Future<void> down(Schema schema) async {
    await schema.dropIfExists('posts');
  }
}
  • table.id() makes an auto increment primary key on every database.
  • table.timestamps() makes created_at and updated_at. The model fills them.

docs.title: 3. Add the fields to the model
4. Run the migrations on server start
docs.text:
There is nothing to change here. The template's bin/server.dart already runs the list from db/migration/migrations.dart before the server starts:

bin/server.dart
import '../db/migration/migrations.dart';

void main() async {
  Dox().initialize(appConfig);

  await Migrator(
    migrations: migrations,
    connection: await databaseConfig
        .getConnectionConfig()
        .getDatabaseConnection(),
  ).migrate();

  await Dox().startServer();
}

So the server runs new migrations each time it starts. This also works in the native binary of step 7.

docs.title: 5. Run the migration and the generator
docs.text:
dox migration:run

Migrating: 2026_10_22_205345_create_posts_table
Migrated: 2026_10_22_205345_create_posts_table

The model needs its generated file post.model.g.dart. dox s makes it while it runs. If dox s is not running, run the generator once:

dart run build_runner build --delete-conflicting-outputs

docs.title: Check it
docs.text:
dox migration:status

Migration                             Batch  Status
2026_10_22_205345_create_posts_table  1      Ran

docs.text: Step 3: Routes and controller

docs.title: Step 3: Routes and controller
docs.text: This step adds a resource controller and the routes to list, create and show posts.

docs.title: 1. Make the controller
docs.text:
dox create:controller Post -r

-r makes a resource controller with the seven CRUD methods. Replace the file with this. It keeps only index, store and show:

lib/app/http/controllers/post.controller.dart
import 'package:blog/app/models/post/post.model.dart';
import 'package:dox_core/dox_core.dart';

class PostController {
  /// GET /api/posts
  Future<List<Post>> index(DoxRequest req) async {
    return Post().all();
  }

  /// POST /api/posts
  Future<DoxResponse> store(DoxRequest req) async {
    Post post = Post()
      ..title = req.input('title')
      ..body = req.input('body');
    await post.save();
    return response(post).statusCode(201);
  }

  /// GET /api/posts/{id}
  Future<Post> show(int id) async {
    Post? post = await Post().find(id);
    if (post == null) {
      throw NotFoundHttpException();
    }
    return post;
  }
}

PostController postController = PostController();

How it works:

  • A controller returns a model or a list of models. Dox sends it as JSON.
  • response(post).statusCode(201) sets the status code.
  • show(int id) gets the {id} from the URL. /api/posts/abc answers 404, because abc is not an int.
  • req.input('title') reads the body as it is. It is not checked yet. Step 4 fixes that.

docs.title: 2. Add the routes
3. Start the server
docs.text:
dox s

If it is still running from step 1, it restarts by itself.

docs.text:
Make a post:

  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \

HTTP/1.1 201 Created
content-type: application/json; charset=utf-8

[{"id":1,"title":"Hello Dox","body":"My first post.","created_at":"2026-10-22T13:58:14.062215Z","updated_at":"2026-10-22T13:58:14.062215Z"}]

Show one post:

{"id":1,"title":"Hello Dox","body":"My first post.","created_at":"2026-10-22T13:58:14.062215Z","updated_at":"2026-10-22T13:58:14.062215Z"}

docs.text: Step 4: Validation

docs.title: Step 4: Validation
docs.text: This step checks the input of create and update with a @Dto class. Bad input gets a 422 answer, and the controller does not run.

docs.title: 1. Make the DTO
docs.text:
dox create:dto SavePost

One class is enough for create and update, because both need the same fields. Replace the file with this:

lib/app/http/dtos/save_post.dto.dart
import 'package:dox_core/dox_core.dart';

part 'save_post.dto.g.dart';

/// Typed, checked input. Run `dox build_runner:build` after a change.
@Dto()
class SavePost {
  @Trim()
  @Length(min: 3, max: 100)
  final String title;

  @Trim()
  @MinLength(10)
  final String body;

  const SavePost({required this.title, required this.body});

  static const DtoSchema<SavePost> schema = $SavePostDto;
}
  • A field that is not nullable and has no default is required.
  • The rules run from top to bottom. @Trim() removes spaces first. An empty string then counts as missing.
  • See Validation for all rules.

docs.title: 2. Give the DTO list to the app
docs.text:
The generator writes a list of all DTOs to lib/dtos.g.dart. Dox needs this list, because it does not use reflection. Add two lines to lib/config/app.dart:

lib/config/app.dart
import 'package:blog/dtos.g.dart';

AppConfig appConfig = AppConfig(
  /// DTOs (generated list in lib/dtos.g.dart)
  dtos: dtos,

  // ... the rest stays the same
);

docs.title: 3. Use the DTO in the controller
docs.text:
Ask for SavePost as a parameter. Dox checks the body and gives you a typed object. This also adds update, so PUT /api/posts/{id} works:

lib/app/http/controllers/post.controller.dart
import 'package:blog/app/http/dtos/save_post.dto.dart';
import 'package:blog/app/models/post/post.model.dart';
import 'package:dox_core/dox_core.dart';

class PostController {
  /// GET /api/posts
  Future<List<Post>> index(DoxRequest req) async {
    return Post().all();
  }

  /// POST /api/posts
  Future<DoxResponse> store(SavePost body) async {
    Post post = Post()
      ..title = body.title
      ..body = body.body;
    await post.save();
    return response(post).statusCode(201);
  }

  /// GET /api/posts/{id}
  Future<Post> show(int id) async {
    return _find(id);
  }

  /// PUT /api/posts/{id}
  Future<Post> update(int id, SavePost body) async {
    Post post = await _find(id);
    post
      ..title = body.title
      ..body = body.body;
    await post.save();
    return post;
  }

  Future<Post> _find(int id) async {
    Post? post = await Post().find(id);
    if (post == null) {
      throw NotFoundHttpException();
    }
    return post;
  }
}

PostController postController = PostController();

Route.resource in lib/routes/api.dart sees the new update method and adds PUT and PATCH /api/posts/{id}. You change nothing there.

docs.title: 4. Run the generator
docs.text:
dox s runs it for you. Without dox s:

dart run build_runner build --delete-conflicting-outputs

It writes lib/app/http/dtos/save_post.dto.g.dart and lib/dtos.g.dart.

docs.title: Check it
docs.text:
A title that is too short, and a body that is too short:

curl -i -X POST http://localhost:3000/api/posts \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"title":"Hi","body":"Short"}'

HTTP/1.1 422 Unprocessable Entity
content-type: application/json; charset=utf-8
...

{"title":"The title must be between 3 and 100 characters","body":"The body must be at least 10 characters"}

An empty body:

curl -X POST http://localhost:3000/api/posts \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{}'

{"title":"The title is required","body":"The body is required"}

Good input still gives 201:

curl -i -X POST http://localhost:3000/api/posts \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"title":"Second post","body":"Validation works now."}'

HTTP/1.1 201 Created

Update the first post:

curl -X PUT http://localhost:3000/api/posts/1 \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"title":"Hello Dox (edited)","body":"My first post, edited."}'

{"id":1,"title":"Hello Dox (edited)","body":"My first post, edited.","created_at":"2026-10-22T13:58:14.062215Z","updated_at":"2026-10-22T13:59:13.539886Z"}

docs.text: Step 5: Login with dox_auth

docs.title: Step 5: Login with dox_auth
docs.text: This step adds register and login with a JWT token, and only lets a logged in user create or change posts.

docs.title: 1. Add the package
docs.text: dart pub add dox_auth:^3.0.0-alpha.4

docs.title: 2. Make the users table
docs.text:
The template already has a User model in lib/app/models/user/user.model.dart:

lib/app/models/user/user.model.dart
import 'package:dox_orm/dox_orm.dart';

part 'user.model.g.dart';

@DoxModel(table: 'users', softDelete: true)
class User extends UserGenerator {
  @override
  List<String> get hidden => <String>['password'];

  @Column()
  String? name;

  @Column()
  String? email;

  @Column()
  String? password;
}

password is in hidden, so it is never in the JSON. This matters: the token holds the user as JSON, and anyone can read a JWT.

The users table already exists. The template has its migration, and the server ran it at the first start in step 1:

db/migration/2023_07_16_131937700_create_users_table.dart
class CreateUsersTable extends Migration {
  @override
  Future<void> up(Schema schema) async {
    await schema.create('users', (Table table) {
      table.id();
      table.string('name');
      table.string('email').unique();
      table.string('password');
      table.softDeletes();
      table.timestamps();
    });
  }
  // ...
}

table.softDeletes() makes the deleted_at column that softDelete: true needs. email is unique, so a second register with the same email fails.

docs.title: 3. Make the DTOs
docs.text:
dox create:dto RegisterUser
dox create:dto LoginUser
lib/app/http/dtos/register_user.dto.dart
import 'package:dox_core/dox_core.dart';
import 'package:dox_orm/dox_orm.dart' hide Schema;

part 'register_user.dto.g.dart';

@Dto()
class RegisterUser {
  @Trim()
  @Length(min: 2, max: 50)
  final String name;

  @Trim()
  @Lowercase()
  @Email()
  @Unique('users', column: 'email')
  final String email;

  @MinLength(8)
  final String password;

  const RegisterUser({
    required this.name,
    required this.email,
    required this.password,
  });

  static const DtoSchema<RegisterUser> schema = $RegisterUserDto;
}

@Unique comes from dox_orm. It reads the database, so it runs after the other rules. dox_orm also has a class named Schema, so the import hides it.

lib/app/http/dtos/login_user.dto.dart
import 'package:dox_core/dox_core.dart';

part 'login_user.dto.g.dart';

@Dto()
class LoginUser {
  @Trim()
  @Lowercase()
  @Email()
  final String email;

  final String password;

  const LoginUser({required this.email, required this.password});

  static const DtoSchema<LoginUser> schema = $LoginUserDto;
}

docs.title: 4. Set up the auth service
docs.text:
A service runs once in every isolate at start. This one tells dox_auth which model to use and how to sign tokens:

lib/services/auth_service.dart
import 'package:blog/app/models/user/user.model.dart';
import 'package:blog/config/env.dart';
import 'package:dox_auth/dox_auth.dart';
import 'package:dox_core/dox_core.dart';

/// Auth service
/// --------------------------
/// Sets up JWT login with the User model.
/// Tokens are signed with APP_KEY and last 7 days.
class AuthService implements DoxService {
  @override
  void setup() {
    Auth.initialize(
      AuthConfig(
        defaultGuard: 'api',
        guards: <String, AuthGuard>{
          'api': AuthGuard(
            driver: JwtAuthDriver(
              secret: SecretKey(env.appKey),
              expiresIn: const Duration(days: 7),
            ),
            provider: AuthProvider(model: () => User()),
          ),
        },
      ),
    );
  }
}

Add it to the service list:

lib/config/services.dart
import 'package:blog/services/auth_service.dart';
import 'package:blog/services/orm_service.dart';
import 'package:dox_core/dox_core.dart';

/// Services to register on dox
/// -------------------------------
/// Since dox run on multi thread isolate, we need to register
/// below extra services to dox so that dox can
/// register again on new isolate.
List<DoxService> services = <DoxService>[ORMService(), AuthService()];

docs.title: 5. Write the auth controller
6. Protect the write routes
docs.text:
Replace Route.resource with single routes. The routes inside Route.middleware need a valid token:

lib/routes/api.dart
import 'package:blog/app/http/controllers/api.controller.dart';
import 'package:blog/app/http/controllers/auth.controller.dart';
import 'package:blog/app/http/controllers/post.controller.dart';
import 'package:dox_auth/dox_auth.dart';
import 'package:dox_core/dox_core.dart';

class ApiRouter extends Router {
  @override
  String get prefix => 'api';

  @override
  List<dynamic> get middleware => <dynamic>[];

  @override
  void register() {
    Route.get('/ping', apiController.pong);

    // Anyone can read posts.
    Route.get('/posts', postController.index);
    Route.get('/posts/{id}', postController.show);

    // Register and log in.
    Route.post('/auth/register', authController.register);
    Route.post('/auth/login', authController.login);

    // Only a logged in user can write posts.
    Route.middleware(<dynamic>[AuthMiddleware()], () {
      Route.get('/auth/user', authController.user);
      Route.post('/posts', postController.store);
      Route.put('/posts/{id}', postController.update);
    });
  }
}

AuthMiddleware reads the Authorization: Bearer <token> header and loads the user. When the token is missing or wrong, it answers 401 Authentication failed.

docs.title: 7. Migrate and generate
docs.text:
dox migration:run
dart run build_runner build --delete-conflicting-outputs

dox s runs the migration and the generator for you when it restarts.

docs.title: Check it
docs.text:
Register:

curl -i -X POST http://localhost:3000/api/auth/register \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"name":"Ann","email":"ann@example.com","password":"secret123"}'

HTTP/1.1 201 Created
content-type: application/json; charset=utf-8
...

{"token":"eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIs...","user":{"id":1,"name":"Ann","email":"ann@example.com","created_at":"2026-10-22T14:01:07.827769Z","updated_at":"2026-10-22T14:01:07.827769Z"}}

The same email again gives 422:

{"email":"The email has already been taken"}

A wrong password gives 401:

curl -i -X POST http://localhost:3000/api/auth/login \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"email":"ann@example.com","password":"wrong"}'

HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized
...

Wrong email or password

Log in and keep the token in a shell variable:

TOKEN=$(curl -s -X POST http://localhost:3000/api/auth/login \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"email":"ann@example.com","password":"secret123"}' \
  | sed -E 's/.*"token":"([^"]+)".*/\1/')
echo $TOKEN

A post without a token is refused:

curl -i -X POST http://localhost:3000/api/posts \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"title":"Third post","body":"Written with a token."}'

HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized
...

Authentication failed

With the token it works:

curl -i -X POST http://localhost:3000/api/posts \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"title":"Third post","body":"Written with a token."}'

HTTP/1.1 201 Created
...

{"id":3,"title":"Third post","body":"Written with a token.","created_at":"2026-10-22T14:01:08.094211Z","updated_at":"2026-10-22T14:01:08.094211Z"}

Who am I:

curl http://localhost:3000/api/auth/user -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN"

{"id":1,"name":"Ann","email":"ann@example.com","created_at":"2026-10-22T14:01:07.827769Z","updated_at":"2026-10-22T14:01:07.827769Z"}

No password in the answer, because it is in hidden.

docs.text: Step 6: Test

docs.title: Step 6: Test
docs.text: This step writes one HTTP test for the list route and runs it.

docs.title: 1. Write the test
docs.text:
The template has test/http_test.dart. Replace it with this:

test/http_test.dart
import 'dart:convert';

import 'package:blog/config/app.dart';
import 'package:blog/config/database.dart';
import 'package:dox_core/dox_core.dart';
import 'package:dox_migration/dox_migration.dart';
import 'package:http/http.dart' as http;
import 'package:test/test.dart';

import '../db/migration/migrations.dart';

String baseUrl = 'http://localhost:${appConfig.serverPort}';

void main() {
  setUpAll(() async {
    Dox().initialize(appConfig);
    Dox().totalIsolate(1);
    await Migrator(
      migrations: migrations,
      connection: await databaseConfig
          .getConnectionConfig()
          .getDatabaseConnection(),
    ).migrate();
    await Dox().startServer();
  });

  tearDownAll(() async {
    await Dox().server.close();
  });

  test('GET /api/posts gives a list', () async {
    http.Response response = await http.get(Uri.parse('$baseUrl/api/posts'));
    expect(response.statusCode, 200);
    expect(jsonDecode(response.body), isA<List<dynamic>>());
  });
}
  • The test starts the real server once, on one isolate. One isolate starts faster.
  • It runs the migrations first, so the test also works on an empty database.
  • package:test and package:http are already in dev_dependencies of the template.

docs.title: 2. Stop the dev server
docs.text: The test listens on the same port as dox s. Stop dox s with Ctrl+C first.

docs.title: Check it
docs.text:
dart test test/http_test.dart

00:01 +1: All tests passed!

Use another database for tests

The test uses the .env file, so it reads and writes db/dox.sqlite. To keep test data out of it, set another file for the test run: DB_NAME=test.sqlite dart test test/http_test.dart.
